title: Feature: add bounded cross-session search for plugin-local LCM history
body:
## Summary

`hermes-lcm` is a current-session tool today. The plugin-local LCM SQLite database (`lcm.db`) accumulates messages across many sessions, including rows that may have been externally backfilled from other sources, but the `lcm_grep` tool surface cannot reach beyond the active session. This issue proposes adding bounded archive search to `lcm_grep` over rows already present in `lcm.db`, with `current` remaining the safe default.

> Note: this issue was originally framed as "imported OpenClaw / lossless-claw history". Per maintainer guidance on PR #102, the reframing is "bounded search over rows already present in `lcm.db`, including externally backfilled rows that may carry source strings such as `openclaw-lcm:*`". The feature stands on rows-already-present, not on an implied or supported import path.

## Current limitation

In `tools.py`, `lcm_grep` reads `requested_session_scope` from args, then hard-codes the search to the current session and logs a warning for any other value:

```python
session_scope = "current"
...
if requested_session_scope != "current":
    logger.warning("Ignoring unsupported session_scope=%s for lcm_grep", requested_session_scope)
```

The schema's `session_scope` enum is locked to `["current"]`. Underneath, both `MessageStore.search` and `SummaryDAG.search` are now bound on `session_id=None` as the explicit all-sessions sentinel (#103, #104), so the data layer is ready. The gap is at the tool layer.

## Why `session_search` is not sufficient

The README correctly directs cross-session queries to Hermes' built-in `session_search`. That tool covers Hermes-tracked session history, but it does not reach plugin-local LCM rows that are only present in `lcm.db`.

Operators may have rows in `~/.hermes/lcm.db` that carry source strings such as:

- `openclaw-lcm:agent:sammy:telegram:direct:503782402:conversation:88`
- `openclaw-lcm:agent:nehemiah:telegram:group:-1003814898545:topic:5:conversation:5`
- `openclaw-lcm:agent:david:telegram:group:-1003814898545:topic:9:conversation:6`

These rows exist in the local LCM database but are not reachable via `lcm_grep` today. The issue is a search-tool gap, not a claim about how those rows got there.

## Proposed scope

Extend `lcm_grep` with:

- `session_scope` values:
  - `current` (default): unchanged behavior
  - `all`: search every session in the local LCM database
  - `session`: search a single session id supplied via `session_id`
- Required filter when `session_scope='session'`:
  - `session_id` — explicit, must be supplied
- A clamped `limit` (hard upper bound)
- Result metadata: `store_id`, `session_id`, `source`, `role`, `timestamp`, compact `snippet`, plus `from_current_session` so callers can prefer in-session expansion paths

Companion expansion path:

- Extend `lcm_expand` with a `store_id` mode for bounded, pageable raw-message expansion regardless of session, so callers can drill into cross-session `lcm_grep` results
- Cross-session DAG / summary-node expansion is intentionally deferred. Broader scopes return raw-message hits only.

## Safety and boundedness

- `current` remains the default; existing callers unaffected
- `session_scope='all'` and `session_scope='session'` must be explicit
- `limit` is clamped (proposed: 200)
- Search stays FTS-backed and bounded; never returns unbounded raw content
- Compact snippets first, not full content
- `_get_session_node` and `_get_externalized_payload` keep their session checks
- `lcm_describe` and `lcm_expand_query` remain current-session in this PR; cross-session variants tracked as follow-up issues
- The distinction between Hermes built-in `session_search` and plugin-local LCM bounded archive search is documented explicitly

## Out of scope (for the PR addressing this issue)

- Cross-session DAG / summary-node expansion (follow-up)
- Cross-session `lcm_describe` and `lcm_expand_query` (follow-up)
- Hermes-side `session_search` integration changes
- Privacy or redaction of cross-session content (existing local-DB threat model unchanged)
- FTS5 schema or migration changes
- `role`, `time_from`, `time_to` filters in `lcm_grep`: tracked separately so they can be pushed into the search layer rather than added as post-fetch filters

## Notes

This is a feature request grounded in an operator use case (rows already in `lcm.db` are unreachable via the agent tool surface), not a bug report and not a claim that an official importer exists. Backwards compatible by design (additive schema, default unchanged). PR follows the project's standard validation, branch naming, and PR-body conventions.

title: feat: add bounded cross-session search to lcm_grep
body:
## Summary
- `lcm_grep` gains explicit opt-in `session_scope='all'` and `session_scope='session'` (with `session_id`) for bounded archive recovery over rows already present in `lcm.db`. Default `session_scope='current'` is preserved byte-for-byte.
- Cross-session scopes return raw-message hits only. Cross-session DAG/summary expansion is intentionally deferred.
- `lcm_expand` gains a `store_id` mode that fetches a single raw message regardless of session, paged via `content_offset`. `node_id` and `externalized_ref` modes remain current-session.
- `limit` is clamped to 200 with `limit_clamped_from` echoed when the input exceeds the cap.
- Each result carries `from_current_session` so callers can prefer in-session expansion paths when both are available.

## Why
- Closes the gap that `lcm_grep` is unreachable for rows already present in the plugin-local LCM database, including externally backfilled rows that may carry source strings such as `openclaw-lcm:*`.
- The narrowing positions this as **bounded archive recovery**, not a memory-system expansion. Tool descriptions continue to direct normal cross-session recall to `session_search`.
- No claim of an official OpenClaw/lossless-claw importer; the feature stands on rows-already-present.
- Refs #101.

## Validation
- `pytest tests/test_lcm_core.py tests/test_lcm_engine.py tests/test_packaging_install.py -q` -> **402 passed**
- `pytest -q` -> **439 passed**
- `python3 -m compileall -q .` -> clean
- `bash -n scripts/install.sh scripts/update.sh` -> clean
- `git diff --check origin/main` -> clean

## Notes
- **Rebased** onto current `main` (past #104 and #106). Branch history was rewritten and force-pushed accordingly. GitHub Actions check runs on a fork PR from a non-collaborator require maintainer approval to run; the empty checks on the head are a permissions thing, not a CI failure.
- **Defers to follow-up issue #108**: pushing `role`/`time_from`/`time_to` filters into the search layer. The maintainer's Bug 2 reproduction is captured as the regression contract on that issue.
- **Cross-session DAG/summary expansion** stays deferred. Sessions remain bound on source-id provenance; returning non-expandable summary hits would push this tool toward a broader memory-system shape than the maintainer's scope direction allows.
- **`lcm_expand` store_id mode** is the only cross-session drilldown path in this PR.

title: Bug: empty session_id silently disables session filter in MessageStore.search and SummaryDAG.search (cross-session leak under default scope)
body:
## Summary

\`MessageStore.search\` (\`store.py:568\`) and \`SummaryDAG.search\` (\`dag.py:359\`) gate the session WHERE clause on Python truthiness:

\`\`\`python
if session_id:
    where.append(\"m.session_id = ?\")
    args.append(session_id)
\`\`\`

An empty string \`\"\"\` is falsy, so the predicate is omitted entirely and the FTS query runs across every session in the database.

\`LCMEngine\` initializes \`_session_id = \"\"\` (\`engine.py:242\`). When an agent calls \`lcm_grep\` (default \`session_scope='current'\`) before a real session is bound, the response advertises \`session_scope: 'current'\` while actually returning rows from every session in the local LCM database.

PR #102 added a defensive guard in \`lcm_grep\` itself (refuse the call when scope=current and \`engine._session_id\` is empty) but did not change the data-layer behavior. The leak is still reachable through any future caller that bypasses the tool surface.

## Reproduction

1. Initialize a fresh \`LCMEngine\` without setting \`_session_id\`.
2. Append messages under multiple session ids via \`engine._store.append(\"a\", ...)\`, \`engine._store.append(\"b\", ...)\`.
3. Call \`engine._store.search(\"keyword\", session_id=engine._session_id)\` (i.e., \`session_id=\"\"\`).
4. Result: hits from both \"a\" and \"b\".

## Expected

When \`session_id\` is an empty string (i.e., the engine has no current session bound), the search should either:
- Return zero results (treating empty as a real, never-matching session id), or
- Raise an explicit error so the caller cannot accidentally rely on falsy-truthy coercion.

## Suggested fix

Replace the truthiness check with an \`is None\` check in both \`store.py\` and \`dag.py\`, and document that an empty string is treated as a literal (non-matching) session id rather than an \"all sessions\" sentinel. \`session_scope='all'\` already passes \`session_id=None\` explicitly, so the contract stays consistent.

\`\`\`python
if session_id is not None:
    where.append(\"m.session_id = ?\")
    args.append(session_id)
\`\`\`

## Severity

Pre-existing on \`main\`. Made more visible by PR #102's \`from_current_session\` field (which consistently reports False under this state) but not introduced by it. Worth fixing because:
- It silently violates the documented current-session contract
- Any tool surface that bypasses lcm_grep's defensive guard reaches it
- It is a one-line fix with regression coverage straightforward to add

## Notes

Found during multi-agent code review of PR #102 (cross-session search). Filed separately so the data-layer fix can land independently of the tool-surface work.

title: Feature: add opt-in lossless-claw/OpenClaw LCM importer
body:
## Summary

Add an explicit, opt-in importer for raw message history from lossless-claw/OpenClaw LCM SQLite databases into hermes-lcm's plugin-local `lcm.db`.

## Motivation

#101/#102 discuss cross-session search over plugin-local LCM rows, including rows that may have been externally backfilled from OpenClaw/lossless-claw databases. That provenance should not stay implicit. If hermes-lcm supports this migration story, it should provide a documented importer rather than relying on mystery/manual backfills.

## Proposed scope

- Add an operator script, not an LLM tool, for example `scripts/import_lossless_claw.py`.
- Default to dry-run.
- Require explicit source and target SQLite paths.
- Backup the target DB before any write.
- Import raw messages only; summary DAG import is out of scope.
- Preserve provenance in `source`, for example `openclaw-lcm:<agent>:<source-session>`.
- Preserve role, content, timestamp, and available tool call/result metadata where possible.
- Be idempotent by recording imported source row identity and skipping rows already imported.
- Provide clear validation counts: scanned, eligible, imported, skipped, conversations/sessions.

## Safety boundaries

- No automatic discovery of old OpenClaw data.
- No writes unless explicitly requested with an apply flag.
- No secrets import.
- No claim that LCM is general memory; this is a one-time local archive migration path.

## Validation expectations

- Unit tests with synthetic lossless-claw SQLite fixtures.
- Dry-run does not mutate target DB.
- Apply creates a backup and imports expected rows.
- Re-running apply is idempotent.
- Unsupported/legacy source schemas fail with actionable errors or skip unsupported metadata safely.

## Relationship to #101/#102

This issue should make the imported-data provenance explicit. Cross-session search can then be evaluated against rows created by a supported importer, instead of depending on undocumented external/manual backfills.

title: Feature: push lcm_grep filter set into the search layer
body:
## Summary

Add `role`, `time_from`, `time_to` (and tighten existing `source`) filters to `lcm_grep` so they push into the FTS / data-layer query rather than running as Python post-filters over a bounded candidate fetch. The previous attempt to add these filters in PR #102 was reverted because the post-fetch shape silently lost valid results when matches sat outside the first candidate window. This issue tracks the proper implementation.

## Why

PR #102 added `role`, `time_from`, `time_to` as Python post-filters applied to the result list returned by `MessageStore.search` / `SummaryDAG.search`. Maintainer review (#102) reproduced the failure:

> `lcm_grep` fetches only `source_limit = max(limit * 4, limit, 20)` from the store/DAG, then applies role/time filters in Python. That means valid filtered matches outside the first candidate window disappear.

Concretely, with one older matching `assistant` row and 25 newer matching `user` rows filling the candidate window, `role: assistant` returned `total_results == 0` instead of the older assistant row. The same shape reproduces with `time_to` and any other post-filter that excludes most of the early candidates.

The filters were removed from PR #102 entirely rather than fixed inline, since pushing them into the data layer is a meaningfully larger change.

## Scope

- Push `role`, `time_from`, `time_to` into the FTS / WHERE-clause layer of `MessageStore.search` (and the equivalent paths in `SummaryDAG.search` if/when summary cross-session expansion lands).
- Either: (a) accept the filters as SQL predicates so the FTS engine returns post-filter candidates directly, or (b) keep the post-filter shape but extend the adaptive-widening loop to keep paging until enough post-filter matches collect, bounded by a hard candidate cap.
- Surface the filters back on `lcm_grep` (and update the schema) once the data-layer contract is solid.
- Naive ISO 8601 inputs (no `Z`, no offset) must be rejected so cross-machine reproducibility holds.

## Test contract

The maintainer's exact reproduction is the regression bar:

```python
# one older matching assistant row
assistant_id = engine._store.append(\"test-session\", {\"role\": \"assistant\", \"content\": \"docker target assistant\"})
engine._store._conn.execute(\"UPDATE messages SET timestamp=? WHERE store_id=?\", (1000.0, assistant_id))

# 25 newer matching user rows fill the pre-filter candidate window
for i in range(25):
    sid = engine._store.append(\"test-session\", {\"role\": \"user\", \"content\": f\"docker noisy user {i}\"})
    engine._store._conn.execute(\"UPDATE messages SET timestamp=? WHERE store_id=?\", (2000.0 + i, sid))
engine._store._conn.commit()

result = json.loads(engine.handle_tool_call(\"lcm_grep\", {\"query\": \"docker\", \"role\": \"assistant\", \"limit\": 1, \"sort\": \"recency\"}))
```

Required: \`result[\"total_results\"] >= 1\` and the assistant row appears in \`result[\"results\"]\`. The same shape with \`time_to\` set to a value that excludes the 25 newer rows must return the older assistant row.

## Related

- PR #102 — the cross-session search PR that originally introduced and then removed these filters
- Maintainer review on #102 (CHANGES_REQUESTED, commit \`19d05f8\`) — the source of Bug 2 and the test contract above

title: Bug: gateway restart mid-session resets _ingest_cursor to 0, silently dropping all subsequent tool result rows
body:
## Summary

Gateway restart mid-session resets `_ingest_cursor` to 0 while the store already has thousands of persisted messages for that session. After restart, `_ingest_messages()` silently ingests nothing — all subsequent tool call results (`role='tool'` rows) are never written to `lcm.db`. User/assistant text rows continue to be stored correctly, but tool results are permanently lost.

## Relationship to #1

This is the same root cause as issue #1 (fixed in 4bc6b9c via `_ingest_cursor`), but triggered by a **gateway restart mid-session** rather than a post-compaction cursor reset.

Fix 4bc6b9c handles the compaction case by resetting `_ingest_cursor = len(compressed)` in `compress()`. It does **not** handle the gateway restart case, where `on_session_start()` is called with the **same session ID** on reconnect.

## Related Issues

- **#1** (closed): Post-compaction ingestion cursor bug — same root cause, different trigger path
- **#95** (closed): SQLite lock in `on_session_end()` blocking gateway heartbeat — same lifecycle path, different failure mode

## Reproduction

1. Start a long-running session (any platform)
2. Accumulate many messages (e.g., 10,000+ store rows)
3. Restart the Hermes gateway mid-session (`hermes restart` or systemd restart)
4. Continue the session — send messages, make tool calls
5. Query `lcm.db` directly:

```sql
SELECT role, COUNT(*), source
FROM messages
WHERE session_id = '<your_session_id>'
  AND store_id > <store_id_at_restart>
GROUP BY role, source;
```

**Observed:** `role='tool'` count = 0 for all messages after restart. `role='assistant'` and `role='user'` rows are present.

**Expected:** All roles persisted continuously, including tool results.

## Evidence (production observation)

Confirmed via direct SQL query on `lcm.db` from a 2,288-message CLI session:

- Session `20260504_093451_e6889bdf`, 2,288 total messages
- Gateway restart occurred at store 11626 (Telegram gateway config change + `hermes restart`)
- **Stores 11627–13529 (~1,900 messages): zero `role='tool'` rows stored**
- Stores before 11626 and after 13529: tool results stored normally
- `role='assistant'` and `role='user'` messages stored throughout — confirming ingestion didn't fully stop, only tool results dropped

```sql
-- Confirms gap
SELECT MIN(store_id), MAX(store_id), COUNT(*)
FROM messages
WHERE session_id = '20260504_093451_e6889bdf'
  AND role = 'tool'
  AND source = 'cli';
-- Result: 11605 | 13636 | 62  (gap of ~1,900 stores in the middle)
```

## Root Cause

In `engine.py` `on_session_start()`, lines 1264–1266:

```python
else:
    self._clear_pending_reset_boundary()
    self._ingest_cursor = 0          # ← resets on same-session-id restart
    self._last_compacted_store_id = 0
```

This `else` branch fires when `previous_session_id == session_id` — i.e., when the gateway restarts and re-binds the same session. `_ingest_cursor` resets to 0, but the store already has e.g. 11,626 persisted rows.

When `on_session_end()` subsequently calls `_ingest_messages(messages)`, the in-memory `messages` list is the short post-restart context (e.g., 50 messages). The cursor at 0 means `new_messages = messages[0:]\ = all 50`. But the store count check in `_ingest_messages()` sees existing rows and the deduplication logic skips rows it believes are already stored — or the `messages` list never grows large enough to include the tool results appended during the post-restart run.

The net effect: tool result rows appended to the conversation **after** the gateway restart are never persisted.

## Suggested Fix

`on_session_start()` should detect a same-session-id restart and set `_ingest_cursor` to the existing store count for that session rather than resetting to 0:

```python
else:
    self._clear_pending_reset_boundary()
    # On same-session restart, pick up from existing store count
    # to avoid re-ingesting or silently dropping post-restart messages
    existing_count = self._store.get_session_count(self._session_id) if self._session_id else 0
    self._ingest_cursor = existing_count
    self._last_compacted_store_id = 0
    self._last_overflow_recovery_failed = False
    self._last_condensation_suppressed_reason = ""
```

This mirrors the pattern from the #1 fix — use a durable cursor independent of in-memory list length.

## Impact

- Tool call results are **silently and permanently lost** after any gateway restart mid-session
- Post-mortem debugging is impossible: the DB shows the correct session ID and all user/assistant text but no tool results — making it look like the agent made no tool calls
- Forensic investigation of operational issues (e.g., which terminal command deleted a file) becomes impossible for the affected window

title: Bug: lcm_expand returns empty sources for carried-over summary nodes
body:
## Summary

After `/new` or session rollover carries retained summary nodes into the new session, `lcm_grep` can surface those carried-over summaries as current-session hits, but `lcm_expand(node_id=...)` returns an empty `expanded` list for the same node.

## Reproduction

1. Create an old-session raw row with source `discord`.
2. Create a retained summary node in `old-session` with `source_ids` pointing to that raw row and `source_type="messages"`.
3. Run `carry_over_new_session_context("old-session", "new-session")` with `LCM_NEW_SESSION_RETAIN_DEPTH=2`.
4. Set the engine session to `new-session`.
5. Run `lcm_grep` for the carried-over summary. It returns the summary under `new-session`.
6. Run `lcm_expand` on that returned `node_id`.

## Expected behavior

`lcm_expand(node_id=...)` should recover the raw message sources behind the carried-over summary, or it should return an explicit contract error explaining why carried-over summary sources are not expandable.

## Actual behavior

`lcm_expand(node_id=...)` returns `expanded: []` even though the node has `source_ids` and `pagination.total_sources == 1`.

Observed repro result on latest `main` (`6b0269b`) and PR #102 head (`c837e9b`):

```json
{
  "grep_types": ["summary"],
  "grep_sessions": ["new-session"],
  "expand_count": 0,
  "expand": {
    "source_type": "messages",
    "expanded": [],
    "pagination": {
      "total_sources": 1,
      "returned_sources": 0,
      "has_more": false
    }
  }
}
```

## Likely cause

`_expand_message_sources()` drops rows whose stored `session_id` does not match `engine._session_id`. Carry-over reassigns the summary node to the new session while preserving descendant raw-message source lineage in the original session, so the expansion helper filters out the exact rows it needs.

## Notes

This appears pre-existing on `main`, not introduced by PR #102. PR #102 only made the issue easier to notice while re-reviewing retrieval contracts.

title: fix: reconcile ingest cursor after session restart
body:
## Summary
- Reconcile the process-local ingest cursor when an existing session is rebound after a gateway restart.
- Match replayed active-context rows against a contiguous durable-store suffix before advancing the cursor.
- Skip explicit LCM scaffold messages, but preserve legitimate new system rows.
- Add restart regressions for normal, compacted, large, repeated non-tail, and new-system cases.

## Why
- Fixes #109.
- `_ingest_cursor` is process-local, but gateway restarts can rebind the same session with an existing durable message store.
- Reconstructing the cursor from the durable store prevents duplicate replay of old tail rows while preserving post-restart tool result rows.
- Suffix-only matching avoids silently dropping a new turn whose content repeats older non-tail history.

## Validation

- `ulimit -n 8192 && python -m pytest tests/test_lcm_core.py tests/test_lcm_engine.py tests/test_packaging_install.py -q` -> 384 passed, 38 warnings
- `ulimit -n 8192 && python -m pytest -q` -> 421 passed, 38 warnings

## Notes

title: Feature: session_load tool for full ordered raw-message transcript by session_id
body:
## Summary

Add a `session_load` (or equivalently shaped) tool to `hermes-lcm` that returns the **full ordered raw-message transcript for a given `session_id`** in a single, bounded, paged tool call.

PR #102 (merged 2026-05-06) shipped the building blocks for this — `lcm_grep` now accepts `session_scope='session'` with explicit `session_id`, and `lcm_expand` gained a `store_id` mode for bounded raw-message retrieval regardless of session. Those primitives make targeted cross-session lookup possible. They do not, however, give the agent a clean path to **load an entire prior session's transcript** without an N-round-trip walk: one `lcm_grep` to enumerate the rows, then one `lcm_expand` per row to materialise raw content. For multi-hundred-message sessions that pattern is impractical at the tool-call level.

This issue proposes a single-call counterpart for the "give me the verbatim transcript of session X" operator use case, layered on the same data-layer primitives PR #102 already validated.

## Why

We run `hermes-lcm` v0.7.0 (now bumping to a `main` SHA past v0.8.0 to pick up PR #102 / #111) inside a Hermes deployment that uses Litestream to replicate `lcm.db` to S3. After an ECS task replacement, the next task restores the same `lcm.db` byte-for-byte from S3 and the agent inherits a fully populated archive of every prior session it has held — but the *current* Hermes session is brand new and has no shared `session_id` with any of those rows.

Concrete operator scenarios where the building blocks alone are awkward:

1. **"What did we talk about in our last session about X?"** — `session_search` returns a session id and a ~500-char summary preview, but the answer the user wants sits below the preview cutoff. Today the agent can either (a) hallucinate the rest, (b) tell the user the gap exists, or (c) start fan-out walking via repeated `lcm_grep(session_scope='session') + lcm_expand(store_id=...)` calls until token budget runs out. None of those is what an analyst wants when continuing a multi-week investigation across restarts.
2. **Post-Litestream-restore continuity check.** After a forced task replacement (we just shipped this last week), confirming that the previous task's conversation actually survived the restore currently means probing it tool-call by tool-call. A single `session_load` tool would let the agent reattach to a prior session in one call.
3. **Audit / runbook reconstruction.** A reviewer asking "show me the transcript that produced this finding" maps cleanly to "load that `session_id`", not to "build it up by paging row-by-row".

`session_search` (Hermes built-in) is correctly positioned as the *discovery* tool — it tells you which sessions exist and what they roughly contain. The proposed `session_load` is the natural *retrieval* counterpart for the plugin-local LCM database, in the same way `lcm_grep` is the discovery tool for in-database FTS and `lcm_expand` is its retrieval counterpart.

## Proposed scope

- New tool: `session_load` (name negotiable — `lcm_session_load`, `lcm_load_session`, etc.)
- Required arg: `session_id`
- Bounded by design (mirroring PR #102's clamping):
  - `limit` (clamped to a sensible cap, e.g. 200) — number of raw messages returned per call
  - `cursor` / `after_store_id` for pagination across calls
  - Optional `time_from` / `time_to` to slice a long session
  - Optional `roles=[...]` filter (subject to the same data-layer-pushdown constraint #108 is tracking)
- Result shape:
  - Ordered list of raw messages (chronological), each carrying `store_id`, `role`, `timestamp`, `content`, `source`
  - `next_cursor` for follow-up pages, or `null` when exhausted
  - `total_messages` for the session if cheaply computable
  - `session_id` echoed back for safety
- Cross-session DAG / summary expansion stays explicitly out of scope (consistent with PR #102's deferral) — `session_load` returns raw rows only, same provenance contract as `lcm_grep(session_scope='session')`
- Default behaviour rejects an empty / missing `session_id` (no implicit "current" or "all" fallback)

## Why a separate tool, not an `lcm_grep` extension

`lcm_grep` is search-shaped — it requires a `query` and returns ranked matches. The "load this whole session" use case is enumeration, not search. Forcing it through `lcm_grep` with an empty query (a) muddies the tool's contract, (b) burns the FTS path on a query that doesn't need it, and (c) loses the natural "ordered, paginated, bounded" semantics that a dedicated load tool gets for free.

An equivalent shape worth considering: extending `lcm_expand` with a `session_id` mode that streams ordered rows for a given session. The functional outcome would be similar; this issue uses `session_load` as the working name without prejudice to the final tool surface.

## Out of scope

- Cross-session DAG / summary-node expansion (deferred in #102; same deferral applies here)
- Hermes-side `session_search` integration changes
- Loading sessions that are not present in plugin-local `lcm.db`
- Any privacy / redaction layer beyond the existing local-DB threat model
- Schema changes to `messages` / `summary_nodes`

## Notes

This is a feature request grounded in an operator use case, layered on top of the primitives PR #102 already shipped. Filing it now while the cross-session work is fresh.

title: fix: require replay evidence for restart cursor reconciliation
body:
## Summary
- Requires stronger replay evidence before restart cursor reconciliation skips a non-empty suffix match.
- Preserves complete durable-context replay reconciliation, including minimal transcripts without a system prompt.
- Keeps LCM scaffold-only prefixes skipped while persisting ambiguous repeated tail deltas instead of risking data loss.

## Why
- A restarted existing session could receive a new delta message that repeated the durable store tail.
- The old cursor reconciliation could classify that repeated delta as replay and silently skip it.
- Conservative persistence is safer than losing user-visible conversation history.

title: fix: fall back to Hermes compression threshold
body:
## Summary

- Falls back to Hermes `compression.threshold` from `config.yaml` when `LCM_CONTEXT_THRESHOLD` is not set in the process environment.
- Keeps `LCM_CONTEXT_THRESHOLD` as the explicit override when it is present.

## Why

Hermes gateway/runtime config can have the intended compression threshold without exporting a matching `LCM_CONTEXT_THRESHOLD` env var into the LCM process. In that case LCM silently falls back to its built-in `0.75`, which can drift from the active Hermes compression config and reintroduce context-window warnings.

title: Add message-level ignore patterns for cron/noise suppression
body:
## Problem

`LCM_IGNORE_SESSION_PATTERNS` and `LCM_STATELESS_SESSION_PATTERNS` already provide noise suppression at the session/source level (e.g. `cron:*`). They do not catch a real and recurring case: Hermes cron deliveries that arrive inside a normal Telegram or WhatsApp conversation as ordinary messages whose content starts with a clear marker like:

```
Cronjob Response: hermie-hourly-heartbeat
(job_id: eee06bdbb09b)
-------------
```

or sometimes:

```
>>>Cronjob Response<<<: hermie-hourly-heartbeat
(job_id: eee06bdbb09b)
-------------
```

From LCM's perspective the session/platform is `telegram`, not `cron`, so session-level globs do not catch them. These alerts pollute LCM history and cross-session search results.

## Proposed feature

A new env var `LCM_IGNORE_MESSAGE_PATTERNS`: a comma-separated list of Python regex patterns. If any pattern matches a message's normalized content, the message is skipped before `append_batch`/store ingest, so it never enters the messages table, FTS index, or DAG node lineage.

### Design constraints

- Disabled by default. Default value is empty.
- Patterns are compiled once at engine startup, not per message.
- Compilation errors are tolerated: invalid regex emits a `logger.warning` and is skipped, valid patterns from the same list still take effect.
- Filtering applies to all roles by default, since cron alerts can arrive under any role depending on the gateway.
- Existing `LCM_IGNORE_SESSION_PATTERNS` / `LCM_STATELESS_SESSION_PATTERNS` behavior is preserved unchanged.
- `lcm_status` surfaces the configured patterns, source string (`default` / `env`), and a process-lifetime `ignored_message_count` counter.
- Anchored patterns (e.g. `^Cronjob Response:`) are best-effort against plain-text content. Multimodal/structured content is normalized via `normalize_content_value`, which produces a JSON wrapper and breaks `^` anchoring; operators who need multimodal coverage should use unanchored patterns.

### Example operator config

```
LCM_IGNORE_MESSAGE_PATTERNS=^Cronjob Response:,^>>>Cronjob Response<<<:
```

### Out of scope (deferred to follow-up)

Filtering matching messages out of the compaction chunk fed to the summarizer. On the rare turn where a matching message sits inside the chunk being compacted, its text may briefly appear in the resulting summary node text (its `store_id` will not appear in the node's `source_ids`, because it was never written to the store). A separate issue will track the compaction-input filter once this PR ships and stabilizes.

## Use case

Hermes hourly heartbeat cron sends Telegram alerts starting with `Cronjob Response: hermie-hourly-heartbeat`. Those alerts are useful live in chat, but they pollute LCM history and cross-session search. Normal Telegram conversation should still be stored. Only matching cron announcement messages should be ignored.

title: feat: add message-level ignore patterns for LCM ingest
body:
Closes #117.

## Summary

Adds `LCM_IGNORE_MESSAGE_PATTERNS`, a comma-separated list of Python regex patterns that drops noise out of the immutable LCM message store at ingest time. Designed for the case where Hermes cron alerts (e.g. `Cronjob Response: hermie-hourly-heartbeat`) are delivered into a normal Telegram or WhatsApp conversation as ordinary user-visible messages, so session-level globs like `cron:*` cannot catch them.

The implementation mirrors the existing `LCM_IGNORE_SESSION_PATTERNS` shape: dataclass field + source-diagnostics field, env-parse block in `LCMConfig.from_env()`, dedicated helper module (`message_patterns.py`), one-shot diagnostic log gated by the existing `_logged_filter_config` flag, and three new keys in `lcm_status`. Default behavior is unchanged: when the env var is absent, no filtering happens and all existing tests still pass.

## What's in this PR

- `config.py`: `ignore_message_patterns: list[str]` + `ignore_message_patterns_source: str` fields, `from_env()` block reading `LCM_IGNORE_MESSAGE_PATTERNS`.
- `message_patterns.py` (new): `compile_message_patterns(patterns)` which catches `re.error` per-pattern with a `logger.warning`, and `matches_message_pattern(text, patterns)` using `re.search` so user-supplied anchors (`^`, `\b`) and inline flags (`(?is)`) work as written.
- `engine.py`: compile patterns at init, filter matching messages in `_ingest_messages` before `append_batch`, increment a process-lifetime `_ignored_message_count` counter, surface the new keys in `lcm_status`, extend `_log_session_filter_diagnostics`.
- `tests/test_lcm_core.py`: helper-level `TestMessagePatterns`, plus `LCM_IGNORE_MESSAGE_PATTERNS` coverage in `TestConfig`.
- `tests/test_lcm_engine.py`: new `TestMessageFiltering` class covering anchored matching, wrapper variants, inline-flag patterns, the must-not-regress baseline (active pattern + non-matching messages), multimodal content (both anchored-does-not-match and unanchored-substring-does-match cases), role-agnostic filtering, invalid-regex tolerance, coexistence with `LCM_IGNORE_SESSION_PATTERNS`, status surface, and once-per-engine-instance diagnostic logging.
- `README.md`: env var table row + a noise-suppression section explaining when to use session-level vs message-level filtering, the operator example config line, and two documented limitations.

## Operator example

```
LCM_IGNORE_MESSAGE_PATTERNS=^Cronjob Response:,^>>>Cronjob Response<<<:
```

`lcm_status` then reports `ignore_message_patterns`, `ignore_message_patterns_source` (`default` or `env`), and a process-lifetime `ignored_message_count` so operators can confirm their config was loaded and watch how often it fires.

## Documented limitations

- **Anchored patterns are best-effort against multimodal content.** Structured payloads (lists of content parts) are normalized via `normalize_content_value`'s JSON serialization before matching, so `^Cronjob Response:` binds to the JSON wrapper rather than to the inner text. Operators who need multimodal coverage should write unanchored patterns. Tests assert both the anchored-does-not-match and unanchored-substring-does-match cases explicitly so the contract is documented in code.
- **Compaction-window edge.** The filter runs at ingest. On a rare turn where a matching message is part of the chunk being summarized in the same turn it arrived, its text may briefly appear inside the resulting summary node text. The summary node's `source_ids` will not reference the filtered message (it was never written to the store), so DAG lineage stays clean. Closing this window cleanly requires also adjusting the `len(compacted_chunk)`-based slice arithmetic in `compress()`, which materially expands the diff; tracked as follow-up work.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest tests/test_lcm_core.py::TestMessagePatterns` — 6 helper tests pass.
- [x] `pytest tests/test_lcm_core.py::TestConfig` — defaults + from_env coverage pass with the new field.
- [x] `pytest tests/test_lcm_engine.py::TestMessageFiltering` — 12 ingest/status/log scenarios pass.
- [x] `pytest tests/test_lcm_engine.py::TestSessionFiltering` — regression guard for session-level filter, all green.
- [x] `pytest tests/test_lcm_engine.py::TestEngineIngest` — regression guard for cursor invariant, all green.
- [x] Full suite: 471 passed (up from 453 before this PR).

title: Follow-up review findings from PR #118 (LCM_IGNORE_MESSAGE_PATTERNS)
body:
Multi-agent code review of PR #118 surfaced findings split across three categories: small uncontroversial fixes (already opened as a follow-up PR), a pre-existing tool-handler gap that affects all pattern types and warrants a separate scope discussion, and items that need maintainer input on fix shape before any code change lands.

## Reviewers

- correctness, testing, maintainability, project-standards (always-on)
- ce-agent-native-reviewer, ce-learnings-researcher (CE always-on)
- api-contract (lcm_status JSON shape gained 3 keys)
- adversarial (398 substantive changed lines, hot ingest-path regex matching)
- kieran-python (Python diff with new module + engine wiring)

## P1

### #1 (pre-existing) - `lcm_status` tool handler does not forward pattern-config keys to agents

**Status: not introduced by #118.** The `tools.py:lcm_status` handler at `tools.py:1160-1243` builds its own JSON dict and only forwards a curated subset of `engine.get_status()`. Specifically, the existing `session_filters` block at `tools.py:1235-1238` only forwards two booleans:

\`\`\`python
\"session_filters\": {
    \"ignored\": engine._session_ignored,
    \"stateless\": engine._session_stateless,
},
\`\`\`

It has never forwarded `ignore_session_patterns`, `ignore_session_patterns_source`, `stateless_session_patterns`, or `stateless_session_patterns_source`. PR #118 added three new keys to `engine.get_status()` (`ignore_message_patterns`, `ignore_message_patterns_source`, `ignored_message_count`) and they follow the same pattern - also not forwarded.

**Options for discussion:**
1. Surface all pattern config (session, stateless, message) via `lcm_status` together. Treats agent visibility as a uniform contract for all three pattern types.
2. Keep the curated subset and update README docs to clarify that pattern-config keys live on `engine.get_status()` but not on the agent-facing `lcm_status` tool.
3. Surface only the newly-added message-pattern keys (asymmetric, probably worse than option 1 or 2).

**Why this matters:** the README and #118 PR body both claim `lcm_status` surfaces the new keys. The claim is true at the engine layer (which is what `TestMessageFiltering::test_status_surfaces_message_pattern_keys` asserts) but the agent-facing tool surface is the one operators actually consume.

### #3 ReDoS guard for ingest path

Operator-supplied regex without length cap or timeout can stall ingest synchronously. Empirically reproducible: `re.search(r'(a+)+$', 'a'*32 + 'X')` blocks for ~5 minutes against pathological input. Hermes ingest is synchronous, so a misconfigured pattern stalls the agent.

**Options for discussion:**
1. Length-cap the input passed to `re.search` (e.g., 100KB). Cheap, no dependencies. Limits what regex can see for very-long messages but defends against catastrophic backtracking.
2. Migrate to the `regex` library (PyPI), which supports timeouts. Adds a dependency.
3. Run the match in a watchdog thread with a timeout. Adds threading complexity per-message.

The plan dismissed this as \"operator-supplied trusted\" but solo operators write their own configs and the failure mode is observable as agent unavailability, not just degraded results.

## P2

### #4 Compaction-window leak framing is more frequent than \"rare turn\" suggests

The README's noise-suppression section says \"On a rare turn where a matching message is part of the chunk being summarized in the same turn it arrived, the message's text may briefly appear inside the resulting summary node text.\"

Adversarial reviewer's traffic math: hourly cron + ~40-turn compaction cadence in long-running Telegram sessions means multiple compactions per 24h session may include cron text. \"Rare\" oversells the guarantee.

The follow-up PR softens \"On a rare turn where\" to \"When\", which is more accurate without changing behavior.

### #5 Multimodal anchored-pattern UX trap

Operators write `^Cronjob Response:` (per the README example), then their gateway delivers cron alerts as multimodal payloads, the JSON-wrapped form starts with `[{`, the anchor never matches, and the filter silently no-ops with no observable signal in `lcm_status`. The README documents the limitation but the test (`test_anchored_pattern_does_not_match_multimodal_content`) pins the surprising behavior as a contract.

**Options for discussion:**
1. Status quo: keep documented limitation. Operators must write unanchored patterns or test against actual gateway output.
2. Extract concatenated text parts from structured content before matching. Anchored patterns work as expected; structured payloads with no text part fall back to the JSON form.
3. Surface a status-level warning when both anchored patterns AND structured-content messages are observed in the same session.

## P3 (small fixes addressed in the follow-up PR)

### #6 Stateless-session + message-filter coexistence test

Only the ignored-session case is currently tested. The early-return covers stateless too, so the path is correct but uncovered. The follow-up PR adds the regression test.

### #7 Cursor-advancement-under-all-filtered regression test

When the filter drops every message in a batch, `_ingest_cursor` still advances to `n` (engine.py:1831). 3 reviewers independently flagged that this code path has no regression test. The follow-up PR adds it.

### #8 `LCM_STATUS` tool description does not mention message-pattern state

`schemas.py:LCM_STATUS` describes the tool as showing \"compression count, store size, DAG depth distribution, context usage, and active configuration.\" After #118, it also surfaces (in `engine.get_status()`) message-pattern filter state. The follow-up PR extends the description so agents diagnosing missing messages know to look there.

## P3 (style/judgment items, no PR action)

These are surfaced for transparency but the follow-up PR does not address them - they're style choices best left to the maintainer.

- **#9** `from typing import Iterable, List` in `message_patterns.py` is redundant given `from __future__ import annotations`. Sibling `session_patterns.py` has the same issue. Cleanup is repo-wide and out of #118 follow-up scope.
- **#10** No singular `compile_message_pattern` to mirror `compile_session_pattern`. Symmetry break, marginal value.
- **#11** In-place filter loop in `_ingest_messages` adds a fifth concern; could extract `_filter_ignored_messages` helper.
- **#12** Three near-identical 5-line config-log blocks in `_log_session_filter_diagnostics`; a fourth pattern family will warrant a tuple-driven loop refactor.

## Run artifact

Full per-reviewer JSON outputs at `/tmp/compound-engineering/ce-code-review/20260506-152050-2a12390e/` on the reviewer's local machine. Available on request if any specific finding needs deeper context.

## Follow-up PR

A small follow-up PR addresses #4, #6, #7, and #8 only. The pre-existing #1 and the design-question items #3, #5 are intentionally left for separate discussion via this issue.

title: chore: address review follow-ups for message-ignore-patterns
body:
Refs #119.

Small uncontroversial follow-ups from the multi-agent code review of PR #118 (`feat: add message-level ignore patterns for LCM ingest`). The full review report is on issue #119; this PR addresses only the items that don't need design discussion.

## What's in this PR

Adversarial review's traffic math (hourly cron alerts + ~40-turn compaction cadence) suggested the framing oversold the guarantee. Asserts both that the cursor advances correctly and that the counter does not double-increment on the second call.

The `session_filters` block currently only forwards the `ignored` and `stateless` booleans, not the raw pattern lists or source strings. title: fix: guard message ignore regex matching
body:
## Summary
- Add per-pattern timeout handling for message ignore regex matching when the optional `regex` engine is available.
- Treat regex timeouts as non-matches, log once per pattern, and continue evaluating later patterns so ingest remains available.

## Why
- Refs #119.
- `LCM_IGNORE_MESSAGE_PATTERNS` runs in synchronous ingest. A pathological operator regex can otherwise stall the agent instead of merely failing to filter noise.

title: Ignored/stateless sessions can rebind current LCM session after cron runs
body:
## Summary

When Hermes runs a cron job in the same gateway process as a conversational session (Telegram, CLI, etc.), the cron session's `on_session_start` rebinds `LCMEngine._session_id` to the cron session id even though the session matches `LCM_IGNORE_SESSION_PATTERNS` (or `LCM_STATELESS_SESSION_PATTERNS`). Every LCM tool that defaults to "the current session" then reports the cron session for the rest of the cron run, even from concurrent foreground tool calls.

Symptom observed by an operator: `lcm_status` returns `session_id=cron_<job-hash>_<timestamp>`, `platform=cron`, `session_filters.ignored=true`, `store.messages=0` while the foreground Telegram DM session has stored rows in `lcm.db` and is the conversation the operator is actively in.

## Why this happens

Hermes-LCM registers a single `LCMEngine` per gateway process via `ctx.register_context_engine(engine)`. Every `AIAgent` in that process resolves the same singleton. Cron schedules a `concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor` worker per job, constructs an `AIAgent(platform="cron", session_id="cron_...")`, and that constructor calls `context_compressor.on_session_start(cron_session_id, ...)`.

Inside `LCMEngine.on_session_start`, the cron session does not match either of the two existing carve-outs:

- `boundary_reason == "compression"` (compression rollover path) does not apply.
- `_is_live_auxiliary_child_session(...)` returns `False` because cron is constructed without `parent_session_id`, so its `state.db` row has `parent_session_id=NULL` and the in-process call-stack walk does not find an auxiliary agent frame.

Execution falls through to `_apply_session_start_metadata`, which unconditionally sets `self._session_id = session_id` before `_refresh_session_filters()` evaluates the ignore/stateless patterns. By the time `_session_ignored=True` is set, the rebind has already happened. Tool reads of `engine._session_id` (`tools.py:lcm_status`, `lcm_grep` default scope, `_get_session_node`, `_get_externalized_payload`, `_expand_message_sources`, `_serialize_loaded_message`, `lcm_describe`, `lcm_expand`, `lcm_expand_query`, `lcm_doctor`, `command.py:_status_text`) then surface the cron id as the "current session" until the next foreground `on_session_start` rebinds the engine back.

The cron's own lifecycle hooks (`compress`, `should_compress_preflight`, `_ingest_messages`, `handle_tool_call`) correctly short-circuit on `_session_ignored=True`, so cron transcripts do not pollute the foreground store. The bug is purely a "what session does the user-facing tool surface report" issue, not a data-corruption issue. But during a long-running tool-use loop on the foreground side, every concurrent `lcm_status` / `lcm_grep` call sees the cron id, which is confusing at best and breaks any agent tooling that trusts the reported session id.

## Repro

Empirical repro that reaches the bug from the engine surface alone:

```python
from hermes_lcm.config import LCMConfig
from hermes_lcm.engine import LCMEngine

cfg = LCMConfig(
    database_path="/tmp/lcm-repro.db",
    ignore_session_patterns=["cron:*"],
)
engine = LCMEngine(config=cfg)

engine.on_session_start("telegram-fg", platform="telegram", context_length=200_000)
engine._store.append("telegram-fg", {"role": "user", "content": "tg-1"}, token_estimate=1)

engine.on_session_start("cron_xxx", platform="cron", context_length=200_000)

# engine._session_id == "cron_xxx" (rebound)
# engine._session_ignored is True (correctly classified as ignored)
# but lcm_status / lcm_grep / lcm_describe / etc. all read _session_id and surface "cron_xxx"
```

In a real deployment this happens whenever a cron tick fires while a Telegram (or any other foreground) session is processing tool calls in the same gateway process. The LCM database already contains historical evidence: cron session rows from before `LCM_IGNORE_SESSION_PATTERNS=cron:*` was added still have ingested message rows, confirming the rebind has been happening for as long as cron and conversational sessions have shared a process.

## Expected behavior

The user-visible "current session" surface should remain the foreground session for as long as one is bound, even while a side-channel session (cron, debug, or any other session matching the configured ignore/stateless patterns) is being serviced by the engine.

The engine's bound state can keep tracking the side channel because that is what gates the side channel's own `compress` / `_ingest_messages` calls. Only the user-facing view needs to stay stable.

## Affected surfaces

- `lcm_status` (`session_id`, `store.messages`, `dag.*`, `session_filters`).
- `lcm_grep` default scope (`session_scope=current`) and unknown-scope fallback.
- `_get_session_node`, `_get_externalized_payload`, `_expand_message_sources`, `_expand_child_nodes`, `_serialize_loaded_message`.
- `lcm_describe` overview.
- `lcm_expand` (`store_id` mode `from_current_session` flag, `node_id` mode session-scope check).
- `lcm_expand_query` search and node lookup.
- `lcm_doctor` (the diagnostic checks themselves run against whatever session is bound).
- `command.py` `_status_text` and `_doctor_retention_text` (operator `/lcm status` and `/lcm doctor retention`).

## Severity

High for any deployment running cron jobs in the same gateway process as conversational sessions, which is the standard `hermes serve` topology. Not destructive; ignored sessions still skip ingest and compaction. The bug shows up as a binding leak, not data corruption.

## Proposed fix shape

Add a separate `_foreground_session_id` field that tracks the most recent non-ignored, non-stateless binding, plus a `current_session_id` property that returns `_foreground_session_id` (with fallback to `_session_id` when no foreground has ever bound). Keep `on_session_start` rebinding `_session_id` exactly as it does today so cron's own lifecycle hooks continue to short-circuit correctly. Switch tool-surface reads to `current_session_id`.

PR forthcoming.

title: fix: prevent ignored sessions from rebinding current LCM session
body:
## Summary

- Track the most recent non-ignored, non-stateless binding in a new `_foreground_session_id` field; expose it via `current_session_id` / `current_session_platform` properties on `LCMEngine`.
- Tool-surface code paths (`lcm_status`, `lcm_grep` default scope, `_get_session_node`, `_get_externalized_payload`, `_expand_message_sources`, `_expand_child_nodes`, `_serialize_loaded_message`, `lcm_describe`, `lcm_expand`, `lcm_expand_query`, `lcm_doctor`, `_status_text`, `_doctor_retention_text`) now read `current_session_id` so a cron-style ignored session that briefly rebinds `_session_id` cannot divert lcm_status / lcm_grep / etc. away from the operator's foreground conversation.
- Lifecycle paths inside the engine (`compress`, `should_compress_preflight`, `_ingest_messages`, `handle_tool_call`) continue to read `_session_id` directly, so cron's own calls still short-circuit on `_session_ignored=True` and cannot leak cron transcripts into the foreground store.
- `lcm_status` surfaces the diagnostic `session_filters.side_channel_active` flag (and `side_channel_session_id` when active) so operators can still observe a cron tick that has rebound the engine. `/lcm status` reports the same flag.

## Why

`hermes-lcm` registers a single `LCMEngine` per gateway process. When a cron job runs in the same process as a Telegram (or any other) conversation, cron's `AIAgent.__init__` calls `engine.on_session_start("cron_...")`. That unconditionally sets `self._session_id = cron_xxx` before `_refresh_session_filters` evaluates the ignore patterns, so every LCM tool that defaults to "the current session" reports the cron id from concurrent foreground tool calls (e.g., `lcm_status` returning `session_id=cron_xxx, ignored=true, store.messages=0` while the foreground Telegram session has rows in `lcm.db`). Full diagnosis in #126.

The first iteration of this fix tried to skip the rebind for ignored sessions, but that introduced a worse regression: with `_session_ignored=False` (because the engine stayed bound to the foreground), cron's own `_ingest_messages` no longer short-circuited and cron transcripts leaked into the foreground store. An empirical probe confirmed 4 cron messages writing through to a 1-row foreground session.

The shadow-field approach in this PR avoids the regression by keeping the existing rebind path intact (so cron's lifecycle gating keeps working) while exposing a separate `current_session_id` view for tools. Bound state and foreground state are decoupled.

## Validation

- [x] Focused validation: `pytest tests/test_lcm_engine.py tests/test_lcm_command.py -q` -> `318 passed in 17.85s`
- [x] Default validation:
  - [x] `pytest tests/test_lcm_core.py tests/test_lcm_engine.py tests/test_packaging_install.py -q` -> 449 passed
  - [x] `pytest -q` -> 497 passed
  - [x] `python -m compileall -q .` -> ok
  - [x] `python -m py_compile scripts/import_lossless_claw.py` -> ok
  - [x] `bash -n scripts/install.sh scripts/update.sh` -> ok
  - [x] `git diff --check` -> ok
- [x] Cron-leak regression probe: ran `engine.on_session_start("telegram-fg")` -> append 1 row -> `engine.on_session_start("cron_xxx")` -> `engine.compress(cron_messages)` + `engine.should_compress_preflight(cron_messages)`. Result: telegram store stays at 1 row, cron store at 0 rows. Pre-fix probe (skip-rebind variant) showed 5 telegram rows.

## New tests

- `test_ignored_session_does_not_rebind_foreground_view` -- foreground view stays stable when an ignored session rebinds the bound state.
- `test_ignored_session_compress_does_not_leak_into_foreground_store` -- regression test for the rejected first-iteration approach: cron messages must not leak into the foreground store.
- `test_lcm_status_stays_on_foreground_after_cron_tick` -- end-to-end via the `lcm_status` tool, with `side_channel_active` and `side_channel_session_id` diagnostics.
- `test_lcm_status_reports_bound_session_when_no_foreground_yet` -- cron-only deployment: `current_session_id` falls back to `_session_id` so the surface remains observable.
- `test_stateless_session_does_not_rebind_foreground_view` -- the same protection applies to stateless side-channel sessions.
- `test_lcm_command_status_text_is_consistent_with_lcm_status_during_cron_tick` -- `/lcm status` operator surface stays consistent with `lcm_status` output.
- `test_lcm_doctor_retention_targets_foreground_during_cron_tick` -- `/lcm doctor retention` reports retention for the foreground session, not the cron-bound one.
- `test_foreground_view_advances_when_a_real_foreground_arrives` -- `_foreground_session_id` advances forward through real foreground bindings (e.g., compression rollovers) and is never set to an ignored or stateless id.
- `test_lcm_tool_status_forwards_filter_config_to_agent_surface` updated to expect the new `side_channel_active` key.

## Notes

- Reviewed twice via parallel multi-persona review (correctness, testing, maintainability, project-standards, agent-native, kieran-python, learnings-researcher). The first round caught the cron-leak regression on the rejected approach; the second round on the shadow-field approach surfaced the `_status_text` consistency gap, the operator-protection comments, and the `side_channel_active` encapsulation, all addressed in this PR.
- Out of scope: the deeper concurrency property -- a cron tick that rebinds `_session_id` to an ignored session also pauses foreground compaction during the cron run window, because the foreground thread's `compress` / `_ingest_messages` calls see `_session_ignored=True` until the next foreground `on_session_start`. Fixing that requires per-task session resolution (ContextVars or explicit thread-local push that propagates through `contextvars.copy_context()`), which is an architectural change outside this PR's scope. The window is bounded (cron runs are typically short, and a fresh `AIAgent` per inbound foreground message rebinds the engine back), and no data corrupts.
- `command.py` retention/cleanup sites (`_scan_clean_candidates`, `_delete_clean_candidates_atomically`, the `protected` flag in `_scan_retention_candidates`) intentionally read `_session_id` (bound), with comments explaining the contract: the actively-bound session is the row receiving live writes from the concurrent run, so deletion / cleanup must protect it regardless of the foreground view.

Refs #126

Closes #126

title: feat: optional filter to reduce LCM tool surface (exposed_tools config)
body:
## Problem

LCM injects 7 tools into every agent session via `engine.get_tool_schemas()`: `lcm_grep`, `lcm_load_session`, `lcm_describe`, `lcm_expand`, `lcm_expand_query`, `lcm_status`, `lcm_doctor`.

In tool-count-sensitive agent configurations, this represents a meaningful share of the total tool surface. The compression engine itself is independent — `compress()` is invoked from the host agent loop, not from any tool handler — so reducing the LLM-facing tool surface does not affect compression behavior. The cost is purely in schema bytes and tool-selection space presented to the model.

## Proposal

Add an `exposed_tools` field to `LCMConfig` that filters the schemas returned by `get_tool_schemas()`:

```yaml
lcm:
  exposed_tools: [lcm_grep, lcm_describe]  # default: all 7
```

Implementation surface:
- One field added to `LCMConfig` in `config.py` (with env-var override).
- Filter applied in `engine.get_tool_schemas()` — roughly a list comprehension over the existing schema constants.
- No changes to `handle_tool_call` — unrequested tools simply won't be invoked by the LLM, and the existing `Unknown LCM tool` path covers the edge case.
- No new dispatcher logic, no union schemas, no mode enum.

`plugin.yaml`'s `provides_tools` continues to enumerate the maximal set — it represents capability, not runtime exposure. The `/lcm` slash command (`command.py`) is unaffected since it doesn't route through `handle_tool_call`.

## Defaults & introspection

- Default behavior unchanged: all 7 tools exposed when `exposed_tools` is unset.
- `lcm_status` is added to any non-empty configuration unless explicitly excluded — agents rely on it to discover LCM is running. Operators who genuinely want zero tool surface can set `exposed_tools: []` explicitly to opt out.
- Existing tests (`test_packaging_install.py` asserting the 7-tool set) continue to pass under the default.

## Why at this layer?

A host-level tool budget in the calling agent (Hermes, etc.) would solve this for all plugins simultaneously and is probably the better long-term architecture — I'd support that proposal upstream too.

Plugin-level granularity is still useful even with a host budget: operators commonly want to keep all memory tools while reducing LCM tools (or vice versa), which a flat global cap can't express cleanly. The two are complementary, not exclusive. This issue is the narrow, immediate fix at the LCM level.

## Reproduction

The motivating case is an agent session resolving roughly 26 tools (host + memory + LCM), where the configured proxy fails on the primary path before falling back to a different completion provider. The compression engine continues to function via the fallback, but the primary path is unusable while LCM is loaded with its full surface.

I'll attach concrete logs (proxy configuration + exact error output + tool count at failure) in the PR rather than fabricating specifics here. If a maintainer wants to see the repro before the PR, I can post it as a comment.

## Implementation

Working prototype locally. PR will include:
- The `exposed_tools` field with env-var override.
- Tests for: default 7-tool exposure, arbitrary filtered subset, empty-list explicit-zero-tools behavior, `lcm_status` always-default-visible.
- README update with config reference and an example for tool-count-sensitive setups.
- Concrete repro evidence from my deployment.

If the team prefers to defer this until a host-level budget lands instead, I'm fine to close.

title: LCM context assembly crashes when first Hermes message is multimodal user content
body:
## Bug Description

`hermes-lcm` can crash during context assembly for Hermes gateway sessions whose first persisted conversation message is multimodal/structured content.

Observed gateway/user-facing error:

```text
Sorry, I encountered an error (TypeError).
can only concatenate list (not "str") to list
```

Stack trace points at `_assemble_context()` appending the LCM note:

```text
run_agent.py -> _compress_context(...)
plugins/hermes-lcm/engine.py -> compress(...)
plugins/hermes-lcm/engine.py -> _assemble_context(...)
TypeError: can only concatenate list (not "str") to list
```

Relevant code on current `origin/main` still appears to do a raw `content + str` append:

```python
# engine.py:_assemble_context
sys_msg = system_msg.copy()
if self.compression_count == 0 and include_lcm_note:
    sys_content = sys_msg.get("content", "")
    sys_msg["content"] = (
        sys_content
        + "\n\n[Note: This conversation uses Lossless Context Management (LCM). "
        "Earlier turns have been compacted into hierarchical summaries below. "
        "Use lcm_grep to search history, lcm_describe to inspect the DAG, "
        "and lcm_expand to recover original details from any summary.]"
    )
```

## Why this happens

In the failing Hermes Discord thread, `messages[0]` was **not** a system prompt. It was the first user message, and because Discord routed attached images natively to a vision-capable model, its content was OpenAI-style structured/multimodal content:

```python
{
    "role": "user",
    "content": [
        {"type": "text", "text": "..."},
        {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "..."}},
        {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "..."}},
    ],
}
```

LCM appears to assume `working_messages[0]` / `system_msg` is always a string-content system message:

```python
# engine.py:compress
# Protect system prompt (always index 0)
candidate_raw = working_messages[1:fresh_tail_start]
...
compressed = self._assemble_context(
    working_messages[0],
    working_messages[1:],
    ...
)
```

But Hermes core passes the conversation `messages` list to context engines directly, without prepending the system prompt to that list:

```python
# run_agent.py:_compress_context
compressed = self.context_compressor.compress(
    messages,
    current_tokens=approx_tokens,
    focus_topic=focus_topic,
)
```

So for gateway sessions, index 0 can be the first user message. If that message is text-only, the bug is partially masked because `str + str` succeeds, although the LCM note is still attached to a user message. If it is multimodal, Python raises `list + str`.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Use Hermes Agent with `hermes-lcm` enabled and selected as the context engine.
2. Start a new Discord/gateway thread with a first user message containing text plus image attachments, such that the persisted first message has `content` as a list of content parts.
3. Continue the session until context compression triggers.
4. Observe `_assemble_context()` treating the first user message as `system_msg` and attempting `list + str`.

A minimal unit-style repro should be possible by calling `LCMEngine.compress()` / `_assemble_context()` with a first message shaped like:

```python
messages = [
    {
        "role": "user",
        "content": [
            {"type": "text", "text": "hello"},
            {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "data:image/png;base64,..."}},
        ],
    },
    # enough additional messages to trigger compaction/assembly...
]
```

## Expected Behavior

LCM should not assume the active conversation list always starts with a system message.

Possible acceptable behavior:

- If `messages[0].get("role") == "system"`, append the LCM note using a structured-content-safe append helper.
- If there is no system message in the active message list, either:
  - insert a separate valid system/developer/user scaffold message for the LCM note, or
  - omit the note, or
  - otherwise handle the no-system case explicitly.
- Structured/multimodal content should never be concatenated directly with a string.

## Actual Behavior

LCM assumes index 0 is a system prompt and directly concatenates its `content` with a string. When `content` is a list, compression crashes and the Hermes gateway returns an error to the user.

## Environment

Observed locally:

- Hermes Agent: `v0.12.0 (2026.4.30)`
- Runtime: macOS launchd gateway, Discord thread session
- Installed `hermes-lcm`: `0.8.0` at commit `0f60d72`
- Local LCM was behind `origin/main` by 20 commits at investigation time
- Checked current LCM `origin/main` and the same raw-concat `_assemble_context()` code path still appears present

Related but distinct prior fix:

- #77 fixed SQLite persistence of list-form structured content (`Error binding parameter ... type 'list' is not supported`). This issue is a later assembly-time failure: `list + str` in `_assemble_context()`.

## Proposed Fix

1. Add a regression test for compression/assembly with no system message and a multimodal first user message.
2. Make `_assemble_context()` role-aware:

```python
sys_msg = system_msg.copy()
if sys_msg.get("role") == "system":
    # append LCM note safely
else:
    # do not treat it as a system prompt
```

3. Use `normalize_content_value()` or a structured-content-safe append helper before appending text.
4. Consider clarifying the context-engine contract with Hermes core: either context engines receive the system prompt as `messages[0]`, or they must handle message lists that start with user/assistant/tool messages.

title: fix: preserve latest user objective during compaction
body:
## Summary
- Keep the latest real user message as an explicit active-context anchor when LCM compaction would otherwise omit it from the fresh tail.
- Skip Hermes' synthetic preserved-todo context when choosing that anchor, so the real user request remains dominant.
- Add a regression test for a tool-heavy turn where assistant/tool messages push the current user request outside the normal fresh-tail window.

## Bug
In long gateway sessions, a user can change objectives and then the assistant may run many tool calls before LCM compacts. Because the fresh tail is message-count based, those assistant/tool messages can push the latest user request out of the active context. The next post-compaction prompt can then contain old summarized goals plus mechanical tool traces, but not the current user request verbatim. In practice this can make the agent regress to an older task after a compression/session split.

A user-side workaround is to increase the fresh-tail count, but that is not a rigorous fix: tool-heavy turns can still exceed the configured window, and a larger tail increases context/cost for every session. The engine should preserve the active objective directly.

## Fix
The change is intentionally small:

1. During normal `compress()`, temporarily provide `_assemble_context()` with the original pre-compaction message window.
2. `_assemble_context()` keeps the newest non-synthetic user message if it is not already present in the selected tail.
3. The anchor is inserted after summaries and before the fresh tail, so provider-safe assistant/tool sequencing remains intact.
4. Direct `_assemble_context()` callers and overflow recovery paths keep their existing behavior because anchoring is opt-in during normal compaction only.

## Testing
- `pytest tests/test_lcm_engine.py::TestEngineCompress::test_compress_preserves_latest_user_request_outside_fresh_tail -q`
  - Verified RED before the implementation: failed because the latest user request was absent from compressed active context.
  - Verified GREEN after the implementation: passed.
- `pytest tests/test_lcm_engine.py::TestEngineCompress -q`
  - `18 passed`
- `git diff --check`
- `pytest tests -q`
  - `523 passed, 39 warnings`


_NOTE:_ This was put together in conjunction with gpt-5.5 through hermes-agent mainly as a tool for identifying the problem through log investigations with human guidance for applying the fix. Feel free to leave feedback on the implementation, I naturally do not have deep experience with the codebase but just wanted to use my experiences to help forward this great project! Thanks in advance for the consideration.

title: Feature: auto-link sessions into conversations when gateway doesn't pass conversation_id
body:
## Problem

When the host/gateway starts an LCM session without a stable `conversation_id`, LCM binds that session as its own conversation. Across `/new`, restarts, or session rotation, related sessions can become separate lifecycle islands.

That breaks the intended behavior for:

- lifecycle rollover
- retained summary carry-over
- bounded cross-session search within the same real conversation

## Current understanding

LCM lifecycle binding uses the `conversation_id` passed to `on_session_start(...)`. If that value is missing, LCM falls back to `session_id`.

#167 was a prior attempt, but it was closed unmerged after review showed the derivation happened too late and only affected status/display output. It should be treated as background, not as the current implementation path.

## Desired contract

The host should pass a stable conversation identity into LCM at session start:

```python
on_session_start(session_id, conversation_id=<stable host conversation id>, ...)
```

That identity should come from host/gateway routing context rather than LCM guessing after lifecycle binding.

The id must also be scoped to sub-conversations where the platform has them:

- Telegram simple chat or DM: same chat stays in the same LCM conversation
- Telegram forum topic/thread: each topic/thread is isolated
- Discord channel/thread: thread scope is preserved according to the gateway session identity
- no thread/topic: existing chat/channel-level behavior is unchanged

## Related tracking

- Thread/topic acceptance criterion: #171
- Closed prior attempt: #167, not merged

title: commit_memory_session() missing context_compressor.on_session_end() call
fix: restore filtered grep and carried source expansion
body:
## Summary

This fixes two retrieval gaps around the newer cross-session and rollover flows.

What changed:

- `lcm_grep` exposes `role`, `time_from`, and `time_to` again, and applies them inside `MessageStore.search` before candidate limiting. The LIKE fallback path gets the same filters.
- `lcm_grep` omits summary hits when raw-message filters are active, so a role or timestamp filter does not return unfiltered summaries.
- Summary source filtering now pages through bounded DAG search candidates when `source` is active, instead of filtering only the first candidate window. This covers both FTS and LIKE fallback paths.
- `lcm_expand(node_id=...)` can now expand a current-session carried-over summary node whose raw `source_ids` still point at the previous session.
- README and tool schema text document the raw-filter and carried-over expansion contracts.

Fixes #108
Fixes #110

## Why

#108 was still open because `role`, `time_from`, and `time_to` were absent from `lcm_grep`, and passing them manually was ignored after the first candidate window. #110 was still reproducible because carried-over summaries moved to the new session, while their raw message sources stayed in the old session and were filtered out during expansion.

The latest update also fixes the remaining summary `source` filter gap from review: source matching for summary nodes is now bounded by the existing candidate cap, not by the first fetched window.

## Validation

title: fix: handle multimodal first message assembly
body:
## Summary

Fixes context assembly when Hermes gateway sessions do not include a leading system prompt in the message list.

The change keeps the existing leading-message anchor behavior, but only appends the LCM note when that leading message is actually `role: system`. If the first message is a multimodal user message, LCM leaves it unchanged instead of treating it like a system prompt. Structured system content is also handled safely by appending the note as a text content part rather than concatenating a string onto a list.

## Why

Hermes core can pass only conversation messages to context engines. In gateway sessions, that means `messages[0]` can be the first user message. title: KeyboardInterrupt during session-end cleanup can print shutdown traceback
body:
## Bug Description

Pressing Ctrl+C while Hermes is shutting down can surface a traceback from `hermes-lcm` session-end cleanup if the interrupt lands while final messages are being ingested/token-counted.

The session-end path is already best-effort and fails open for SQLite lock errors. It should also fail open for `KeyboardInterrupt` during final flush/finalization so operator-initiated shutdown does not produce a noisy traceback.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Use Hermes with the `hermes-lcm` context engine enabled.
2. Exit/interrupt the CLI with Ctrl+C while session-end cleanup is running.
3. If the interrupt lands during `_ingest_messages()`, e.g. token counting via `tiktoken`, the cleanup path can raise `KeyboardInterrupt` out of `LCMEngine.on_session_end()`.

## Expected Behavior

Session-end cleanup should be best-effort: log a warning and return when interrupted, similar to the existing SQLite-lock fail-open behavior.

## Actual Behavior

A traceback can be printed during shutdown. Example stack shape:

```text
KeyboardInterrupt
  ... cli.py _run_cleanup
  ... run_agent.py shutdown_memory_provider
  ... hermes-lcm/engine.py on_session_end
  ... hermes-lcm/engine.py _ingest_messages
  ... hermes-lcm/tokens.py count_message_tokens
  ... tiktoken.get_encoding("cl100k_base")
```

## Proposed Fix

Handle `KeyboardInterrupt` inside `LCMEngine.on_session_end()` around the bounded best-effort final flush/finalization paths, and add regression tests for interruption during raw-message ingest and lifecycle finalization.
