title: fix: add CREATE_NO_WINDOW to _git() subprocess call on Windows
body:
## Problem

When the Hermes gateway runs under `pythonw.exe` (GUI subsystem, no console), the `subprocess.run()` call to `git` in `_git()` (engine.py) allocates a visible `conhost.exe` window.

## Root Cause

`pythonw.exe` is a GUI-subsystem process with no console. When it spawns a console-mode child (like `git.exe`), the child allocates its own console — which appears as a visible window. The `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` flag (`0x08000000`) suppresses this.

## Fix

Add `creationflags=0x08000000` (`CREATE_NO_WINDOW`) to the `subprocess.run()` call in `_git()` on Windows. No-op on POSIX.

```python
if sys.platform == "win32":
    popen_kwargs["creationflags"] = 0x08000000  # CREATE_NO_WINDOW
```

## Testing

- Verified on Windows 10 with Hermes gateway running as `pythonw.exe`
- `git` calls from LCM engine no longer pop up console windows
- POSIX behavior unchanged

title: Data-safety fixes: GC tombstone, ingest visibility, ignore-drop count, recall order
body:
## Summary
- Transcript GC only takes the fast externalized-ref branch when the whole row IS the placeholder (`is_externalized_placeholder`); an embedded ref now falls through to the content-equality lookup instead of tombstoning the entire row.
- Per-turn `ingest()` and `should_compress_preflight()` record persistence failures (count, last error) instead of swallowing them at debug; `get_status()` and `lcm_doctor` surface an `ingest_health` check, and failures escalate to error when consecutive.
- Preflight fails closed on ingest failure (does not compact against a store missing the latest turn) but still honors emergency overflow recovery.
- `ignore_message_patterns` drops are counted, logged at info, and surfaced in status/doctor (`ignore_pattern_drops`).
- The relevance/hybrid LIKE search fallback scans deterministically recent-first up to the candidate cap instead of scoring an arbitrary storage-order slice with no `ORDER BY`.

## Why
- The core guarantee is that nothing is ever lost, but a tool row that merely quotes an externalized placeholder (e.g. output of the LCM recall tools) had its surrounding, never-externalized text discarded by GC.
- A failing store (disk full, lock beyond busy-timeout, corruption) previously stopped persisting turns silently, with only a debug log; the loss must be operator-visible and must not let the prompt overflow the provider.
- An over-broad `ignore_message_patterns` silently discarded substantive turns from the "lossless" store; drops should at least be visible.
- Without an `ORDER BY`, relevance/hybrid recall on CJK/degraded-FTS queries never scored the best matches beyond the first storage-order page.

## Validation
- Resolved current-main merge conflicts on branch head `f66c290`.
- Addressed Codex P2 on LIKE fallback ordering: SQL candidate cap now orders by relevance/hybrid primary score before exact whole-query tie-breaks, avoiding single-term exact rows crowding out stronger multi-term matches.
- Focused local validation with host stub: CJK LIKE fallback relevance tests, exact whole-query/multi-term regression tests, sensitive-ingest search regression, and ingest-failure status tests passed.
- CI green on head `f66c290`: workflow-lint and Python 3.11, 3.12, 3.13, 3.14.

title: Perf: memoize token counts and skip unchanged metadata commits
body:
## Summary
- Add an LRU cache to `count_tokens`, keyed on the string; non-string/unhashable inputs (e.g. `tool_call` arguments passed as a dict) are counted uncached to preserve the existing tolerance, and strings over 32KB bypass the cache to bound its memory.
- Make the char-based token fallback (used when `tiktoken` is absent) non-ASCII-aware so CJK/other dense scripts are not undercounted ~3-4x.
- Read-before-write the generated-ignored placeholder count/ordinal metadata: skip the UPSERT (and its fsync commit under `synchronous=FULL`) when the stored value already matches.

## Why
- Assembly and preflight re-count the same message content many times per turn, and the assembler re-measures candidates while packing to budget (~O(n^2) on tool-heavy transcripts); the encoder is decided once per process, so a content-keyed cache is stable and behavior-preserving.
- An undercounted CJK context makes preflight under-trigger and assembly overflow the real budget.
- The placeholder metadata was UPSERT+committed unconditionally on every ingest, i.e. up to two fsync commits per turn even when nothing changed.

## Validation
- CI green after fix commit `bb0e016` across workflow-lint and Python 3.11-3.14 matrix

title: Serialize lifecycle/DAG writes and keep the frontier monotonic
body:
## Summary
- Add a reentrant lock and a `@_synchronized` decorator over the lifecycle store's read-modify-write methods (`bind_session`, `finalize_session`, `record_rollover`, `record_debt`, `record_maintenance_attempt`, `record_reset`, `prune_empty_sessions`).
- `advance_frontier` computes the new value with SQL `MAX(current_frontier_store_id, ?)` so it stays monotonic even against a stale read.
- `SummaryDAG.delete_below_depth` / `delete_session_nodes` / `reassign_session_nodes` now take `_db_lock` like the other DAG mutators.

## Why
- The lifecycle connection is opened `check_same_thread=False` in autocommit mode and shared across the gateway thread, dispatcher, and sub-agents, but its read-modify-write methods held no lock.
- Two callers advancing the checkpoint frontier could interleave (T1 reads 10 -> writes 15 while T2 reads 10 -> writes 12), regressing the frontier and forcing the same raw range to be compacted again (duplicate summary nodes / GC passes).
- The three DAG mutators executed + committed on the shared connection without the lock the other mutators already hold.

## Validation

title: Harden ingest protection: ReDoS-safe redaction, wrapped base64, path containment
body:
## Summary
- Route only the `private_key` sensitive pattern (lazy `.*?` under DOTALL) through the optional `regex` engine with a match timeout, or a length bound when `regex` is absent; the other patterns are character-class-bounded and linear, so they always run via stdlib and never fail open.
- Detect and externalize line-wrapped base64 (MIME 76 / PEM 64 chars per line), and compute the base64 ratio over whitespace-stripped content so canonical CRLF line endings do not sink it below threshold.
- Warn (once) when a configured externalized-payload path escapes the `hermes_home` base and `LCM_HERMES_BASE_DIR` is unset; the strict raise still applies when the base is set.

## Why
- The `private_key` pattern rescans to end-of-string for every unmatched `BEGIN` header, so a multi-MB payload with many headers and no `END` blocked ingest for seconds-to-minutes; restricting fail-open to that one pattern avoids a silent secret-redaction bypass on the linear patterns under load.
- Line-wrapped base64 never forms a single 4096-char contiguous run, so it slipped past the externalizer and landed inline in SQLite/FTS/WAL/backups; CRLF (the canonical MIME case) additionally failed the ratio gate.
- Default deployments had no path containment at all; a warning surfaces an escaped path without breaking legitimate custom volumes.

## Validation

title: Add a summary spend guard and a schema-too-new open guard
body:
## Summary
- Add `SummarySpendGuard`: a per-scope sliding-window rate limit with backoff for summarizer calls. When the budget is exhausted, escalation falls back to deterministic L3 truncation; the guard is checked per-route so a mid-chain trip stops the remaining fallbacks.
- The guard is deliberately NOT cleared on the automatic `force_overflow` path, and is wired into both the leaf and condensation summarization call sites. Config via optional `getattr` fields; `summary_spend_max_calls=0` disables it.
- Add `SchemaVersionTooNewError`: `run_versioned_migrations` refuses to open a database whose stored `schema_version` exceeds this build's `SCHEMA_VERSION`.

## Why
- The existing circuit breaker reacts only to summarizer failures; a pathologically looping compaction that keeps succeeding can burn auxiliary-model spend without bound. `force_overflow` is the sustained-over-cap state such a loop produces, so clearing the guard there would defeat it; a tripped guard still converges the emergency via L3 (no spend).
- Opening a v-newer database with older code and silently migrating/degrading it risks corrupting data written under semantics this build does not understand; refusing is safer than degrading after a downgrade/rollback.

## Validation

title: Reuse precomputed stored-row identities in the store-id map
body:
## Summary
- In `_get_store_id_map_for_messages`, capture each candidate's `_message_replay_identity(stored_row=True)` and its cleanup-identity variant once (both are already computed for the identity counts) and reuse them in the match-probe loops instead of recomputing per probe.
- Keep raw-placeholder identities lazy (memoized on demand), so histories with few/no placeholder-ref messages pay nothing extra.

## Why
- The store-id map aligns active messages to `store_id`s by scanning candidates and comparing replay identities. The probe loops recomputed `_message_replay_identity(stored_row=True)` for every `(message, probe)` pair — `O(candidates^2)` recomputes per call.
- That identity call reads the externalized payload file from disk for any stored row that carries one, so on tool-output-heavy histories the recomputation is `O(candidates^2)` disk reads. Reusing the already-computed values removes both.
- The change is behavior-preserving: identical identity values, computed once instead of repeatedly.

title: docs: spike async compaction atomic publish
body:
## Summary
- Add a design spike for opt-in async/background LCM compaction with atomic publish.
- Define the two-phase lifecycle: prepare non-canonical summaries in the background, then validate/promote a complete batch atomically from foreground compaction.
- Add strict-xfailed RED tests for the intended contract: default-off behavior, pending invisibility, stale/config/model rejection, race safety, restart safety, backoff behavior, rollback, and status/doctor visibility.

## Why
Foreground LCM compaction currently does the expensive summarization work on the turn-critical path. That keeps active context stable and cache-friendly, but it can add latency when the summarizer is slow or when leaf chains grow.

The goal here is not a casual refactor or “background thread writes canonical summaries.” The safe shape is a two-phase model: prepare old stable chunks in the background, keep them non-canonical and invisible, then atomically validate/promote a complete batch only when foreground compaction would have run anyway.

This is also meant to capture the guardrails from Lossless Claw:
- #807: background-prepared summaries are useful only if they stay ignored until a publish boundary
- #942: live config must beat stale persisted thresholds/debt
- #902: summary failure/backoff must not permanently wedge foreground recovery

## Scope
- Add a design doc for opt-in async/background LCM compaction with atomic publish.
- Link the design from `docs/architecture.md`.
- Add strict-xfailed RED spike tests that define the intended contract before implementation.

This PR intentionally does **not** implement the production worker, schema, promotion path, or runtime behavior yet.

## Agreed contract
- Default behavior stays unchanged.
- Feature is behind explicit flags.
- Pending/prepared summaries are ignored by active context, search/grep, describe/expand, transcript GC, and normal doctor integrity checks until promoted.
- Promotion must be atomic: canonical node inserts, lifecycle frontier updates, batch state changes, and superseding older batches share one SQLite transaction boundary.
- Promotion validates source IDs/source identity, lifecycle frontier, live config/policy fingerprint, summary route/model fingerprint, and complete source coverage.
- Live config wins over stale persisted batch metadata, including threshold/preflight policy changes.
- Foreground compaction racing background prep is safe: no double-compaction or mixed generations.
- Restart with pending/preparing/ready work resumes or discards safely without making pending rows canonical.
- Summary failure/backoff is visible but cannot block normal foreground compaction recovery.
- Status/doctor expose async counts such as pending/prepared/promoted/rejected/failed/superseded batches and pending summaries.

## Tests added
The new spike tests are intentionally strict-xfailed until the async compaction API/schema exists:
- default-disabled async compaction is inert
- pending summaries are invisible until atomic promotion
- stale source identity rejects without canonical mutation
- live config/policy changes reject stale prepared batches
- summary route/model changes reject stale prepared batches
- foreground compaction race rejects/supersedes pending work
- background summary failure/backoff does not wedge foreground compaction
- restart recovers/discards pending work safely
- successful atomic promotion commits canonical nodes/frontier/batch state together
- injected partial-publish failure rolls back without half-state
- status/doctor report async compaction counts

## Validation
- `python -m pytest tests/test_async_background_compaction_design.py -q -o addopts=` → `12 xfailed`
- `python -m pytest tests/test_lcm_core.py tests/test_lcm_engine.py tests/test_packaging_install.py -q -o addopts=` → `803 passed`

title: fix: recover persisted Hermes tool outputs losslessly
body:
## Summary
- recover Hermes `<persisted-output>` tool results from safe temp backing files before ingest storage
- externalize recovered results durably, redact sensitive content first, and keep unrecoverable/truncated markers visible inline
- make replay reconciliation treat recovered/externalized persisted-output tool rows as stable after temp cleanup
- add regression coverage for unsafe paths, nested/symlinked result dirs, symlinked temp roots, FIFO/special-file targets, literal tag collisions, embedded marker blocks, retried tool-call replay identity, current-marker replay recovery, stale retry marker proof, redacted preview recovery, distinct temp-path metadata, overwritten temp-file preview mismatch, inline-stored markers, CRLF content, externalization-disabled behavior, existing refs, and drill-down outputs

## Why
Hermes can spill oversized tool results to temporary host files and leave only a `<persisted-output>` marker in the conversation. If LCM ingests only that marker, later retrieval can preserve a lossy preview while the full result was actually recoverable at ingest time.

This keeps LCM’s lossless contract honest:
- recover full tool output only when the host backing file is safe and still available
- store recovered content durably so temp-file cleanup does not create replay duplicates
- preserve unrecoverable truncation markers visibly instead of hiding them behind recoverable-looking refs
- keep drill-down output usable instead of adding another opaque externalization hop

## Validation

- Codex xhigh focused diff review for raw-marker recovery before redaction and distinct-path metadata preservation → no blockers found
- Codex xhigh focused diff review for redaction-config-change replay identity and durable preview metadata safety → no blockers found

## Notes
- Updated after Codex flagged macOS-style symlinked temp roots: path validation now canonicalizes to the safe temp `hermes-results` parent, then reads via that canonical parent plus basename while still rejecting symlinked result dirs and symlinked targets.
- Updated after Codex flagged special-file and literal-tag edge cases: recovery now rejects non-regular files before opening and uses nonblocking open defensively; the inline-marker bypass now requires a standalone Hermes persisted-output marker shape, not just a literal tag substring.
- Updated after Codex flagged replay identity: replay substitution now uses full persisted-output marker validation, recovers the current marker backing file before falling back to durable payloads, and does not drop retried tool calls with ordinary or embedded marker text.
- Durable replay fallback now requires marker-specific metadata captured before redaction: the marker’s saved path and advertised char count must match the durable payload metadata for the reused `tool_call_id`.
- Live temp-file recovery now verifies the recovered content starts with the marker preview prefix before accepting same-length backing files, protecting against temp path reuse/overwrite.
- Recovery uses the raw persisted-output marker before sensitive redaction can alter preview text, while the recovered payload is still redacted before durable storage.
- Payload dedupe is skipped when marker metadata is supplied, so identical recovered content from different temp paths keeps path-specific replay proof.
- Durable replay fallback is checked before live temp-file recovery for incoming persisted markers, but only when path, advertised length, and raw marker preview-prefix metadata match. That keeps redaction-config changes from duplicating replayed rows while preserving stale/overwritten temp-file safety.
- Inline-stored markers are compared safely because replay identity attempts the same safe backing-file recovery for stored and incoming markers; if the temp file is gone and no proven durable payload exists, the marker text remains the identity.

title: fix: bound ignored session context fallback
body:
## Summary
- Bound ignored/stateless/thread-context-stateless sessions with host/native fallback compaction instead of letting them grow unbounded.
- Kept bypassed sessions out of LCM raw-message/DAG storage, including compression-boundary rollover, missing-platform boundary children, reused session-id, and late session-end edge cases.
- Added bypass-lineage, native fallback reset/isolation, tool-pair sanitization, redaction/externalized-prefix-safe session-end handling, deterministic trim regressions, and native fallback failure handling.
- Hardened same-id/off-current session-end prefix handling for tied normal/bypass prefixes, first-flush reused normal sessions, preflight/compress-only bypass evidence, ignored late suffixes, and tool-call identity.
- Documented ignored/stateless storage ownership vs host context-window protection.

## Why
- Ignored/stateless sessions should remain outside LCM storage, but they must not bypass all context-window protection.
- Compression-boundary children of bypassed sessions must inherit bypass lineage even when the host omits platform metadata.
- Reused session IDs and late `on_session_end()` callbacks can otherwise either leak bypass content into normal LCM storage or drop valid normal final messages.
- Native fallback errors should fail closed into deterministic trim, not leave bypassed transcripts unbounded.

title: fix: use auxiliary usage for bypass checks
body:
## Summary
- Tracks prompt-token usage for active auxiliary/thread-stateless sessions without mutating foreground session counters.
- Lets bypass-mode `should_compress()` and `compress()` use active auxiliary token totals when callers do not pass explicit prompt-token counts.
- Leaves auxiliary `compress()` token counts unknown when no usage has been recorded yet, so native host fallback compressors do not see a false zero for oversized first-turn payloads.
- Clears stale auxiliary usage while preserving the right guard state when compression handoff adopts a continuation ID that was previously used by another auxiliary generation.
- Retires previous in-process auxiliary generations for reused continuation IDs so stale old frames with the same parent cannot end or update the newly active continuation.
- Preserves foreground-reuse suppression when stale auxiliary handoff callbacks arrive after an auxiliary ID has been reused as a real foreground session.
- Allows direct host session-end callbacks to clear the current active generated auxiliary generation with cached usage, while guarded/reused ambiguous generations still reject direct no-frame ends.
- Uses expected handoff parent identity plus retired-generation checks so stale old frames cannot end or update a reused continuation, while the real continuation can still report usage and clean up.
- Preserves auxiliary lineage for stale old-frame detection while preventing reused foreground IDs from poisoning later normal children, off-current session ends, or compression boundaries.

## Why
- Follow-up to #310 after Codex found that oversized in-process auxiliary sessions could still miss host-fallback compaction when callers relied on no-argument compression APIs.
- Those sessions are intentionally excluded from LCM storage, but they still need host/native context bounding.
- Public and local review also found adjacent stale auxiliary token/lineage paths around session-end cleanup, same-ID reuse, handoff, off-current callbacks, and native fallback token propagation; this update closes those cases before final review.

## Validation
- `python -m pytest tests/test_lcm_engine.py::TestSessionRollover::test_stateless_auxiliary_rebind_preserves_parent_lineage tests/test_lcm_engine.py::TestSessionRollover::test_stale_auxiliary_boundary_preserves_off_current_reused_normal_suffix tests/test_lcm_engine.py::TestSessionRollover::test_clean_generated_continuation_reuse_does_not_guard_direct_end tests/test_lcm_engine.py::TestSessionRollover::test_guarded_auxiliary_reuse_does_not_poison_later_foreground_children -q -o addopts= --tb=short` → `4 passed`
- `git diff --check && python -m py_compile engine.py tests/test_lcm_engine.py` → clean
- `python -m pytest tests/test_lcm_engine.py tests/test_lcm_core.py -q -k "thread_context_stateless or auxiliary or bypass or stateless or ignored or host_fallback or native_fallback or session_end or compression_boundary or reused" -o addopts=` → `238 passed, 686 deselected`
- `python -m pytest -q -o addopts=` → `1422 passed, 12 xfailed`
- `scripts/validate_release.sh --full --keep-going --output /tmp/hermes-lcm-release-validation-pr312-local-full16-20260705154608` → `PASS: release validation full`
- Local Codex CLI full review on head `33896436b5dd76d1ec8112e8249b453a08e21cf6` after the final dirty-diff patch → `No discrete correctness issues were found in the changes. The full test suite passes locally.`

## Risk / impact
- Medium-low, focused on process-local token accounting and lifecycle classification for active auxiliary/thread-stateless bypass checks.
- Does not add LCM storage for auxiliary sessions.
- Does not change explicit `should_compress(prompt_tokens=...)` behavior.
- Avoids foreground token bleed into fresh auxiliary sessions without affecting non-aux ignored/stateless fallback decisions.
- Preserves stale-frame protection for auxiliary lineage while suppressing reused foreground IDs as parent/ancestor evidence for normal children and boundaries, even after stale handoff callbacks.
- Avoids forwarding a false `current_tokens=0` to native fallback compressors when an auxiliary frame has not sampled usage yet.
- Avoids carrying stale usage while still guarding reused continuation IDs against stale generated end/update callbacks.
- Allows a real handed-off continuation to report usage and end cleanly after same-parent stale frames are rejected.
- Avoids stale generation adoption from late usage callbacks after an auxiliary session has ended or after its previous in-process generation has been retired by handoff reuse.

## Scope boundaries
- This only lands the auxiliary no-arg compression and lifecycle follow-up that missed the #310 merge window.
- It does not reopen the broader ignored/stateless fallback design from #310.

## Rollout / operator notes
- No migration, config, or operator action required.
- Existing ignored/stateless session behavior remains unchanged except for no-arg auxiliary compression decisions and safer auxiliary lifecycle cleanup.

## Reviewer focus
- Confirm auxiliary prompt-token state cannot leak into foreground `last_prompt_tokens` decisions.
- Confirm bypass sessions still do not write raw messages or DAG nodes while retaining context-bound checks.
- Confirm native fallback compressors receive positive auxiliary usage when available, but not a false zero before usage exists.
- Confirm handoff to a reused auxiliary continuation ID clears stale usage while preserving enough guard state to reject stale generated end/update callbacks.
- Confirm a real handed-off continuation can still clean itself up before usage when its parent identity matches the handoff source.
- Confirm late auxiliary usage callbacks, same-id reuse, foreground reuse, off-current session ends, and compression handoff do not reintroduce stale auxiliary state or poison normal foreground sessions.

title: Fix strict persisted-output replay identity
body:
## Summary
- Adds strict persisted-output replay identity for Hermes tool-output markers.
- Requires live-file/stat-backed proof before a recovered persisted-output marker can satisfy durable replay identity.
- Treats missing or unrecoverable raw persisted-output markers as append-worthy instead of replay-proof, even when path/preview/length or inline-looking metadata matches.
- Preserves safe file-generation metadata for recovered persisted-output payloads while avoiding raw content hashes and lossy preview digest leaks.
- Expands regression coverage for forged inline metadata, stale durable payloads, externalization-disabled fallback, legacy preview-prefix handling, and lossy redaction retries.

## Why
- Persisted-output markers are only trustworthy while the backing Hermes temp file can be safely recovered and matched.
- Inline marker text is untrusted preview content; treating it as proof after the file is gone can silently drop legitimate retried tool results.
- The safer replay contract is: dedupe only with real proof, otherwise append rather than lose data.

## Validation
- `python -m pytest tests/test_lcm_core.py::TestIngestExternalization -q -o addopts=` → `49 passed`
- `python -m pytest tests/test_lcm_core.py tests/test_lcm_engine.py tests/test_packaging_install.py -q -o addopts=` → `927 passed`
- `python -m pytest -q -o addopts=` → `1400 passed, 12 xfailed`
- `python -m compileall -q engine.py externalize.py ingest_protection.py tests/test_lcm_core.py && git diff --check origin/main...HEAD && git diff --check` → clean
- Static scan of `engine.py`, `externalize.py`, and `ingest_protection.py` for `persisted_output_content_sha256` / `content_sha256` → `STATIC_SCAN_CLEAN`
- Local Codex CLI review with `model_reasoning_effort="xhigh"` on the final branch diff → `No blockers found.`

## Risk / impact
- Replay behavior is intentionally stricter for persisted-output markers whose backing file is missing or unrecoverable: these markers append instead of deduping, to avoid silent data loss.
- This can create duplicates in ambiguous replay cases, but only where the branch cannot prove identity safely.
- Recovered persisted-output payload metadata now carries file generation fields (`size`, `mtime_ns`, `ctime_ns`) for non-content identity checks.
- No schema migration or config change is required.
- The implementation avoids raw full-content hashes and avoids preview-derived digests for lossy redaction cases.

## Scope boundaries
- Does not change Hermes host-side tool result persistence.
- Does not introduce provenance-signed inline trailers; inline marker text remains untrusted.
- Does not try to dedupe missing-file persisted-output markers without live-file proof.
- Does not change unrelated compaction, summarization, or tool APIs.

## Screenshots / before-after
- Not applicable (non-UI change).

## Rollout / operator notes
- No migration steps required.
- Existing externalized payloads remain compatible.
- Legacy preview-prefix metadata is still handled where safe, but lossy redaction cases avoid deriving replay identity from raw legacy preview text.
- Operators should expect safer append behavior for ambiguous missing-file persisted-output replays.

## Reviewer focus
- Please focus on the replay gates around persisted-output markers in `engine.py`.
- Check that missing/unrecoverable temp files cannot become replay-proof through forged inline marker identity/generation text.
- Check that live-file proof, file-generation metadata, redaction handling, and legacy preview-prefix compatibility stay aligned across `ingest_protection.py`, `externalize.py`, and the regression tests.

title: Move metadata JSON read/write onto MessageStore
body:
## Summary
- Add two `MessageStore` methods that own the metadata table's key/value JSON access:
  - `read_metadata_json(key)` -> JSON-decoded value, or `None` for a closed connection / missing / empty row. Decoding is intentionally left unwrapped so a malformed value still raises.
  - `write_metadata_json(keys, serialized, *, skip_unchanged=False)` -> UPSERT the pre-serialized payload to each key under the write lock with a single commit; `skip_unchanged=True` keeps the hot-path "skip write+commit when unchanged" optimization.
- Route all eight engine metadata helpers (`_load_hash_list_for_metadata_keys`, `_remember_hash_for_metadata_keys`, and the placeholder count/ordinal + dependent-reply load/write pairs) through them.

## Why
- Those eight helpers each re-implemented the same SQLite boilerplate: fetch `self._store._conn`, guard it, `SELECT value FROM metadata`, `json.loads`; and on writes acquire `self._store._write_lock`, UPSERT per key, commit (with the count/ordinal writers additionally skipping the write when unchanged, per #299).
- That duplicated ~110 lines and reached into the store's **private** connection and lock from the engine. Consolidating the boilerplate on `MessageStore` removes the duplication and the layering violation — the engine no longer touches `self._store._conn` / `self._store._write_lock` at all.

## Validation
- [x] Focused validation:
  - [x] Direct helper behaviour checks (roundtrip; `skip_unchanged` False->wrote / True->no-op; missing key -> `None`; empty value -> `None`; malformed JSON propagates) -> all pass
  - [x] `PYTHONPATH="<stub>:." python3 -m pytest tests -q -k "metadata or placeholder or ignored or dependent or ordinal"` -> `182 passed`
- [x] Default validation:
  - [x] `PYTHONPATH="<stub>:." python3 -m pytest tests -q` -> `1385 passed, 12 xfailed` (identical to pre-change)
  - [x] `python3 -m compileall -q .`
  - [x] `python3 -m py_compile scripts/import_lossless_claw.py`
  - [x] `bash -n scripts/install.sh scripts/update.sh`
  - [x] `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` -> clean
- [x] Workflow validation: not applicable; no workflows changed.
- [x] Added-line private/secret hygiene scan -> `0` hits.

## Notes
- Behaviour-preserving: signatures, return values, per-caller error scoping, and the unchanged-skip commit semantics are all unchanged. `read_metadata_json` deliberately does not swallow `json` errors so each loader keeps its historical abort-vs-skip behaviour (the hash-list loader discards a partial result on error; the count/ordinal loaders keep what they accumulated).
- Validation used a minimal local `agent.context_engine` stub because this plugin repository is tested standalone outside the Hermes host package.
- Net `engine.py` is 111 lines lighter; `store.py` gains the two documented helpers.

title: Add compaction telemetry (per-conversation snapshot)
body:
## Summary
- Persist a lightweight **per-conversation compaction-telemetry** record and surface it under `get_status()["compaction_telemetry"]`.
- Stored as a single JSON row in the **existing metadata table** — no new table, no `SCHEMA_VERSION` bump, no client lockout.
- Recorded once per turn (in `update_from_response`): last prompt / cache-read / cache-write tokens; `cache_state` (hot|cold|unknown) + consecutive-cold streak; `turns_since_leaf_compaction`; `peak_prompt_tokens_since_leaf_compaction`; `total_compactions`; `last_leaf_compaction_at`; `last_compaction_duration_ms`; provider/model; `last_api_call_at`; `activity_band` (reserved, carried forward as `"low"`).
- `compress()` logs the leaf-compaction wall-clock at INFO (log-only; durations/queue-wait are not persisted).
- New `MessageStore.read_compaction_telemetry` / `write_compaction_telemetry` keep the engine out of the store's private connection/lock.

## Why
- Operators currently have no persisted view of cache behaviour or compaction cadence. This adds one cheaply and additively.
- Modelled on the TS reference (`compaction-telemetry` in `martian-engineering/lossless-claw`), but deliberately scoped down: the reference uses a dedicated table + migration; here a single metadata JSON row avoids a schema-version bump entirely.
- The since-compaction accumulators reset off the monotonic `compression_count` (which also drops to 0 on a session reset) rather than instrumenting the `compress()` hot path — one comparison in the per-turn recorder, no invasive pipeline change.

## Validation
- [x] Focused validation:
  - [x] `PYTHONPATH="<stub>:." python3 -m pytest tests/test_compaction_telemetry.py -q` -> `8 passed` (per-turn snapshot, turns/peak accumulation, cold streak + hot reset, idle-turn skip, reset-on-compaction, no-conversation no-op, unknown state, store roundtrip + skip-unchanged)

  - [x] `python3 -m compileall -q .`
  - [x] `python3 -m py_compile scripts/import_lossless_claw.py`
  - [x] `bash -n scripts/install.sh scripts/update.sh`
  - [x] `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` -> clean
- [x] Workflow validation: not applicable; no workflows changed.
- [x] Added-line private/secret hygiene scan -> `0` hits.

## Notes
- Best-effort and non-blocking by design: turns with no token/cache signal are skipped so idle turns never churn the row; the write is skipped when the serialized payload is unchanged; every read/write is guarded so telemetry can never break a turn. Missing cache signals degrade to `cache_state="unknown"` with the cold streak carried.
- `activity_band` is a reserved carry-forward field (matches the reference, which has no live `medium`/`high` computation yet).
- Purely additive (+313 lines, no deletions). The two new store methods are purpose-named and independent of the generic `read_metadata_json`/`write_metadata_json` helpers proposed in a separate PR; they can be unified later if that lands.

title: feat: improve current-session recovery during long mid-turn tool loops
body:
## Problem

LCM currently persists ordinary conversation history primarily at completed-turn boundaries (`post_llm_call`) and during existing explicit ingest paths such as preflight/compression, LCM tool dispatch with live `messages`, and session-end flush.

That is usually fine, but it leaves a visibility/recovery gap during long tool-calling turns, especially immediately after a compression boundary that rotates into a new child session.

Observed shape:

1. A parent session compresses and rotates to a child session.
2. LCM correctly carries a summary node into the child session, with source ids pointing back to the parent raw rows.
3. The agent continues inside the same long tool-calling turn.
4. The host session DB accumulates many child-session assistant/tool intermediate rows.
5. LCM `messages` can still have `0` raw rows for the child until the turn produces a final assistant response and `post_llm_call` fires.

This is not a lifecycle/carry-over bug: the summary node and lifecycle state are correct. The gap is specifically that mid-turn assistant/tool rows are not yet visible in LCM raw search/recovery.

## User or operator impact

For long-running debugging / RE / sysadmin turns with many tool calls, the operator may ask “what did the tool output just say?” or need current-session recovery while the turn is still in progress. During that window:

- `lcm_grep session_scope=session` for the new child session may not find post-compression intermediate messages, because the child has no raw LCM rows yet.
- The same messages may already exist in the host session DB, so there is an inconsistent recovery story: host history can see them, LCM cannot.
- If the process crashes before the final assistant response, the host DB may retain intermediate rows while LCM raw storage/retrieval for the child remains incomplete.
- This is most visible after compression rotation because the child session can contain a carried-over summary node but no child raw rows yet.

Severity: enhancement / reliability improvement, not data-loss proof. In the observed case, the state DB retained the intermediate rows and LCM carry-over worked.

## Proposed direction

Please choose the right architecture; this issue is meant to provide evidence and constraints rather than prescribe one implementation.

Possible directions:

1. Add a bounded mid-turn ingest hook for assistant/tool messages.
   - For example, after tool-call batches or after each tool result append.
   - Must preserve message sequence integrity and avoid duplicate rows.

2. Add a host/session-DB fallback for current-session recovery when LCM raw rows lag during an active turn.
   - LCM tools could optionally consult host active rows for the current session when the engine detects a mid-turn gap.
   - This may be safer than writing incomplete tool-call sequences into LCM immediately, but it couples LCM retrieval to host session storage.

3. Add a diagnostic/status surface only.
   - Detect and report “mid-turn raw ingest pending” so operators understand why current child raw count is zero.
   - Lower risk, but does not improve recovery/search.

4. Add an opt-in configuration.
   - Example shape: `LCM_MID_TURN_INGEST=off|tool_batch|tool_result` or similar.
   - Default can remain current behavior if mid-turn persistence has sequence/performance risks.

## Alternatives and tradeoffs

- Keep current completed-turn-only behavior:
  - Simple and avoids duplicate/corrupt partial sequences.
  - But LCM current-session recall lags behind host state during long tool-heavy turns.

- Ingest after every tool result:
  - Best crash/recovery freshness.
  - Higher SQLite write frequency and higher duplicate/cursor complexity.

- Ingest only after a tool-call batch completes:
  - Good compromise for long tool loops.
  - Still needs careful cursor/reconciliation handling with existing `_ingest_messages` semantics.

- Query host session DB as fallback:
  - Avoids mid-turn LCM writes.
  - Retrieval semantics become split-brain unless clearly surfaced as fallback evidence.

## Backward compatibility

Suggested default: keep current behavior unless maintainers are confident mid-turn ingest is safe.

If implemented as opt-in, existing users see no behavior change. If implemented by default, it should preserve:

- no duplicate rows across `post_llm_call`, compression/preflight ingest, and LCM tool-call ingest;
- valid assistant/tool-call sequencing;
- existing ignore/redaction/externalization behavior;
- bounded write volume for tool-heavy sessions.

## Validation or evidence

Observed after a compression rotation:

- Parent session compressed successfully.
- Child session had a carried-over LCM summary node.
- Child session had `0` LCM raw message rows during the active tool-calling turn.
- Host session DB already had many child rows:
  - one child user row;
  - all child assistant rows had `finish_reason = tool_calls`;
  - no final assistant response existed yet.

That supports “expected mid-turn gap” rather than `post_llm_call` failure.

Concrete observed counts from one rotated-child case:

```text
child LCM summary_nodes: 1
child LCM messages: 0
child state DB messages: 188
child state DB role counts: assistant=94, tool=93, user=1
child assistant finish_reason counts: tool_calls=94, final/non-tool-call=0
```

Relevant current code paths:

- `__init__.py`: plugin registers `post_llm_call` hook for per-turn ingest.
- `engine.py`: `LCMEngine.ingest()` calls `_ingest_messages()` when invoked.
- `engine.py`: LCM tool dispatch can ingest live `messages` before handling a tool call.
- Hermes host `turn_finalizer.py`: `post_llm_call` fires only when `final_response and not interrupted`.

Cross-check from another active session with in-place compression:

- Same-session compression created an LCM DAG node and later raw rows continued to ingest normally after completed turns.
- LCM had 401 raw messages with timestamps after the summary node’s `created_at`.
- This suggests ordinary post-turn ingest is working; the issue is the active mid-turn window, not a general failure to ingest after compression.

## Implementation status

Design sketched

## Additional notes

This is related to operator experience around current-session recall after compression. It should not block lifecycle/carry-over fixes: in the observed rotation case, carry-over itself was correct and there was no `skipped carry-over` warning.

title: Encapsulate MessageStore connection behind a public accessor
body:
## Summary
- Add a public `MessageStore.connection` property (read-oriented) plus `MessageStore.commit()` and `MessageStore.backup(dest)`.
- Route every remaining `engine._store._conn` reach-in in `command.py` and `tools.py` through the new public surface.
- Finishes the WS5 encapsulation started in #316 (metadata JSON read/write) for the store's raw connection.

## Why
After #316 moved the metadata JSON read/write onto `MessageStore`, the `/lcm`
command handlers and the inspect/doctor tools were the last callers still
poking the store's private `_conn`: ad-hoc diagnostic reads (integrity /
quick / journal-mode PRAGMAs, FTS sync counts, schema health, payload-risk
scans, inspect totals) and the backup path's flush + snapshot. That coupled
diagnostics and the CLI to the store's private field and its name. Giving the
store a documented public seam removes that coupling and keeps the None/closed
handling in one supported place, mirroring the already-public `db_path`.

## Validation
- `ruff check store.py command.py tools.py` → All checks passed
- `python -m pytest -q -o addopts=` (full suite) → 1545 passed, 12 xfailed
- `python -m pytest tests/test_lcm_command.py tests/test_lcm_inspect.py tests/test_tool_contracts.py tests/test_lcm_core.py -q -o addopts=` → 385 passed
- `scripts/validate_release.sh --full --keep-going --output <dir>` → PASS

## Notes
- Behaviour-preserving: `connection` returns the same object callers used
  before, so their existing `if conn is None` guards are unchanged; `commit`
  and `backup` are thin wrappers that keep the live-connection requirement (a
  closed store still raises, matching direct `_conn.commit()` / `_conn.backup()`
  use).
- Scope is deliberately the `MessageStore` connection only. The `_dag` and
  `_lifecycle` connections are separate classes with their own `_conn`; the
  backup flush in `_flush_engine_connections` still commits those directly.
- Trade-off, stated plainly: `connection` is a *read* seam for diagnostics, not
  full method-level encapsulation, so it does technically expose a handle a
  caller could write through outside `_write_lock`. That is enforced by
  convention (docstring) rather than the type system. It is not a new capability
  — callers already reached the same `_conn` directly — and writes in-tree still
  go through the store's locked methods. Happy to add per-check read methods
  instead if you'd prefer the connection stay private.
- `engine.py`'s two `_store._append_protected_batch(...)` calls are a private
  *method* on the append path, a different encapsulation question, and are left
  as-is.
- The one hand-rolled `FakeStore` test double gains a `connection` property to
  mirror the real store's public API; other tests set/read the real store's
  `_conn` field directly, which the property returns unchanged.

## Refs
- Follows #316 (metadata JSON on MessageStore); same WS5 encapsulation line.

title: Drive scalar env config from a declarative field spec (WS5.6)
body:
## Summary
- Introduce a declarative `ENV_FIELD_SPECS` registry `(name, env_key, py_type)` in `config.py` for the scalar `LCM_*` env overrides.
- Replace the ~35 repetitive per-field assignments in `LCMConfig.from_env` with one uniform loop over the registry.
- Let `presets.py` derive its preset-field env/parse lookups from the same registry instead of two hand-maintained parallel dicts.

## Why
WS5.6 of the WS5 workstream. `from_env` was ~160 lines of
`c.X = _int/_float/_bool/_str("LCM_X", c.X)` boilerplate, and `presets.py`
kept a second copy of the field→env and field→type mapping (`_FIELD_ENV` /
`_FIELD_PARSERS`). This gives one source of truth for the scalar env overrides,
consumed by both config parsing and preset dry-run.

## Validation
- `ruff check config.py presets.py` → All checks passed
- **Equivalence harness** (byte-identical proof): snapshots `from_env()` — full
  `asdict` + `config_sources` + `config_source_warnings` — plus preset override
  discovery across **600 scenarios** (every `LCM_*` key absent / valid /
  invalid). Result: **0 differing scenarios**, preset maps identical.
- `python -m pytest -q -o addopts=` (full suite) → 1545 passed, 12 xfailed
- `scripts/validate_release.sh --full --keep-going --output <dir>` → PASS

## Notes
- Behaviour-preserving. Source-tracked fields (provenance recording and/or a
  computed default: `fresh_tail_count`, `leaf_chunk_tokens`, `context_threshold`,
  the `summary_spend_*` and `summary_timeout_ms` fields, codex autoraise) stay
  explicit and are skipped by the loop via `_SOURCE_TRACKED_ENV_FIELDS`.
  Pattern-list overrides (with their `_source` sidecar) and the inline
  `gc_max_age_hours` float parse also stay explicit.
- `presets.py` still owns *which* fields are preset-overridable (`_PRESET_FIELDS`,
  unchanged set of 5) and only sources the env var + parse type from the shared
  spec — so `explicit_operator_overrides` / `invalid_operator_overrides` keep
  scanning exactly those 5 fields, not the whole registry.
- No import cycle: `presets` imports `config`; `config` imports neither.
- Independent of #322/#323/#324/#325 (touches only `config.py` + `presets.py`).

## Refs
- Design: WS5 engine decomposition, companion workstream WS5.6 (declarative config).

WS5 engine decomposition. `engine.py` is ~9k lines; detecting SQLite lock-contention error chains and temporarily bounding `busy_timeout` on gateway-critical paths are a cohesive, pure SQLite concern with no engine state. title: Extract active-engine registry into engine_registry.py (WS5 seam)
body:
## Summary
- Move the process-wide active-LCM-clone registry out of `engine.py` into a new `engine_registry.py`: the registry `RLock`, the two `WeakValueDictionary` registries (by session id / conversation id), the resolver/matcher helpers, the removal helper, and the public `resolve_active_lcm_engine`.
- `engine.py` imports the shared lock, the two registries, `_remove_registry_entries_for_engine`, and `resolve_active_lcm_engine`. The matcher helpers (`_is_usable_lcm_engine`, `_engine_matches_session_binding`, `_engine_matches_conversation_binding`) stay internal to the module.

## Why
WS5 engine decomposition. `engine.py` is ~9k lines; the process-wide registry that lets post-turn ingest follow the active per-agent LCM clone (instead of the plugin singleton) is a cohesive concern with its own lock and weak maps. Isolating it shrinks the monolith with no behaviour change, alongside the earlier `sanitize.py` / `maintenance.py` / `codex_routing.py` / `sqlite_util.py` / `runtime_identity.py` / `message_analysis.py` splits.

## Validation
- `ruff check engine_registry.py engine.py` → All checks passed
- **Equivalence harness**: reconstructs the five helpers from `git show main:engine.py` (AST slice) and proves (1) the moved source is **byte-identical** (5/5 functions), and (2) behavioural parity old-vs-new by driving two independent registries through an 18-step register/resolve/remove sequence (session/conversation collisions, non-usable engines, missing-ingest engines, session-id reuse across engines) and comparing both the resolved engine and the full registry key→engine structure at every step. Result: **0 differing**.
- `python -m pytest -q -o addopts=` (full suite) → **1570 passed, 12 xfailed**
- `scripts/validate_release.sh --full --keep-going --output <dir>` → **PASS**

## Notes
- Behaviour-preserving; the moved code is byte-identical to its pre-move form.
- The `LCMEngine` binding methods (`_register_active_engine_binding` / `_unregister_active_engine_binding`) keep their bodies verbatim: the lock and the two registries are shared mutable objects, so mutating them through the imported names (`_ACTIVE_ENGINES_BY_SESSION_ID[sid] = self`, `with _ACTIVE_ENGINE_REGISTRY_LOCK:`) hits the same objects the resolver reads.
- `resolve_active_lcm_engine` is re-exported from `engine.py` (`# noqa: F401`) so any host importing it from `hermes_lcm.engine` keeps working; it is also importable from `hermes_lcm.engine_registry`.
- No import cycle: `engine_registry` imports only the stdlib; `engine` imports `engine_registry`.
- Independent of the other WS5 seams (touches only `engine.py` + the new module).

## Refs
- Design: WS5 engine decomposition, companion to the earlier seams (#323–#331).

title: Extract placeholder-ledger bookkeeping into a mixin (WS5 Seam 1)
body:
## Summary
- Move the 35 ignored-active-replay placeholder / dependent-reply bookkeeping methods out of `LCMEngine` into a `PlaceholderLedgerMixin` in the new `placeholder_ledger.py`, and mix it in: `class LCMEngine(PlaceholderLedgerMixin, ContextEngine)`.
- The methods are relocated **verbatim** and keep running bound to the engine instance, so nothing else changes: no call sites, no tests.

## Why
WS5 engine decomposition, Seam 1. `engine.py` was ~9k lines. The placeholder ledger — session-scoped metadata-key builders, generated-placeholder hash/count/ordinal load+persist, active-replay digest budgets, dependent-reply fingerprints/records, and `_apply_ignored_active_replay_placeholders` — is a large, cohesive concern (~660 lines). A mixin lifts it into its own file while preserving `self` semantics: because `self` is still the `LCMEngine`, the methods read/write the engine's shared runtime state and call engine helpers through normal MRO attribute lookup.

## Validation
- `ruff check placeholder_ledger.py engine.py` → All checks passed
- **Byte-identity proof**: AST-slices all 35 methods from `git show main:engine.py` (in `LCMEngine`) and from the new `placeholder_ledger.py` (in `PlaceholderLedgerMixin`) and asserts the source text is identical → **35/35 byte-identical**, and **35/35 removed** from `engine.py`'s `LCMEngine`.
- Focused placeholder/ignored/dependent/digest/ordinal/hash tests → **105 passed**
- `python -m pytest -q -o addopts=` (full suite) → **1570 passed, 12 xfailed** (the ~130 white-box tests in `tests/test_lcm_engine.py` that call these private methods directly are unchanged and green)
- `scripts/validate_release.sh --full --keep-going --output <dir>` → **PASS**
- `engine.py`: 9048 → 8391 lines (−657)

## Notes
- Behaviour-preserving; method bodies are byte-identical to their pre-move form (only the module-local `logger` name changes, as in the earlier `runtime_identity.py` split).
- **State ownership is unchanged.** The two shared placeholder-id sets (`_generated_ignored_active_replay_placeholder_hashes` / `_message_ids`) and the per-turn `_current_compress_store_ids_by_message_id` cache stay owned/initialised by `LCMEngine` — they are also touched by sanitize/reconcile methods that remain on the engine — so the mixin is a pure relocation, not a state-ownership change. It accesses them, and callbacks (`_get_store_id_map_for_messages`, `_matches_ignore_message_patterns`, `_stable_tool_calls_identity`, `_message_replay_identity`, `_copy_active_replay_messages_preserving_generated_ids`), via `self`.
- No import cycle: `placeholder_ledger` imports only stdlib + `.message_content`; `engine` imports `placeholder_ledger`.
- MRO: `LCMEngine(ContextEngine, PlaceholderLedgerMixin)` — the moved names live only on the mixin (removed from `LCMEngine`), so they resolve there; no collisions with `ContextEngine`.

## Refs
- Design: WS5 engine decomposition, Seam 1. Companion to the earlier module seams (#323–#332).

title: Extract the leaf-compaction pipeline into a mixin (WS5 Seam 6)

## Why
WS5 engine decomposition, Seam 6. The compaction gate + leaf-selection pipeline is a large, cohesive concern (~750 lines). A mixin lifts it into its own file while preserving `self` semantics: `self` is still the `LCMEngine`, so `_ingest_cursor`, `_store`, `_dag`, `_lifecycle`, the per-turn caches and the ~60 sibling helpers stay on the engine and resolve via normal MRO attribute lookup.

## Validation
- `ruff check compaction.py engine.py` → All checks passed
- **Byte-identity proof**: AST-slices all 8 methods from `git show main:engine.py` (in `LCMEngine`) and from `compaction.py` (in `CompactionMixin`) → **8/8 byte-identical**, and **8/8 removed** from `engine.py`.
- Focused compaction tests (compress/leaf/compact/preflight/rescue/chunk) → **153 passed**
- `python -m pytest -q -o addopts=` (full suite) → **1570 passed, 12 xfailed**
- `scripts/validate_release.sh --full --keep-going --output <dir>` → **PASS**

## Notes
- Behaviour-preserving; method bodies are byte-identical to their pre-move form (only the module-local `logger` name changes).

- No import cycle: `compaction` imports stdlib + `.dag` / `.message_content` / `.sanitize` / `.tokens`; `engine` imports `compaction`.

title: Extract ingest-cursor reconciliation into a mixin (WS5 Seam 4)
body:
## Summary
- Move the ingest-cursor reconciliation machinery and the stable replay-identity primitives it relies on out of `LCMEngine` into a `ReconcileMixin` in the new `reconcile.py`, and mix it in: `class LCMEngine(ReconcileMixin, ContextEngine)`.
- 20 methods: tool-call/message replay-identity primitives, persisted-output durable-replay evidence helpers, and the reconciliation orchestration (`_find_reconciled_cursor_for_store_tail`, `_reconcile_ingest_cursor_from_store`, `_get_store_id_map_for_messages`, …).

## Why
WS5 engine decomposition, Seam 4. The post-restart reconciliation of the persisted store tail against the active message list — plus the replay-identity primitives that make it deterministic — is the single largest cohesive concern left in `engine.py` (~1.1k lines). A mixin lifts it into its own file while preserving `self` semantics: `_store`, `_session_id`, `_config` and the safety-critical `_ingest_cursor` stay on the engine and resolve via `self` (`_ingest_cursor` is still written by `_ingest_messages` from the reconciler's return value).

## Validation
- `ruff check reconcile.py engine.py` → All checks passed
- **Byte-identity proof**: AST-slices all 20 methods from `git show main:engine.py` vs `reconcile.py` → **18/20 byte-identical**; the two differing methods differ *only* by the deliberate class-qualifier rename below (verified: reversing `ReconcileMixin.` → `LCMEngine.` makes them identical). **20/20 removed** from `engine.py`.
- Focused reconcile/replay-identity/store-id-map/persisted-output tests → **63 passed**
- `python -m pytest -q -o addopts=` (full suite) → **1570 passed, 12 xfailed**
- `scripts/validate_release.sh --full --keep-going --output <dir>` → **PASS**
- `engine.py`: 9048 → 7943 lines (−1105)

## Notes
- Behaviour-preserving. Method bodies are byte-identical except two mechanical, behaviour-preserving adjustments needed to break an `engine` ↔ `reconcile` import cycle:
  - The two tool-call-identity **staticmethods** call the canonicalizer via the mixin class (`ReconcileMixin._canonicalize_tool_call_identity_value`) instead of `LCMEngine`. `LCMEngine` inherits the staticmethod from the mixin, so resolution is identical.
  - `_PRESERVED_OBJECTIVE_CONTEXT_PREFIX` moves to `reconcile.py` (used by the reconciliation scan) and is **re-imported into `engine.py`** for its other readers, so no code that reads it changes.
- Drops six now-exclusive `ingest_protection`/`externalize` imports from `engine.py` (moved to `reconcile.py`).
- No call sites and no tests change; the white-box tests that bind `_message_replay_identity` / `_get_store_id_map_for_messages` call them on an `LCMEngine` instance and resolve via the mixin.
- The reconcile methods are all private, so mixing after `ContextEngine` is fine (no protocol-name collision).

## Refs
- Design: WS5 engine decomposition, Seam 4. Companion to Seam 1 (#333), Seam 6 (#334), and the module seams (#328–#332).

title: Prefer the host's explicit subagent signal over the call-stack frame walk (WS5.7)
body:
## What this changes
LCM now identifies a subagent/auxiliary child session — and resolves its parent
session — from the **host's own explicit signal** when the host provides it,
instead of walking the call stack and reading private agent attributes. The old
mechanism stays as a fallback, so nothing regresses on hosts that don't emit the
signal.

## Why
When `on_session_start` fires for a session, LCM needs to know *is this a
subagent, and who is its parent?* to attribute lineage correctly (session
ownership, ignore/stateless handling). The `ContextEngine.on_session_start`
callback carries **no** subagent/parent argument, so until now LCM's only option
was `_in_process_parent_session_id` walking up ~32 `inspect.currentframe()`
frames and sniffing private attributes on the calling agent object
(`_subagent_id`, `_parent_subagent_id`, `_delegate_depth`, `log_prefix`,
`enabled_toolsets`, `_memory_write_context`, …).

That heuristic works but is fragile:
- it reads **undocumented host internals** — a host rename silently breaks
  detection (no error, just wrong lineage);
- it depends on stack shape (a 32-frame budget), so refactors on either side can
  move the target frame out of range.

The host already publishes the same information **explicitly and publicly**: the
plugin hook bus fires `subagent_start` / `subagent_stop` with
`child_session_id`, `parent_session_id`, `child_subagent_id`,
`parent_subagent_id`, and `child_role` when a delegate/subagent is spawned. (The
shipped `observability/nemo_relay` plugin already consumes these.) Using that
signal is both more robust and keeps LCM off the host's private surface.

## How
- **`aux_session.py`** — a small, process-wide, lock-guarded, memory-bounded
  registry `_SUBAGENT_LINEAGE_BY_SESSION_ID` keyed by child session id, with
  `record_subagent_start` / `record_subagent_stop` / `explicit_subagent_lineage`
  helpers. `_in_process_parent_session_id` consults this explicit registry
  **before** the frame walk.
- **`__init__.py`** — `register()` subscribes to `subagent_start` /
  `subagent_stop` when the host exposes `register_hook` (guarded with
  `getattr`/`callable`, like the existing `register_tool` gating). The
  `subagent_start` event fires before the child's `on_session_start`, so the
  linkage is present when LCM needs it.

## Precedence (unchanged where the signal is absent)
1. an explicit `parent_session_id` kwarg (highest);
2. **new:** the recorded `subagent_start` lineage for this session id;
3. the legacy `inspect.currentframe()` frame walk (fallback).

On a host with no plugin hook bus, step 2 is simply empty and behaviour is
byte-for-byte the old path.

## Validation
- `ruff check` → clean.
- New `tests/test_subagent_lineage.py` (5 tests): registry record/query/stop
  roundtrip, missing-child-id ignored, **explicit parent takes precedence over
  the frame walk** (and reverts to the frame walk after `subagent_stop`), hook
  subscription via `register()`, and the no-hook-bus no-op fallback.
- `python -m pytest -q -o addopts=` (full suite) → **1575 passed, 12 xfailed**
  (1570 prior + 5 new; the existing frame-walk tests are unchanged and green,
  confirming the fallback is untouched).
- `scripts/validate_release.sh --full --keep-going` → **PASS**.

## Notes
- Additive and backward-compatible: no host change is required. (A future
  one-line host addition — passing `parent_session_id=` into the
  `on_session_start` call — could let LCM drop the frame walk entirely, but this
  PR does not depend on it.)
- Builds on the WS5 Seam 5 extraction (`aux_session.py`, #337).

## Refs
- WS5.7 (frame-walk isolation) from the WS5 engine-decomposition plan.

title: Encapsulate DAG/lifecycle connections behind a public accessor (WS5.5)
body:
## What this changes
`command.py` and `tools.py` reached directly into the **private** SQLite
connections of the summary DAG (`engine._dag._conn`) and the lifecycle store
(`engine._lifecycle._conn`) to run read-only doctor/inspect diagnostics — FTS
sync counts, integrity checks, latest-node lookups, and the maintenance-debt
scan. This adds a public read-only `connection` accessor to both stores and
routes those reach-ins through it.

## Why
Reaching into a helper's `_conn` from another module bypasses the store's
encapsulation and its write-lock contract, and is exactly the kind of layer
violation the `MessageStore.connection` accessor (#323) was introduced to fix for
the message store. The DAG and lifecycle stores were still accessed raw. Making
the read-only diagnostic access explicit keeps the SQLite ownership in one place
and lets those stores evolve their internals without breaking `command.py` /
`tools.py`.

## How
- **`dag.py`** — add a `SummaryDAG.connection` read-only property (live
  connection or `None`), documented as read-only; writes still go through the
  DAG's own methods under `_db_lock`.
- **`lifecycle_state.py`** — add the same `LifecycleStateStore.connection`
  property.
- **`command.py` / `tools.py`** — route the seven cross-module reach-ins
  (`engine._dag._conn` ×5, `engine._lifecycle._conn` ×2, including the
  `getattr(..., "_conn", None)` doctor form) through the new accessors.

## Validation
- `ruff check dag.py lifecycle_state.py command.py tools.py` → clean.
- `python -m pytest -q -o addopts=` (full suite) → **1570 passed, 12 xfailed**;
  the 199 doctor/inspect/fts/integrity/lifecycle tests exercise the rerouted
  accessors.
- `scripts/validate_release.sh --full --keep-going` → **PASS**.

## Notes
- Behaviour-preserving: each accessor returns the same connection object the
  reach-in previously read (and tolerates `None`). Writes are unchanged.
- Completes the WS5.5 "layer discipline" cleanup begun in #323 (store connection)
  and #327 (doctor session-stat scans) for the remaining two SQLite-backed
  helpers.

## Refs
- WS5.5 (layer discipline) from the WS5 plan; companion to #323, #327.

title: Extract LCM-bypass fallback handling into a mixin (WS5 seam)
body:
## Summary
- Move the 14 methods that handle sessions bypassing LCM context management out of `engine.py` into a new `BypassMixin` in `bypass.py`.
- The cluster covers bypass detection (`_bypasses_lcm_context_management`, `_bypass_lcm_reason`, `_session_id_matches_lcm_bypass_filters`, …), host-fallback-compressor mirroring (`_get_host_fallback_compressor`, `_sync_host_fallback_compressor`, `_mirror_host_fallback_state`, …), and the deterministic bypass tail-compaction (`_bypass_compaction_target_tokens`, `_truncate_bypass_content_value`, `_trim_bypass_compacted_to_cap`, `_fallback_tail_compaction`, `_compress_lcm_bypassed_session`).
- `LCMEngine` mixes `BypassMixin` in before `ContextEngine`, so `self` still resolves every reference; call sites, shared engine state, and method names are unchanged.
- The two imports the block solely used (`importlib`, `_assistant_tool_call_ids`) move to `bypass.py` and are dropped from `engine.py`.

## Why
- Continues the WS5 engine decomposition. This is the first of the remaining "rest" clusters after the six documented seams landed; it is the lowest-risk one (no external call sites, no `LCMEngine.` statics, no module-level constants in the block).
- `engine.py` shrinks by 474 lines (5554 → 5080).

## Validation
- `ruff check .` -> `All checks passed!`
- Byte-identity: the extracted method bodies are byte-for-byte identical to `git show main:engine.py` lines 927-1401 (AST-slice compare, 0 diffs).
- `PYTHONPATH=<hermes-agent> python -m pytest -q -o addopts=` -> `1575 passed, 12 xfailed` (unchanged from the v0.19.0 baseline).
- `scripts/validate_release.sh --full` -> `PASS: release validation full` (all 12 gates; pytest full `1575 passed, 12 xfailed`, low-fd `1575 passed, 12 xfailed`, focused `402 passed`).

## Notes
- Behaviour-neutral, mechanical move only. No logic changes.
- Mixin ordering follows the established WS5 convention: `CompactionMixin` stays first (it overrides the compaction protocol); `BypassMixin` overrides no protocol method, so its position before `ContextEngine` is arbitrary and safe under any merge order.
- Deliberately left in `engine.py` (separate concerns / future seams): the bypass-lineage family (shares the auxiliary-session lock) and the session-end fingerprint/prefix helpers.

## Refs
Follows the WS5 module/mixin decomposition (#324, #325, #333, #334, #335, #337).

title: Extract session-end prefix matching into a mixin (WS5 seam)
body:
## Summary
- Move the 18 methods that compare the durable store's message prefix against replayed messages at session end -- and maintain the per-session LCM bypass/normal message-prefix fingerprints -- out of `engine.py` into a new `PrefixMatchingMixin` in `prefix_matching.py`.
- The cluster covers the session-end store-prefix comparison (`_session_end_matches_current_store_prefix`, `_session_end_prefix_compare_value/content/tool_calls/identity`, `_session_end_store_prefix_count`), the bypass/normal fingerprint bookkeeping (`_lcm_bypass_message_fingerprint`, `_remember_lcm_bypass_message_prefix`, `_remember_lcm_normal_message_prefix`, `_lcm_normal_prefix_key`), the prefix-match predicates (`_messages_match_*`, `_matching_*_prefix_count`, `_matching_lcm_bypass_prefix_evidence`), and `_append_off_current_session_end_suffix`.
- `LCMEngine` mixes `PrefixMatchingMixin` in before `ContextEngine`, so `self` still resolves every reference; call sites, shared engine state, and method names are unchanged.

## Why
- Continues the WS5 engine decomposition (second of the remaining "rest" clusters after the six documented seams). This cluster is self-contained: no external call sites, no `LCMEngine.` statics, and its one module-level constant is used nowhere else.
- `engine.py` shrinks by 344 lines (5554 -> 5210).

## Validation
- `ruff check .` -> `All checks passed!`
- Byte-identity: the extracted method bodies and the moved constant are byte-for-byte identical to `git show main:engine.py` (AST-slice compare, 0 diffs).
- `PYTHONPATH=<hermes-agent> python -m pytest -q -o addopts=` -> `1575 passed, 12 xfailed` (unchanged from the v0.19.0 baseline).
