title: Make schema-column migrations idempotent under concurrent startup
body:
## Summary
- Add `add_column_if_missing(conn, existing_columns, column, alter_sql)` in `db_bootstrap.py` and route all column migrations through it. It keeps the existing "skip if already present" check and additionally swallows exactly the `duplicate column name` `OperationalError` (any other error still propagates), making each `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN` idempotent under concurrency.
- Converted call sites: `ensure_lifecycle_state_columns` / `ensure_message_origin_columns` (db_bootstrap.py), `MessageStore._ensure_source_column` / `_ensure_conversation_id_column` (store.py), `SummaryDAG._ensure_source_window_columns` (dag.py).

## Why
In the multi-agent deployment (gateway + CLI sessions + sub-agents) every process opens its own connection to the same `lcm.db` and runs the startup migrations concurrently. Each column migration did check-`PRAGMA table_info`-then-`ALTER` in autocommit with no guard, so two processes could both observe a column as absent and both issue the ALTER. The loser raised `sqlite3.OperationalError: duplicate column name`, which propagated out of `_init_db` and **crashed store construction**. This bites precisely at an upgrade boundary, when many processes restart together.

Behaviour is unchanged on the non-racing path (same check, same ALTERs); only the concurrent loser now skips instead of crashing.

## Validation
- New regression test `TestConcurrentStartupMigration` (tests/test_crash_safe_wal.py) races `ensure_message_origin_columns` from 8 threads, each with its own connection to one seeded pre-v5 DB (FTS-free, to isolate the column DDL). Without the guard 7/8 threads raise `duplicate column name: conversation_id`; with it every thread migrates and the column exists exactly once.
- `ruff check .` -> clean.
- `PYTHONPATH=<hermes-agent> python -m pytest -q -o addopts=` -> `1576 passed, 12 xfailed`.
- `scripts/validate_release.sh --full` -> `PASS: release validation full` (all 12 gates, incl. low-fd).

## Notes
- Out of scope / follow-up: the FTS structural rebuild (`repair_external_content_fts`) has a separate concurrency window on a different trigger (missing shadow tables / corruption, not column upgrades — a column migration does not change row counts, so it does not enter that path). Left for a focused follow-up so this PR stays scoped to the verified crash.
- Rollback: revert the commit; migrations return to the prior unguarded check-then-ALTER.

## Refs
Surfaced by a comparison against the more mature lossless-claw, whose `runLcmMigrations` serializes migrations under `BEGIN EXCLUSIVE`.

title: Discard reasoning-only summaries instead of persisting them (unclosed <think>)
body:
## Summary
- Add `_sanitize_reasoning_summary(text)` in `escalation.py` and route `_call_llm_for_summary`'s return through it, so a reasoning-only summarizer response is discarded (returns `""`) instead of being persisted as the summary.
- Add `_REASONING_START_RE`, which matches an *unclosed* leading reasoning marker — including non-tag shapes: `<|think|>` / `<|start_of_think|>`, `[think]`, and prose headers `Thinking Process:` / `Chain of thought:`.

## Why
`_strip_reasoning_blocks` only removes *closed* `<think>...</think>` pairs (backreferenced regex). A reasoning model (Qwen/QwQ/DeepSeek-R1, GLM, MiniMax) that runs into `max_tokens` before emitting the closing tag leaves an **unclosed** block the regex cannot match. The leftover raw reasoning — which, per the existing module comment, often quotes the summarizer system prompt verbatim — was then accepted as the summary purely because `count_tokens(result) < source_tokens`, persisted as a `SummaryNode`, and replayed into the model as context (and re-fed by `lcm_expand_query`). That is both a summary-quality bug and a system-prompt leak.

With the fix, a reasoning-only response is falsy, so the existing escalation path advances to the next model / L2 / deterministic L3 truncation of the real source text. Behaviour is unchanged for normal summaries and already-handled closed blocks.

## Validation
- `_sanitize_reasoning_summary` unit test: closed->clean, unclosed->"", pipe/bracket/prose shapes->"", empty->"".
- `_call_llm_for_summary` integration: an unclosed `<think>` response returns `""` (without the fix it returns the raw reasoning blob — proven by temporarily reverting the wire-in).
- Escalation test: a reasoning-only primary escalates to the fallback model instead of accepting the empty result.
- `ruff check .` -> clean; full suite `1578 passed, 12 xfailed`; `scripts/validate_release.sh --full` -> `PASS: release validation full`.

## Notes
- The same closed-tag-only strip is used in `extraction.py`, `tools.py`, and `sanitize.py`; those non-summary paths are left for a focused follow-up so this PR stays scoped to the persisted-summary leak.
- Rollback: revert the commit; `_call_llm_for_summary` returns to `_strip_reasoning_blocks(content).strip()`.

## Refs
Mirrors lossless-claw `sanitizeReasoningSummaryText` (src/summarize.ts), which forces the empty-summary path on `reasoningOnly` output.

title: Budget L3 deterministic truncation in tokens, not chars*4 (CJK overshoot)
body:
## Summary
- Add `truncate_text_to_tokens(text, max_tokens, *, from_end=False)` in `tokens.py`: an exact tiktoken-encoder cut when available, with a script-density-aware char fallback (bounded-corrected so it never exceeds the budget) when tiktoken is absent.
- Rewrite `escalation._deterministic_truncate` to budget its head+tail cut in **tokens** (reserving the marker's token cost), instead of a flat `char_budget = max_tokens * 4`.

## Why
HL counts tokens accurately with tiktoken everywhere else, but the Level-3 deterministic-truncation fallback sized its cut with chars*4. For CJK / dense scripts (~1-2 chars/token) that overshoots the real token budget ~2-4x, so an L3 summary aimed at N tokens could emit 2-4N — overflowing the very budget L3 exists to guarantee and defeating overflow recovery on non-English conversations. Latin text is materially unchanged (chars*4 was already about right there).

## Validation
- `truncate_text_to_tokens` respects the budget (head/tail, short text, zero budget).
- `_deterministic_truncate` on dense CJK yields far fewer tokens than the reconstructed old chars*4 output and stays within ~1.4x of the budget (vs the old ~2-4x); converges; Latin head/tail preserved.
- `ruff check .` -> clean; full suite `1579 passed, 12 xfailed`; `scripts/validate_release.sh --full` -> `PASS: release validation full`.

## Notes
- Test-environment caveat baked into the test: CI has no tiktoken, so the char fallback over-counts the ASCII marker at the CJK density; the CJK test therefore compares against the reconstructed old chars*4 output (env-robust) rather than an absolute token bound. With tiktoken the result lands within a token or two of the budget.
- Rollback: revert; `_deterministic_truncate` returns to the chars*4 cut.

## Refs
Surfaced by a comparison against lossless-claw, which budgets its deterministic cap with the Unicode-aware estimateTokens (`compaction.ts` `capSummaryText`) that HL's L3 bypassed.

title: fix: KeyError: 'context_threshold'` in `lcm_status` — Transient Crash After Plugin Update
body:
### Expected behavior

# `KeyError: 'context_threshold'` in `lcm_status` — Transient Crash After Plugin Update

**Date:** 2026-07-07  
**Plugin:** `hermes-lcm` v0.19.0 (git `df9239ef`, branch `main`, working tree dirty)  
**Python:** 3.12.3  
**Session platform:** WebUI

---

## Symptom

Calling `lcm_status` (and every other LCM tool function: `lcm_grep`, `lcm_doctor`, `lcm_inspect`, etc.) raised:

```
KeyError: 'context_threshold'
```

The Hermes tool executor caught it and reported:

> Context engine tool 'lcm_status' failed: 'context_threshold'

---

## NOT Reproducible

After a **WebUI process restart** (`systemctl restart hermes-webui`), all LCM tools work flawlessly. No configuration change, no code rollback — only a process restart. The error has not returned in a session with 10,000+ messages and 18 DAG compression cycles since the restart.

---

## Code Analysis: Current Code Is Clean

A full static analysis of the entire plugin (`engine.py`, `config.py`, `tools.py`, `command.py`, `presets.py`) and the Hermes core (`context_engine.py`) found:

| Location | Access Pattern | Safe? |
|----------|---------------|-------|
| `engine.py:232` | `self._config.context_threshold` | ✅ Attribute access |
| `engine.py:517` | `self._config.config_sources.get("context_threshold", "manual_or_default")` | ✅ `.get()` with fallback |
| `engine.py:3468-71` | `self._config.context_threshold` / `self.context_threshold` | ✅ Attribute access |
| `tools.py:2373-76` | `full_status.get("context_threshold", engine._config.context_threshold)` | ✅ `.get()` with fallback |
| `tools.py:2408` | `engine._config.context_threshold` | ✅ Attribute access |
| `tools.py:2694` | `float(getattr(engine, "context_threshold", c.context_threshold))` | ✅ `getattr()` with fallback |
| Core `context_engine.py` | n/a — no access to `context_threshold` | ✅ Not referenced at all |

**No production code uses bare dict bracket access (`dict["context_threshold"]`).** Only test files and `benchmarking/types.py` use bracket access — these are never imported at runtime.

---

## Root Cause Hypothesis

### 1️⃣ Plugin Update During Active WebUI — Most Likely

The plugin directory shows `.bak` files dated 2026-07-03 — manual changes/backups happened recently. If `git pull` (or manual file edit) ran inside `/root/.hermes/plugins/hermes-lcm/` **while the WebUI was serving requests**, Python's import system could have read a **partially written `.py` file**.

**Python 3.12 uses hash-based `.pyc` invalidation (PEP 552).** This protects against *stale* `.pyc` files — but it does **NOT** protect against *incomplete* `.py` source files being read during a write. The sequence would be:

1. `git pull` starts writing `engine.py` (or `config.py`)
2. WebUI process triggers an LCM tool call → Python imports/reloads the module
3. Python reads the partially written `.py` file and compiles **broken bytecode**
4. The broken `get_status()` method uses a **mutated access pattern** — possibly a stale code path from an older git commit that used `dict["context_threshold"]` instead of the current safe `.get()`
5. → `KeyError: 'context_threshold'`
6. After process restart: `.py` file is fully written → correct bytecode → no error

### 2️⃣ Race in `from_env()` — Less Likely

`config.py:from_env()` builds the config dataclass and records `config_sources`. If `config_sources` were populated **after** `context_threshold` was written (race in `__post_init__` vs `from_env()`), a brief window exists where `self.context_threshold` is set but `config_sources["context_threshold"]` is not. However, the current code reads `self._config.context_threshold` (attribute), not `config_sources[...]` (dict), so this should not happen.

### 3️⃣ Stale `__pycache__` — Disproven

Python 3.12's hash-based `.pyc` invalidation (PEP 552) stores the source hash in the `.pyc` header. A stale `.pyc` cannot be loaded if the source hash doesn't match. Only a corrupted `.pyc` with a matching hash could cause this — which requires the source to be incomplete during compilation (covered by hypothesis #1).

---

## Recommendations

### Immediate (Operator)
- **Always run `hermes plugins update hermes-lcm` BEFORE starting the WebUI**, never during an active session
- Or restart WebUI after a plugin update: `systemctl restart hermes-webui`

### Medium-Term (Plugin)
- Add a **defensive wrapper** in `engine.py:get_status()` that catches `KeyError` on `context_threshold` and falls back to the config default (0.35)
- Consider **delayed initialization**: separate import-time setup from runtime setup
- Could add a **version stamp** in the plugin's `__init__` that's validated on tool calls

### Long-Term (Hermes Core)
- Make `hermes plugins update` atomic: clone to tmpdir, then rename
- Or: plugin update should trigger a graceful WebUI reload
- Or: add a `hermes plugins update --restart-webui` flag

---

## Open Questions

- [ ] Do older git commits of `hermes-lcm` contain code with `dict["context_threshold"]` bracket access? (If so, a partial write + import of an older state could explain the exact error)
- [ ] Are other users seeing transient `KeyError` crashes on `lcm_status`?
- [ ] Can `hermes plugins update` be made atomic (clone → hash check → atomic rename)?

---

## Environment

| Component | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Hermes WebUI | systemd service at `/usr/local/lib/hermes-webui/server.py` |
| LCM plugin path | `/root/.hermes/plugins/hermes-lcm/` |
| LCM plugin version | v0.19.0 (git `df9239ef`, dirty — has `.bak` files) |
| LCM DB | `/root/.hermes/profiles/labbot/lcm.db` (10K+ messages, 18 DAG nodes) |
| OS | Linux (Proxmox LXC) 7.0.12-1-pve |
| Python | 3.12.3 |

---

*Compiled by labbot on 2026-07-07 after forensic analysis of the transient `KeyError: 'context_threshold'` crash. Error was NOT reproducible after WebUI restart.*

title: fix: prevent LCM scaffold recursion and preflight skips
body:
## Summary
- Stop treating previously emitted preserved-objective scaffolds as eligible latest-user anchor sources.
- Expose LCM's effective active-context assembly cap as the host-visible `threshold_tokens` preflight trigger.
- Add regressions for lower `max_assembly_tokens` and reserve-based assembly caps so Hermes core does not skip preflight when LCM's real assembly budget is lower than the normal context-threshold value.

## Why
- Preserved-objective scaffolds are derived continuity metadata, not human turns. Reusing a prior scaffold as the next latest-user anchor can recursively preserve stale/synthetic context and grow active context pressure.
- Hermes core uses a compressor's `threshold_tokens` as a cheap gate before it pays for the full request estimate that includes system prompt and tool schemas.
- LCM can enforce a stricter active-context budget than `context_length * context_threshold` via `LCM_MAX_ASSEMBLY_TOKENS` or `LCM_RESERVE_TOKENS_FLOOR`. If LCM advertises only the larger context threshold, Hermes can skip preflight and then send a request that exceeds the real active-context budget.
- New invariant: when an assembly cap is active, LCM exposes `min(context_threshold_tokens, effective_assembly_cap)` as `threshold_tokens`.

## Validation
- [x] Focused validation: `python3 -m pytest -q tests/test_lcm_engine.py::test_threshold_tokens_respects_lower_max_assembly_cap_for_host_preflight tests/test_lcm_engine.py::test_threshold_tokens_respects_lower_reserve_based_cap_for_host_preflight tests/test_lcm_engine.py::test_codex_oauth_context_cap_constrains_reserve_based_assembly_cap` -> `3 passed`
- [x] Engine validation: `python3 -m pytest -q tests/test_lcm_engine.py` -> `698 passed`
- [x] Lint: `python3 -m ruff check engine.py tests/test_lcm_engine.py` -> `All checks passed!`
- [x] Diff check: `git diff --check` -> exit 0 before commit
- [x] GitHub CI on `dddc80c5ff6b769d1602d4dfbee81e2e4b40c8bc` -> `workflow-lint`, `lint`, `test (3.11)`, `test (3.12)`, `test (3.13)`, and `test (3.14)` passed
- [ ] Broader local adjacent validation: `python3 -m pytest -q tests/test_lcm_engine.py tests/test_ingest_protection.py` -> `828 passed, 2 failed`; both failures are the existing `import_lossless_claw` legacy data-URI externalization assertions and reproduce on pristine `origin/main` with the two focused failing tests.

title: fix(escalation): never str.format() the auto-derived focus topic
body:
## Summary

`_build_l1_focus_brief` / `_build_l2_focus_brief` run `str.format()` over a string
that already embeds the **auto-derived focus topic**, which comes from raw user
message text. When that text contains literal curly braces, `.format()` parses
them as replacement fields and raises — aborting compaction and dropping the whole
turn.

## Root cause

Both builders assemble the guidance string from adjacent literals, one of which is
an **f-string** that interpolates the untrusted topic, and then call `.format()`
over the *entire* assembled string:

```python
markers = " / ".join(...)              # compile-time constant
return (
    "Focus brief:\n"
    f"Primary focus: {topic}\n"        # <-- untrusted topic embedded here
    ...
    "mark them under one of these historical headings: {markers}.\n"
    ...
).format(markers=markers)              # <-- .format() re-parses the whole string, incl. topic's braces
```

`topic` is produced by `LCMEngine._derive_auto_focus_topic`, which pulls the raw
text of the latest user turns (whitespace-collapsed / redacted / truncated only —
braces preserved; the truncation can even slice a JSON object mid-brace). So any
brace in recent user content flows into `.format()`:

- `unmatched '{' in format spec` (e.g. `plan {tier: {gold`, or JSON sliced mid-object)
- `Single '}' encountered in format string` (a lone `}`)
- `KeyError` / `IndexError` (`{"k": "v"}`, `{0}` …)

We hit this in production when the latest user message was a brace-dense JSON
payload: every compaction on that session failed with
`ValueError: unmatched '{' in format spec`, before any summarizer model call, and
the turn was lost.

Traceback tail:

```
escalation.py:_build_l1_prompt -> _build_l1_focus_brief(focus_topic)
    ).format(markers=markers)
ValueError: unmatched '{' in format spec
```

## Fix

`{markers}` is the only real placeholder and it is a compile-time constant, so
there is no reason to run `.format()` over the assembled string. Make the
`{markers}` line an f-string segment and drop `.format()` entirely. The untrusted
topic is then only ever embedded via f-string interpolation, which does **not**
re-parse the interpolated value for braces.

Applied to both `_build_l1_focus_brief` and `_build_l2_focus_brief` (4 lines).

## Tests

Adds `tests/test_focus_brief_brace_safe.py`: parametrized over both builders and
over lone `{`, lone `}`, balanced `{}`, nested `{x:{y`, and a brace-dense JSON
focus topic — asserts no exception, the historical-heading markers still render,
and the topic text is embedded verbatim (braces intact). Also covers the
empty-topic `""` path. Fails on `main` (10/12), passes with this change (12/12).

title: feat: per-model compression threshold overrides
body:
## Summary

- Add `model_thresholds`, a mapping of model-name substrings to context-compaction threshold fractions.
- Resolve the longest matching substring whenever the active model changes.
- Support both `lcm.model_thresholds` in `config.yaml` and `LCM_MODEL_THRESHOLDS` for existing env-driven deployments.
- Reject empty keys, booleans, non-finite values, and thresholds outside `(0, 1]`.
- Keep existing behavior unchanged when the mapping is empty.

## Why

A single fraction is a poor fit when one Hermes installation switches between models with materially different context windows. For example, an operator may want a 256K route to compact at 70% while a 1M route compacts at 25%.

## Configuration

```yaml
lcm:
  context_threshold: 0.35
  model_thresholds:
    glm-5.2: 0.70
    glm-5.2-1M: 0.25
```

Or, for existing env-driven deployments:

```bash
LCM_MODEL_THRESHOLDS=glm-5.2:0.70,glm-5.2-1M:0.25
```

Longest substring wins, so `glm-5.2-1M` takes precedence over `glm-5.2`. The selected per-model override takes precedence over the global threshold and the Codex GPT-5.5 auto-raise. Empty mappings preserve current behavior.

This PR deliberately stays at the existing model-identity seam. Context-window-class and session-pattern policies are useful follow-up work, but would introduce a larger policy language and are not required for this bounded operator override.

## Validation

- `tests/test_per_model_threshold.py`: 18 passed
- `tests/test_lcm_core.py::TestConfig` plus focused model-update/Codex threshold tests: 54 passed
- Broad core/command/engine component suite: 1,155 passed
- Packaging/install suite with isolated `HERMES_HOME`: 38 passed
- Ruff, compilation, and `git diff --check`: passed

The refreshed branch is based on current upstream `main` (`v0.21.0-rc2`).

title: fix: make focus brief formatting brace-safe
body:
## Summary
- make L1/L2 focus brief construction safe when the focus topic contains literal braces such as JSON snippets or `{0}` placeholders
- add regression coverage for both focus brief builders

## Why
- focus topics are derived from recent user turns, which can include logs, JSON, markdown, or placeholders with `{}`
- the previous builders formatted the whole assembled prompt with `.format(markers=...)`, so braces from the user-derived topic were parsed as format fields and could crash compression before summarization

title: fix(search): keep natural-language queries on the FTS5 path instead of crashing to the LIKE fallback
body:
## Problem

Any conversational search query containing an apostrophe, comma, question mark, or most other punctuation (for example `don't`) is a syntax error to FTS5. `store.search` catches the error and silently degrades to the LIKE fallback, so in practice nearly every natural-language query runs on the slow, unranked fallback path instead of the FTS index.

## Mechanism

`sanitize_fts5_query` (`search_query.py:47`) only replaces the fixed operator set `_FTS5_SPECIAL_CHARS` (`search_query.py:36`), leaving apostrophes, commas, and question marks in the unquoted query text. `store.search` (`store.py:931`) passes the result to `messages_fts MATCH`, FTS5 raises `fts5: syntax error near "'"`, and the handler at `store.py:997` logs "FTS message search failed, falling back to LIKE" and degrades. `dag.py:427` has the same path for summary search.

## Fix

Outside quoted phrases, keep only bareword-safe characters (alphanumerics, underscore, whitespace) and replace everything else with spaces. That is exactly the token alphabet the unicode61 tokenizer indexed, so the sanitized query matches the index instead of erroring; `don't` becomes `don t`, which matches rows containing `don't`. Quoted phrases pass through verbatim, as before.

The LIKE fallback must not use that strict sanitization: it matches raw stored content, so apostrophes, emoji, and CJK punctuation have to survive for the fallback to find them (an emoji-only query would otherwise produce zero terms and return nothing). The helper is therefore split in two: `sanitize_fts5_query` (strict, used by the FTS MATCH paths) and `sanitize_like_terms_query` (the previous operator-stripping behavior, used by `_search_like` in `store.py` and `dag.py`).

## Verification

New tests cover: `don't` returning its row on the FTS path with no fallback warning, a full conversational sentence (`what did I tell you, don't you remember?`) searching without any `OperationalError` or fallback, quoted phrases with trailing conversational punctuation still matching as phrases, and sanitizer unit cases. On unpatched main the new tests fail with the exact production error (`fts5: syntax error near ","`). The full `tests/test_lcm_core.py` suite passes (288 tests), including the existing emoji and LIKE-fallback regression tests.

## Incident evidence

One live store logged the FTS-to-LIKE fallback warning over 300 times, meaning nearly every conversational search had been silently running on the degraded fallback path.

title: Compaction can remove the only user message → Qwen-family chat templates reject the request (400: 'No user query found in messages')
body:
Found on v0.12.0 driving a local Qwen3.5-family model (Ornith-9B via oMLX/mlx-lm).

**Symptom:** after a leaf compaction on an agentic session (one user query followed by a long assistant/tool chain), the next model call fails `400: Chat template error: No user query found in messages.` — the client (Hermes) retries the deterministic 400 and surfaces 'model provider failed after retries'.

**Root cause:** `LCMEngine._leading_anchor_count` anchors only the system prompt, so the session's single user message is eligible for compaction. Once folded into a DAG summary, no user-role message remains (fresh tail is all assistant/tool), and Qwen-family chat templates hard-raise (`chat_template.jinja`: `raise_exception('No user query found in messages.')` when the trailing scan finds no real user query).

**Fix that works for us** (patched locally, verified end-to-end — compacted shape now renders, control still 400s):
1. Anchor the first user message too:
```python
n = 1 if (messages and messages[0].get('role') == 'system') else 0
for i in range(n, min(len(messages), n + 3)):
    if messages[i].get('role') == 'user':
        return i + 1
return n
```
2. Adapt the overflow-recovery call site so the multi-message anchor isn't dropped: `working_messages[1 if leading_anchor_count else 0:]` for the tail argument (identical under old semantics).

Anchoring the original query also keeps the task grounding in raw context, which the existing docstring already argues for. Happy to PR if useful.

title: Auxiliary-frame detection is defeated by hermes-agent setting the background_review marker after __init__ (store pollution; host fix in hermes-agent#61088)
body:
## Summary

The auxiliary-frame detection that protects the store from background-review forks (`_caller_is_auxiliary_agent_frame`, in `engine.py` through v0.18.x and `aux_session.py` in v0.19+) trusts the agent attribute `_memory_write_origin == "background_review"`. A timing bug on the hermes-agent side means that attribute does not exist yet at the moment the detection runs, so the protection is silently defeated. This issue is a heads-up plus a pointer to the host-side fix, since the failure lands in hermes-lcm's store even though the bug lives in the host.

## What happens

hermes-agent's `spawn_background_review_thread` constructs the review fork with a plain `AIAgent(...)` call and only assigns `_memory_write_origin = "background_review"` after the constructor returns. But the engine's `on_session_start` fires during `__init__` (from agent_init), and before that agent_init unconditionally sets `_memory_write_origin = "assistant_tool"`. So when the frame walk runs with the fork's fresh session id, it sees the foreground default on the constructing agent, every other auxiliary signal also misses (the fork inherits the parent's full toolsets for provider-cache parity, has no subagent id, and its state.db row makes it a direct child of the foreground session, which the child-session probe deliberately does not treat as auxiliary), and the engine binds the fork's session id as a real foreground session.

The fork's post-LLM ingest then bulk-ingests the entire parent conversation snapshot into the store as a brand-new session stamped with the replay time. On one live deployment this produced one to three fake sessions per day. Over weeks that added up to roughly a fifth of the whole store being wrong-dated duplicates, and "most recent session" style queries kept returning a replay artifact instead of the real conversation.

## Host-side fix

Filed against hermes-agent as https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/61088: the fork is constructed through a small `AIAgent` subclass that seeds both markers before `super().__init__`, and agent_init now honors a pre-seeded value instead of clobbering it. With that in place the existing hermes-lcm detection works exactly as designed (verified live: the fork's session is registered auxiliary and nothing is ingested).

## Why you might still want a change on the hermes-lcm side

Even after the host fix, the engine's protection depends on a host attribute existing at construction time, which is fragile against future host refactors (this is the second ordering-sensitive interaction between the two codebases). A possible defense in depth: re-evaluate the auxiliary signals at first ingest for a session, not only at `on_session_start`. At ingest time the review fork's markers ARE set (the assignment happens before `run_conversation`), so a re-check would catch this class of bug even when the bind-time check misses. A cheaper alternative is a bulk-ingest heuristic: a "new" session whose first ingest delivers dozens of messages timestamped in the past is almost certainly a replay, not a live conversation.

Happy to provide more detail or logs from the incident if useful. Related but independent: #354 (FTS5 natural-language query sanitization).

title: fix: preserve ambiguous durable-tail overlap rows
body:
## Summary

Preserve incoming rows whenever a partial durable-tail overlap is ambiguous. A synthetic LCM scaffold proves that context was prepended, but does not independently prove that following rows replay durable history.

This repair removes the unsafe scaffold + unique-partial-tail inference. Explicitly proven replay paths remain unchanged: full exact replay, durable message identity, tool-call/source/generation identity, and cursor-based reconciliation can still advance the ingest cursor. Without such independent proof, reconciliation prefers duplicate-over-loss and persists the incoming rows.

The branch also incorporates current `main` through a normal non-rewriting merge. The previous PR head and current `main` are both ancestors of this head.

## Root cause

The prior heuristic treated a unique multi-row suffix match after synthetic scaffold rows as replay evidence. For stored tail `X, Y` and incoming scaffold + summary + `X, Y, Z`, that advanced past `X, Y` and persisted only `Z`. The scaffold established only that synthetic context existed; it could not distinguish replayed `X, Y` from fresh rows that happened to repeat the durable tail.

Because false-positive deduplication loses messages while false-negative deduplication only duplicates them, ambiguous overlaps must preserve the full incoming delta.

## Behavior

- Ambiguous unique partial-tail overlap: preserve incoming rows.
- Repeated-tail and singleton overlap: remain ambiguous and preserve incoming rows.
- Scaffold-only prefix with fresh matching rows: preserve incoming rows.
- Full exact replay and complete cursor replay: still deduplicate.
- No-overlap ingest: unchanged.
- Durable/tool/source/generation identity: remains available to prove replay.
- Restarted and compacted sessions: do not lose ambiguous rows.

## Validation

Exact head: `83e2334172e3e32676db944e00bc7f0a002dcf5f`

- TDD RED on untouched PR head: compacted restart regression failed because fresh matching `X, Y` rows were dropped (`1 failed, 702 deselected`).
- Focused ambiguity/replay/restart matrix: `10 passed`.

## Related review

- The later Codex P1 correctly identified that a synthetic scaffold still did not make the overlap unambiguous.
- This repair removes that remaining inference rather than adding another heuristic.

title: feat: add store-level replay-flood backstop on batch ingest
body:
## Summary
Adds a store-level replay-flood backstop before protected batch writes, plus engine-level refusal handling and status telemetry.

The latest repair makes contentless assistant tool-call replay identity stable without changing the durable format:

- user replay floods are refused at the external threshold (default `8`);
- repeated internal identities are refused at the internal threshold (default `32`);
- `tool_calls` participates in assistant replay identity, including contentless tool-call messages;
- direct `function.arguments` objects/lists are canonicalized recursively, so mapping key order does not change identity;
- IDs and nested string-valued argument leaves remain byte-distinct, including JSON-looking strings;
- existing plain `json.dumps(tool_calls)` rows remain visible to the replay probe;
- refusal happens before any insert, leaves count/cursor unchanged, and a later genuinely fresh ingest succeeds;
- thresholds remain configurable with `LCM_REPLAY_FLOOD_THRESHOLD_EXTERNAL` and `LCM_REPLAY_FLOOD_THRESHOLD_INTERNAL`; `0` disables the corresponding guard.

## Why
`messages` has no identity hash or uniqueness constraint, and the protected append path otherwise writes a reconciled batch unconditionally. A bad replay/ambiguity decision could therefore persist duplicate rows, replay them into active context, pollute recall, and skew token accounting.

The guard is deliberately batch-shaped and conservative: normal per-turn deltas avoid existence probes, intentionally ambiguous small duplicate deltas remain admissible, and only a replay-shaped threshold breach becomes a loud, atomic refusal.

title: fix: retry WAL conversion on lock contention at connection setup
body:
## Summary
Follow-up to #346 (concurrent-startup migration race), one phase earlier in the same failure class. `configure_connection` runs `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL` as its first statement. Converting a rollback-journal database to WAL needs the exclusive lock, and SQLite can return `SQLITE_BUSY` for that upgrade **without consulting the busy handler** while sibling connections are mid-setup on the same file. Concurrent process startup (gateway + CLI + sub-agents — the documented topology) on a not-yet-WAL database therefore crashed sporadically with `sqlite3.OperationalError: database is locked` during store construction. Steady state is immune: once the database is WAL, the pragma is a plain read.

Two changes:
- **`db_bootstrap.configure_connection`**: set `busy_timeout` first, then run the WAL conversion through `_execute_wal_conversion_with_lock_retry` — a bounded exponential-backoff retry (5ms→250ms steps, total budget `SQLITE_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS`) that only swallows lock-contention errors and re-raises everything else or on budget exhaustion.
- **`tests/test_crash_safe_wal.py::TestConcurrentStartupMigration`**: the regression test that exposed this had a second bug of its own — `barrier.wait()` without timeout. The thread that crashed pre-barrier left the seven survivors parked forever, so instead of a red test the whole pytest run deadlocked (observed twice as a `validate_release --full` hang at 4%, 8 threads in futex wait, zero CPU). The barrier now uses a timeout and `abort()` on failure, `join` is bounded with a liveness assert, and the final assert reports the root-cause exception instead of hiding it.

## Why
The hang variant is worse than the crash variant: it silently stalls any CI/validation run that executes the suite, with no error to act on. And the underlying crash is the same first-boot scenario #346 fixed for column DDL — a fresh install or an upgrade from a pre-WAL database with several Hermes processes starting together.

## Validation
```
ruff check db_bootstrap.py tests/test_crash_safe_wal.py     # All checks passed!
python -m pytest tests/ -q                                   # 1590 passed, 12 xfailed
```
Reproduction & proof (Linux, 8-thread barrier race on a rollback-journal seed DB):
- Unfixed: standalone repro script hit `database is locked` from `configure_connection` (`PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL`) within 15 attempts; the unhardened test hung 2/10 runs (killed only by an external timeout).
- Fixed: 60/60 repro attempts clean; hardened test file looped 30× with zero failures or hangs.

## Notes
- Retry scope is deliberately the WAL conversion only — the other pragmas are per-connection settings that do not take the exclusive-lock upgrade path.
- The hardened test now degrades into an actionable assertion (with the recorded root-cause exception) if any future setup-phase error appears, instead of deadlocking the suite.

## Refs
- #346 (atomic column migrations, same concurrent-startup family)
- `db_bootstrap.py::configure_connection`, `SQLITE_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS`

Second WS1.5 step, stacked on #362: preserve messages matched by `ignore_message_patterns` in the lossless `ignored_messages` sidecar while keeping them out of the active LCM path.

Previously, matching messages were dropped permanently. The sidecar provides an audit-only durable path, but restart reconciliation must distinguish already persisted ignored rows from fresh input. ## Summary

- Allow every scalar `LCM_*` setting represented by `ENV_FIELD_SPECS` to be configured under the `lcm:` section of `~/.hermes/config.yaml`.

Today only `lcm.context_threshold` is supported in YAML on `main`; other LCM tuning controls require process environment variables. lcm:

title: fix(codex): add gpt-5.6 Codex OAuth effective context cap (372K)
body:
## Summary

- Add a `"gpt-5.6": 372_000` entry to `_CODEX_OAUTH_CONTEXT_CAPS` in `codex_routing.py`.

## Root cause

OpenAI's Codex model catalog reports `context_window: 372000` for GPT-5.6 Sol/Terra/Luna:
https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/models-manager/models.json

The previous `_CODEX_OAUTH_CONTEXT_CAPS` table had no `gpt-5.6` entry. Bare-slug matching in
`_codex_oauth_context_cap` therefore fell through to the generic `"gpt-5" -> 272_000` fallback,
clamping the real 372K window down to 272K. Because ENG-540's `_effective_context_length` clamps
`raw_context_length` to the cap whenever `raw > cap`, the host-advertised 372K context length got
silently capped at 272K, firing context compression ~100K tokens too early.

This matches the user-visible symptom: `/model` shows "Context: 372,000 tokens" (Hermes core
resolves 372K correctly), but the chat budget drops to 272K (`effective_context_length_reason:
codex_oauth_context_cap`), and compression triggers at 0.8 * 272K = 217.6K.

## Fix

Add `"gpt-5.6": 372_000` ahead of the generic `"gpt-5"` entry. Since matching iterates longest
slug first, all `gpt-5.6*`, `gpt-5.6-luna`, `gpt-5.6-terra`, `gpt-5.6-sol` variants resolve to
372K. The clamp then becomes a no-op (raw == cap), preserving the real window.

## Verification

Direct helper check after the change:
```
_codex_oauth_context_cap("gpt-5.6-luna", "openai-codex")  -> 372000
_codex_oauth_context_cap("gpt-5.6-terra", "openai-codex") -> 372000
_codex_oauth_context_cap("gpt-5.6-sol",   "openai-codex") -> 372000
_codex_oauth_context_cap("gpt-5.6",       "openai-codex") -> 372000
_codex_oauth_context_cap("gpt-5.5",       "openai-codex") -> 272000  (unchanged)
_codex_oauth_context_cap("gpt-5.4",       "openai-codex") -> 272000  (unchanged)
```

This mirrors NousResearch/hermes-agent PR #61910 (core-side 372K refresh for GPT-5.6) so the
LCM cap and the host-advertised context length agree.

## Notes

- `gpt-5.5` / `gpt-5.4` remain pinned at 272K, which is correct for the ChatGPT Codex OAuth route
  (see NousResearch/hermes-agent issue #27918 — direct OpenAI API is 1M, but Codex OAuth enforces 272K).
- No test changes: existing `codex_oauth_context_cap` tests use `gpt-5.5`/400K placeholders and are
  unaffected. A `gpt-5.6` regression case can be added if desired; I left it out to keep the diff minimal.

title: fix: never block token counting on tiktoken's network download
body:
## Reworked per review — thank you @Tosko4, you were right

Your point 4 sent me back to instrument the actual stack, and the finding invalidates my original design entirely. This PR is now a different, much smaller change; the async executor, backlog semaphore, drain handle, and pre-warm are all **gone**, and the four post-hook tests pass **unmodified** (the hook is synchronous again).

## The real root cause (profiled, reproduced)

`tiktoken.get_encoding("cl100k_base")` downloads its BPE file over the network on first use when it isn't cached on disk. On a restricted-egress host that request hangs until the transport gives up. `_get_encoder()` sits under `count_tokens()` on the ingest path — which hosts run inside the synchronous `post_llm_call` hook — so the first turn after every process start blocked reply delivery.

cProfile of the first ingest of a ~45K-token history on a restricted-egress host:

```
1  128.108s  engine.py ingest
1  128.107s  engine.py _ingest_messages
2  127.852s  tokens.py count_message_tokens
1  127.791s  tiktoken load_tiktoken_bpe → requests.get(...)
```

Second turn, same process: 0.1s. You were right that `ingest()` does no summarization — my "two 60s summary timeouts" reading of the 127s was a coincidence of numbers; the duration is the network transport's give-up time, which is why it was so repeatable.

## The fix

`tokens.py` only: load the encoder in a daemon thread. The first caller waits up to 2s (the common cached-on-disk case still gets exact counts immediately); after that, callers never wait — they use the existing char-based estimator until the loader finishes, then the encoder is adopted and `_count_tokens_cached` is cleared (counts for identical text change on adoption). A permanently blocked download degrades to the estimator for the life of the process — the same posture as tiktoken being uninstalled, which this module already supports.

Measured on the same blocked-egress host: first-turn hook **128.5s → 2.2s**, fully synchronous.

## Your review points

1–3 (stale rebind, foreground serialization, executor lifecycle): all real, all mooted — that machinery no longer exists in this PR.
4 (prove the root cause): profile and reproduction above.

Validation: full suite 1608 passed (3 new tests: hung-loader non-blocking contract, post-load adoption + cache clear, loader-failure fallback); ruff clean; `compileall` clean.

title: Feature Request: Per-provider compaction mode (inline aggressive vs cache-aware deferred)
body:
## Summary

Extend `ModelCompactionPolicy` to carry a `compaction_mode` field so that compaction strategy can be selected per provider/model, not just as a global flag. This lets operators use aggressive inline compaction on providers where cached tokens provide no discount (e.g. Ollama Cloud) while using cache-aware deferred compaction on providers that do offer cache discounts (e.g. Anthropic).

## Background

Research into Ollama Cloud's billing model (GPU-time-based, not per-token) reveals that cached tokens provide no measurable savings:

- Ollama Cloud's pricing page says "prompts that share cached context use less" but there is zero transparency — `cached_tokens` is always reported as 0 (issue #15758 on ollama/ollama).
- A subscriber benchmarked Ollama Cloud and confirmed the cache benefit is "not there" in practice (issue #16714 on ollama/ollama, Jun 2026).
- The billing model is opaque GPU-time — you cannot verify whether cached prefixes reduced usage.

Meanwhile, Anthropic and other providers DO offer prompt cache discounts. The optimal compaction strategy depends on the provider:

| Provider | Cache discount? | Optimal strategy |
|----------|----------------|------------------|
| Ollama Cloud | No (confirmed) | Aggressive inline compaction — reduce tokens per prompt as fast as possible |
| Anthropic | Yes (300s TTL) | Cache-aware deferred compaction — preserve cached prefix, defer summarization to `maintain()` after cache expiry |
| OpenAI | Yes (cached input tokens) | Cache-aware deferred compaction |
| DeepSeek | Yes (cache hit pricing) | Cache-aware deferred compaction |

hermes-lcm currently has `cache_friendly_condensation_enabled` and `deferred_maintenance_enabled` as **global** boolean flags. This means you must choose one strategy for all providers — which is wrong for multi-provider setups (e.g. LlamaHerd routing to Ollama Cloud + OpenAI fallback).

## Proposed Design

### 1. Add `compaction_mode` to `ModelCompactionPolicy`

Extend `policy.py`:

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ModelCompactionPolicy:
    # ... existing fields ...
    
    # Compaction mode: "inline" (aggressive, immediate) or "deferred" (cache-aware)
    compaction_mode: str = "inline"  # "inline" or "deferred"
    
    # Cache TTL for deferred mode (seconds, 0 = no cache tracking)
    cache_ttl_seconds: int = 0
```

### 2. Add per-model policy presets

Extend `_DEFAULT_CUTOVER_OVERRIDES` into full policy presets or create a parallel `_DEFAULT_POLICY_PRESETS` dict:

```python
_DEFAULT_POLICY_PRESETS: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {
    # Ollama Cloud models — no cache discount, aggressive inline compaction
    "glm-5.2": {
        "cutover_threshold": 0.35,
        "compaction_mode": "inline",
        "cache_friendly_condensation_enabled": False,
    },
    "deepseek-v4-flash": {
        "cutover_threshold": 0.85,
        "compaction_mode": "deferred",
        "cache_friendly_condensation_enabled": True,
        "cache_ttl_seconds": 300,
    },
    "deepseek-v4-pro": {
        "cutover_threshold": 0.80,
        "compaction_mode": "deferred",
        "cache_friendly_condensation_enabled": True,
        "cache_ttl_seconds": 300,
    },
    # Anthropic models — cache discount, defer compaction
    "claude-sonnet-4": {
        "cutover_threshold": 0.75,
        "compaction_mode": "deferred",
        "cache_friendly_condensation_enabled": True,
        "cache_ttl_seconds": 300,
    },
    "claude-opus-4": {
        "cutover_threshold": 0.75,
        "compaction_mode": "deferred",
        "cache_friendly_condensation_enabled": True,
        "cache_ttl_seconds": 300,
    },
    # OpenAI models — cached input tokens, defer compaction
    "gpt-5.5": {
        "cutover_threshold": 0.85,
        "compaction_mode": "deferred",
        "cache_friendly_condensation_enabled": True,
        "cache_ttl_seconds": 300,
    },
    # GPT-5.6 via Codex — preserve cached prefix
    "gpt-5.6-sol": {
        "cutover_threshold": 0.85,
        "compaction_mode": "deferred",
        "cache_friendly_condensation_enabled": True,
        "cache_ttl_seconds": 300,
    },
    "gpt-5.6-terra": {
        "cutover_threshold": 0.85,
        "compaction_mode": "deferred",
        "cache_friendly_condensation_enabled": True,
        "cache_ttl_seconds": 300,
    },
}
```

### 3. Config YAML: `lcm.model_policies`

Add a new `lcm.model_policies` section in `config.yaml` for user-defined per-model overrides (extends the existing `lcm.model_thresholds` which only covers cutover):

```yaml
lcm:
  model_policies:
    glm-5.2:
      compaction_mode: inline
      cutover_threshold: 0.35
      cache_friendly_condensation: false
    claude-sonnet-4:
      compaction_mode: deferred
      cutover_threshold: 0.75
      cache_friendly_condensation: true
      cache_ttl_seconds: 300
    deepseek-v4-flash:
      compaction_mode: deferred
      cutover_threshold: 0.85
      cache_friendly_condensation: true
      cache_ttl_seconds: 300
```

Resolution priority (highest first):
1. `lcm.model_policies` explicit per-model entry (longest match)
2. `_DEFAULT_POLICY_PRESETS` built-in per-model preset (longest match)
3. `lcm.model_thresholds` legacy per-model cutover override (backward compat)
4. `lcm.context_threshold` scalar global default
5. `DEFAULT_UNKNOWN_CUTOVER` (0.75)

### 4. Environment variable: `LCM_MODEL_POLICIES`

For env-only deployments:

```
LCM_MODEL_POLICIES=glm-5.2:inline:0.35:false,claude-sonnet-4:deferred:0.75:true:300
```

Format: `model:mode:cutover:cache_friendly[:cache_ttl]`, comma-separated.

### 5. Behavior change in `compaction.py`

`should_compress_preflight()` and `compress()` should consult `policy.compaction_mode`:

```python
def should_compress_preflight(self, messages):
    policy = self._resolve_policy()  # already resolves per-model
    
    if policy.compaction_mode == "deferred" and policy.cache_friendly_condensation_enabled:
        # Record debt but don't block current turn
        # Preserve cached prefix for providers with cache discounts
        return self._record_deferred_compaction_debt(messages)
    
    # Inline mode: aggressive compaction, reduce tokens immediately
    return super().should_compress_preflight(messages)
```

The existing `cache_friendly_condensation_enabled` global flag becomes the fallback default when no per-model policy is resolved. Existing behavior is preserved — the global flag still works, it's just overridden when a per-model policy exists.

### 6. Cache-aware gate for deferred mode

New `cache_aware.py`:

```python
class CacheAwareCompactionGate:
    def __init__(self, cache_ttl_seconds: int = 300):
        self._cache_ttl = cache_ttl_seconds
        self._last_cache_write = 0.0
    
    def record_cache_write(self):
        self._last_cache_write = time.time()
    
    def cache_still_hot(self) -> bool:
        if self._last_cache_write == 0:
            return False
        return (time.time() - self._last_cache_write) < self._cache_ttl
    
    def should_defer_compaction(self) -> bool:
        return self.cache_still_hot()
```

Called from `should_compress_preflight()` when `policy.compaction_mode == "deferred"`.

### 7. `lcm_status` and `lcm_inspect` reporting

The `ModelCompactionPolicy.to_status_dict()` method should include `compaction_mode`, `cache_friendly_condensation_enabled`, and `cache_ttl_seconds` so operators can verify which mode is active for the current model/provider.

## What Does NOT Change

- `SummaryDAG`, `SummaryNode`, `MessageStore` — DAG structure is identical
- `lcm_grep`, `lcm_expand`, `lcm_describe`, `lcm_doctor` — tool interfaces unchanged
- SQLite schema — no new tables for this feature
- FTS5 search, expansion, retrieval — unchanged
- The existing `cache_friendly_condensation_enabled` and `deferred_maintenance_enabled` global flags remain as backward-compatible defaults when no per-model policy is resolved

## Migration Path

1. **Phase 1 (config only):** Add `compaction_mode`, `cache_ttl_seconds` to `ModelCompactionPolicy`. Add `_DEFAULT_POLICY_PRESETS`. Default behavior unchanged — all existing models get `compaction_mode="inline"` unless their preset says otherwise.
2. **Phase 2 (wiring):** `should_compress_preflight()` and `compress()` consult `policy.compaction_mode`. Deferred mode records debt and processes in `maintain()`.
3. **Phase 3 (cache gate):** Implement `CacheAwareCompactionGate`. Wire `record_cache_write()` into the post-turn hook.
4. **Phase 4 (config):** Add `lcm.model_policies` YAML parsing and `LCM_MODEL_POLICIES` env var parsing.
5. **Phase 5 (testing):** Benchmark both modes on the same conversation traces across Ollama Cloud and Anthropic. Verify token usage reduction on Ollama Cloud, verify cache preservation on Anthropic.

## Motivating Research

- Ollama Cloud pricing page (ollama.com/pricing): "Usage reflects actual utilization of Ollama's cloud infrastructure - primarily GPU time"
- Ollama GitHub issue #15758: "Ollama's Cloud doesn't report number of cached tokens" — always reports 0
- Ollama GitHub issue #16714: "I have benchmarked requests and I am 100% sure that the positive effect that we expect to see from carefully set cache boundaries in agentic loops are not there when using ollama cloud"
- OpenClaw lossless-claw plugin: implements cache-aware deferred compaction as the default mode, with TTL tracking and `maintain()` processing

## Related Code

- `policy.py` — `ModelCompactionPolicy`, `resolve_policy()`, `_DEFAULT_CUTOVER_OVERRIDES`
- `config.py` — `LCMConfig`, `cache_friendly_condensation_enabled`, `deferred_maintenance_enabled`
- `compaction.py` — `CompactionMixin.should_compress_preflight()`, `compress()`
- `engine.py` — `_assemble_context()`, model/provider resolution
- `model_routing.py` — `ModelRoute`, provider resolution

title: [Bug]: GPT-5.6 Codex OAuth live catalog rolled back to 272K; 372K fallback is stale
body:
## Summary

PR #369 changed the GPT-5.6 Codex OAuth cap to 372,000 based on the static `openai/codex` repository catalog. The current authenticated Codex client catalog has since rolled Sol, Terra, and Luna back to:

- `context_window: 272000`
- `effective_context_window_percent: 95`

The public repository copy still says 372,000, so it is currently stale relative to the live catalog delivered to clients.

## Impact

Hermes core currently supplies 272K, so LCM remains safe when that host metadata wins. However, `_CODEX_OAUTH_CONTEXT_CAPS["gpt-5.6"] = 372_000` is now an unsafe fallback whenever host/live metadata is absent, stale, or larger than the actual Codex OAuth limit.

This can cause LCM to defer compression beyond the live route's supported window.

## Reproduction

1. Refresh the authenticated Codex model catalog/cache.
2. Inspect Sol, Terra, and Luna entries: each currently reports 272,000 with a 95% effective window.
3. Call `_codex_oauth_context_cap("gpt-5.6-sol", "openai-codex")` in current Hermes-LCM main.
4. Observe that the helper still returns 372,000.

## Suggested fix

- Restore the conservative GPT-5.6 Codex OAuth fallback to 272,000 until the live catalog re-enables a larger window.
- Prefer live/host metadata when available, but never let a static fallback raise the effective cap above a lower live value.
- Add regression coverage for a live 272K value overriding a stale 372K fallback.

Related:

- #369

title: feat: opt-in active-replay stubbing for externalized textual tool results
body:
# feat: opt-in active-replay stubbing for externalized textual tool results

## Problem

Hermes-LCM already externalizes oversized payloads before SQLite/FTS storage (#139 / #148), and it returns compact active stubs for whole-message generic `raw_payload` externalization (#214). However, ordinary oversized textual tool results remain raw in the provider-facing active replay even after a durable externalized payload and compact stored reference exist.

Current `_ingest_messages()` creates provider replay messages separately from `protect_messages_for_ingest()`. It substitutes the protected content into active replay only for the existing generic `raw_payload` active-stub case. `_assemble_context()` then appends the selected tail and performs tool-pair cleanup, but no textual tool-result stub substitution. This means large tool output can continue to consume the active context, force earlier compaction/eviction, and churn the stable prompt prefix even though lossless recovery is already available through `lcm_expand` / `lcm_describe`.

This is deliberately narrower than #139. Storage externalization is implemented. The missing surface is provider-facing replay of already-durable textual tool results.

## Prior art

Martian-Engineering/lossless-claw implemented this in several layers:

- [#628](https://github.com/Martian-Engineering/lossless-claw/pull/628): replace externalized evictable historical tool-result rows with compact references while preserving tool-call/result pairing, content shape, fresh tail, and drilldown.
- [#862](https://github.com/Martian-Engineering/lossless-claw/pull/862): run the large-tool interceptor on live messages before normal/degraded assembly so current-turn/fallback paths cannot bypass stubbing.
- [#946](https://github.com/Martian-Engineering/lossless-claw/pull/946): do not re-externalize `lcm_describe` drilldown output.
- [#950](https://github.com/Martian-Engineering/lossless-claw/pull/950): recover full live `read` output before externalizing a host-truncated fragment.

Hermes-LCM should reuse its existing externalized payload store and tools rather than port Lossless Claw's storage layer.

## Proposed direction

Add a separate opt-in active-replay policy for oversized textual tool results whose payload has already been externalized durably.

Suggested constraints:

- Default off; no behavior change for existing users.
- Reuse the durable externalized ref produced by ingest protection; do not create a second payload.
- Fail open: if persistence or ref validation fails, retain the original tool result.
- Preserve role, `tool_call_id`, assistant `tool_calls`, ordering, and structured provider content shape.
- Preserve the intentional #226 contract for structured image/media and tool-result media unless explicitly configured otherwise.
- Exempt `lcm_expand` / `lcm_describe` recovery output from immediate recursive re-stubbing, or provide an explicit bounded expansion path.
- Apply consistently to normal active assembly and overflow/degraded fallback paths.
- Make the threshold token-aware if practical; at minimum document its relationship to the current character-based externalization threshold.
- Keep historical backfill/migration a separate, dry-run-first operator surface; future ingest should need no new schema.

## Acceptance criteria

- An oversized textual tool result is stored once as a recoverable externalized payload and appears as a compact provider-facing reference when the new option is enabled.
- The option disabled is byte/structure compatible with current active replay.
- Tool-call/result pairing remains provider-valid.
- Multi-block content remains provider-valid.
- Structured media behavior from #226 remains unchanged.
- Normal assembly and overflow/degraded fallback cannot bypass enabled stubbing.
- `lcm_expand` / `lcm_describe` can recover the full original content, and their recovery response does not enter an accidental stub loop.
- Storage failure leaves the original result inline.
- Focused benchmarks report active prompt tokens saved and assembly latency.

## Non-goals

- Replacing existing Hermes externalization storage.
- Changing compaction policy or implementing sweep compaction in this issue.
- Automatically rewriting existing databases without an explicit backup/dry-run/apply workflow.

title: roadmap: cache-stable tool-output and full-sweep parity with Lossless Claw
body:
## Goal

Bring the highest-value, narrowly portable Lossless Claw behaviors into Hermes-LCM without replacing Hermes-native storage or changing defaults:

1. opt-in provider-facing stubs for durably externalized textual tool results
2. dry-run-first historical sidecar backfill
3. token-bounded protected fresh tails
4. bounded search over externalized payloads
5. bounded atomic threshold full sweeps

We maintain Martian Engineering's Lossless Claw implementation and are porting the proven pattern into Hermes-LCM. The intent is behavioral parity where it materially improves prompt size, recoverability, and cache stability—not a storage-layer or runtime transplant.

## Non-goals

- Replacing Hermes-LCM's existing externalized-payload store.
- Copying Lossless Claw's entire runtime, scheduler, or database schema.
- Enabling new behavior by default in the first PRs.
- Background/deferred compaction; #287 remains the separate async design discussion.
- Duplicating read-tool recovery covered by open PRs #364 and #365.
- Merging, releasing, or changing any live deployment from this tracker.

## Ordered work

- [ ] #374 / #380 — active replay stubbing
- [ ] #377 / #381 — token-bounded fresh tails
- [ ] #376 / #382 — historical externalization backfill
- [ ] #378 / #383 — externalized-payload search
- [ ] #379 / #384 — bounded atomic threshold full sweeps (stacked on #381)

## Acceptance criteria

- Every behavior is default-off or backward-compatible by default.
- Raw message rows and existing DAG lineage remain recoverable.
- Tool-call/result pairing and structured media behavior remain provider-valid.
- Operator mutations are dry-run-first, idempotent, and reversible where safe.
- Full sweeps are bounded by iterations and wall clock and publish one assembled context per invocation.
- Each child issue has a focused PR, tests, docs, and honest validation evidence.
- GitHub Actions is the canonical Python-version validation surface.

## Validation gates

Each PR follows the repository template and, where applicable:

- focused pytest for the changed behavior
- `ruff check .`
- `pytest -q`
- low-file-descriptor pytest
- `python -m compileall -q .`
- script and shell syntax checks
- benchmark/stress smoke
- `git diff --check`
- current-head CI and review-thread readback

## Evidence and provenance

A representative synthetic assembly benchmark for #374 measured **79.78% fewer provider-visible prompt tokens, from 300,288 to 60,709, while the original payload remained recoverable**. This is prompt-assembly evidence, not measured billing savings or an absolute zero-loss claim.

Lossless Claw prior art:

- historical/evictable tool stubs: Martian-Engineering/lossless-claw#628
- live/degraded interception: Martian-Engineering/lossless-claw#862
- recovery recursion guard: Martian-Engineering/lossless-claw#946
- read recovery: Martian-Engineering/lossless-claw#950
- full-sweep redesign: v0.14.0 compaction redesign map

## Stop conditions and rollback

- Stop a child PR if it requires replacing Hermes-native storage, weakens recovery, or changes default behavior without maintainer agreement.
- No PR is a merge or release authorization.
- No live profile/database rollout is part of this tracker.
- Operator backfill retains raw rows and refuses unsafe rollback when a created sidecar is already referenced.

## Current status

All five focused implementation PRs are open. No PR has been merged or released, and none has been installed into the live EVA profile. GitHub created CI runs for all five, but the runs are currently `action_required` with zero jobs because fork-origin workflows await upstream-maintainer approval.

## Exact next action

An upstream maintainer approves the five pending fork-origin CI runs. After jobs complete, address any current-head P0–P2 findings and rerun only changed heads.

title: feat: add dry-run historical tool-output externalization backfill
body:
## Problem

Forward ingest externalization does not pre-create durable sidecars for textual tool-result rows already present in `lcm.db`. Active replay can externalize eligible rows lazily, but a migrated or long-running installation may pay that discovery/write cost during context assembly and may retain a large unprepared historical corpus indefinitely.

Parent tracker: #375

## User or operator impact

Operators with existing LCM history need a bounded, inspectable way to prepare old textual tool outputs for active-replay stubbing without rewriting raw rows, changing DAG lineage, or pointing an ad-hoc migration at a live database.

## Proposed direction

Add a standalone operator script that:

- scans tool-result rows from an explicit target database
- uses the Hermes-native externalized-payload format and deduplication helpers
- defaults to dry run and writes only with `--apply`
- accepts optional session and token-threshold filters
- never rewrites `messages.content`, `messages.tool_calls`, summary nodes, or lifecycle state
- emits a scrubbed manifest containing created refs, content hashes, counts, and token estimates, never raw content
- is idempotent across repeated runs
- supports manifest-based rollback only when file digests still match and no message or summary node references the sidecar
- refuses unsafe rollback rather than deleting a recoverability dependency

This is a prewarm/operator surface for #374, not a new storage layer.

## Alternatives and tradeoffs

- Lazy-only externalization avoids an operator command but moves sidecar creation onto the provider-facing assembly path.
- Rewriting historical message rows would make refs explicit but is materially riskier and unnecessary because Hermes can find sidecars by content/session/tool identity.
- Copying Lossless Claw's blob migration would duplicate storage Hermes already owns.

## Backward compatibility

No schema rewrite and no default runtime behavior change. Dry run is the default. Raw rows remain authoritative and recoverable.

## Validation or evidence

A local migrated profile contained hundreds of eligible historical tool rows; no private rows, session IDs, or raw content will be included in public evidence. Tests will cover dry run, apply, idempotency, manifest safety, referenced-sidecar rollback refusal, missing/corrupt files, and no-row-mutation invariants.

## Implementation status

PR incoming.

## Additional notes

We maintain Martian Engineering's Lossless Claw implementation and are porting the proven operator pattern into Hermes-LCM while retaining Hermes-native storage.

title: feat: cap the protected fresh tail by tokens
body:
## Problem

Hermes-LCM protects the newest raw context by message count only. A small number of very large messages—especially tool results—can dominate that protected tail, reduce assembly headroom, and leave little eligible history for compaction.

Parent tracker: #375

## User or operator impact

A count-only tail is predictable for ordinary chat but not for tool-heavy sessions. Operators cannot bound protected-tail cost without reducing the message count for every session.

## Proposed direction

Add optional `LCM_FRESH_TAIL_MAX_TOKENS`, disabled at `0`/unset, and centralize fresh-tail boundary resolution so assembly, compaction eligibility, rotation/status, and active-replay historical stubbing use the same ordinal.

Semantics:

- `fresh_tail_count` remains the maximum message-count boundary.
- The token cap may move the boundary forward within that count window.
- The newest message is always preserved even when it exceeds the cap.
- The boundary retreats when necessary to preserve a complete assistant tool-call and contiguous tool-result group.
- Existing behavior is byte-compatible when the token cap is disabled.

## Alternatives and tradeoffs

- Lowering `fresh_tail_count` globally is simpler but penalizes ordinary short-message conversations.
- Active tool stubbing reduces the worst tool-output cases but does not bound other oversized fresh messages.
- Allowing the cap to split tool pairs would create provider-invalid replay and is not acceptable.

## Backward compatibility

Default disabled. Existing count-only behavior remains unchanged until explicitly configured.

## Validation or evidence

Tests should cover disabled compatibility, ordinary cap selection, newest-message preservation, oversized messages, assistant/tool grouping, structured tool results, compaction/assembly agreement, status, rotation, and historical-stub boundary agreement.

## Implementation status

PR incoming.

## Additional notes

Prior art: Lossless Claw v0.14 `freshTailMaxTokens`. We maintain Martian Engineering's Lossless Claw implementation and are porting the behavior with Hermes-specific tool-pair safety.

title: feat: add bounded search over externalized payloads
body:
## Problem

Hermes-LCM can describe or expand an externalized payload when its ref is already known, but `lcm_grep` searches message and summary indexes rather than the content stored in externalized JSON sidecars. Once active replay uses more compact refs, unknown details inside those payloads become harder to rediscover.

Parent tracker: #375

## User or operator impact

Recoverability exists, but discovery requires already knowing the ref. Tool-output stubbing is substantially more useful when agents can perform a bounded search and then expand the matching payload intentionally.

## Proposed direction

Extend `lcm_grep` with:

- `content_scope: history | externalized | both`, default `history`
- optional `externalized_refs` restriction
- current-session-only externalized search in v1 so every result remains compatible with existing `lcm_expand(externalized_ref=...)`
- incremental decoding of at most the first 512,000 bytes of each JSON payload's top-level content string
- hard bounds for candidate files, results, and returned characters
- result metadata: ref, tool-call ID, line/byte position, snippet, original size, and scan-truncated flag
- rejection of symlinks, invalid refs, session mismatches, and unsupported cross-session externalized search

The existing history/FTS path remains unchanged when `content_scope=history`.

## Alternatives and tradeoffs

- Indexing all sidecar content in SQLite would speed repeated search but adds schema, synchronization, and backfill complexity.
- Loading whole JSON files is simpler but defeats bounded-memory behavior.
- Returning cross-session refs before cross-session expansion exists creates unusable results, so v1 stays current-session-only.

## Backward compatibility

The default schema behavior and existing result types remain unchanged. New search targets are opt-in.

## Validation or evidence

Tests should cover JSON escapes split across chunks, Unicode, >512K payloads, literal matching, bounded snippets, candidate/result caps, ref filtering, session isolation, symlink/path rejection, malformed files, and `both` result merging.

## Implementation status

PR incoming.

## Additional notes

Prior art: Lossless Claw v0.14 `lcm_grep(scope="files")`. We maintain Martian Engineering's Lossless Claw implementation and are porting the bounded-discovery behavior rather than its storage layer.

title: feat: add bounded atomic threshold full sweeps
body:
## Problem

Hermes-LCM's normal threshold compaction performs one leaf pass when dynamic chunking is disabled, or a bounded set of passes that stops once estimated pressure falls below the trigger when dynamic chunking is enabled. Long sessions can therefore change the prompt prefix at several later threshold events, and a large non-dynamic backlog can be summarized monolithically into the hard output cap.

Parent tracker: #375

## User or operator impact

Operators who prioritize prompt-cache stability cannot currently ask Hermes-LCM to treat the threshold as one bounded compaction boundary: drain the eligible raw prefix in quality-controlled chunks, then condense summarized-prefix pressure, and publish one assembled context.

## Proposed direction

Add opt-in synchronous threshold full sweeps:

- `LCM_THRESHOLD_FULL_SWEEP_ENABLED=false`
- `LCM_SUMMARY_PREFIX_TARGET_TOKENS=0` with a derived target near one leaf budget
- maximum 12 total leaf/condensation passes
- 120,000 ms wall-clock deadline
- repeatedly summarize oldest raw chunks outside the protected fresh tail without stopping merely because estimated pressure falls below the trigger
- always enforce the configured working leaf chunk cap, including when dynamic chunking is disabled
- condense same-depth summaries only when summarized-prefix tokens exceed the target
- treat the existing max depth as the routine preferred depth, with bounded pressure condensation permitted beyond it
- persist each completed DAG/frontier mutation but return one assembled replacement context per invocation
- stop cleanly on deadline, iteration cap, auth/failure, or no token progress and expose telemetry/status

Keep this synchronous and separate from background-compaction proposal #287.

## Alternatives and tradeoffs

- Dynamic leaves reduce monolithic-summary risk but still stop after pressure falls below the trigger and can spread prefix mutations across future turns.
- Deferred maintenance moves latency but creates later-turn prompt mutations and requires a different atomic state-machine design.
- Unbounded sweep loops are unacceptable on the foreground path.

## Backward compatibility

Default off. Existing compaction remains unchanged unless explicitly enabled. Existing leaf size, fan-in, depth, fresh-tail, summarizer fallback, and spend-guard settings are reused.

## Validation or evidence

Tests and benchmarks should cover below-threshold no-op, complete eligible-prefix drainage, final undersized chunks, fixed leaf caps, fresh-tail protection, one returned assembly, summarized-prefix targeting, routine/pressure depth behavior, deadline/iteration/no-progress stops, partial-progress recovery, tool-pair validity, token reduction, summary-call count, latency, and prompt-prefix publication count.

## Implementation status

PR incoming.

## Additional notes

Prior art: Lossless Claw v0.14 full-sweep redesign. We maintain Martian Engineering's Lossless Claw implementation and are porting the bounded threshold behavior without copying deferred scheduling or the Lossless storage/runtime stack.

body:
## Summary - add a **bounded, session-scoped search lane over externalized payloads** to `lcm_grep` via `content_scope: history | externalized | both` - externalized hits merge under an **explicit sort tier**: history results keep their exact current ordering (tier 0, BM25/blended ranks untouched); payload hits follow in tier 1 with byte offset as their native in-tier rank — BM25 ranks and byte offsets are never compared on one scale - auto-discovery is **session-safe under multi-session load**: ownership is probed (bounded at 4,096 metadata probes, truncation reported) **before** the 256 owned-file cap, so a busy shared storage dir can't starve the active session's own payloads - payload reads are **race-hardened**: final-component `O_NOFOLLOW` open (where available) + `os.fstat` regular-file and `(st_dev, st_ino)` identity validation before any read — all reads use the validated descriptor - prefix-bounded content reads (512 KB/file), response char cap, and scan telemetry (`discovery_files`, `discovery_truncated`, rejection counters) in the result payload We maintain Martian Engineering's Lossless Claw and are porting the proven pattern into Hermes-LCM. An agent that remembers "that huge build log had the linker error" has no way to search it without re-expanding payloads into context. payload sidecars)] R -->|bounded prefix search
session-scoped| X classDef hot fill:#b45309,stroke:#7c2d12,color:#fff class R hot ``` Retrieval-only: no ingest, compaction, or assembly behavior changes. ## Validation - [x] focused regressions — **13 passed** (message-only ordering byte-identical between `content_scope=history` and the message subset of `content_scope=both`; synthetic-rank proof that a byte offset of 0 can no longer outrank a history hit; >256 foreign-session-file discovery; path-replacement race rejection) - [x] full `pytest -q` — **1620 passed, 1 skipped, 12 xfailed**; 3 failures are the known macOS baseline (1 tokenizer-dependent + 2 `/var` vs `/private/var`), reproduced identically on the untouched upstream clone at `31675c6` — Linux CI is the canonical gate - [x] `ruff check .` + `git diff --check` — pass - [x] `scripts/validate_release.sh --full --keep-going` — all gates pass (focused pytest 410 passed; benchmark + both stress tiers pass; the two full-suite variants carry only the same three macOS baseline assertions) - [x] rebased onto current `main` (`31675c6`), no conflicts (Fork workflow runs need maintainer approval — validation output above is locally reproducible until then.) ## Notes - Opt-in surface: nothing changes unless a caller passes `content_scope: externalized | both`; `history` (default) is byte-identical to current behavior, regression-proven. - Sort-tier semantics: payload hits deliberately rank below history hits in `relevance`/`hybrid` — they are bulk recovered content, not conversation.
