title: bug(escalation): acceptance gate accepts source-inclusive echoes when source > budget (should enforce token budget)
body:
## Summary

`summarize_with_escalation`'s acceptance gate accepts a summary whenever it is smaller than the **source** (`count_tokens(result) < source_tokens`), not when it fits the requested **budget**. When the source chunk is large, an LLM "summary" that simply echoes the source passes the gate (it is smaller than the source) even though it is many times larger than the `token_budget` the prompt asked for.

## Expected behavior

The accepted summary should be bounded by the `token_budget` (the value the prompt communicates and the caller relies on). A summary that exceeds the budget should be rejected and escalation should proceed to the next level (L2 → L3 deterministic truncation).

## Actual behavior

With a large source chunk (multi-hundred-K to multi-million tokens), the gate `count_tokens(result) < source_tokens` is nearly vacuous — the model's max output (16K-32K tokens) is always smaller than the source, so any model output is accepted regardless of the budget. The stored summary can be ~an order of magnitude larger than the budget the caller intended.

## Repro

A unit-level repro (mocked LLM): `summarize_with_escalation(text=<2.2M-char source>, source_tokens=2_212_704, token_budget=12_000)` with the LLM returning a 100K-token echo:

- **Old gate** (`< source_tokens`): the 100K echo is accepted (100K < 2.2M) → returns `(echo, level 1)` — 8x over budget.
- **New gate** (`<= token_budget`): the echo is rejected → escalates to L2 (also rejected) → L3 deterministic truncation (~512 tokens, bounded).

Observed in production at scale: a widened-compaction path produced 2.2M-token "summaries" that grew the context 10x instead of shrinking it (the anti-growth guard then refused the result, stalling compression entirely).

## Suggested fix

Both acceptance predicates (L1 and L2) should enforce the budget, not the source:

```python
accepts_result=lambda result: count_tokens(result) <= token_budget,   # L1
accepts_result=lambda result: count_tokens(result) <= l2_budget,      # L2
```

PR: https://github.com/stephenschoettler/hermes-lcm/pull/561

## Notes

- The `token_budget` is already the value the L1/L2 prompts communicate ("Target ~{token_budget} tokens"), so this makes the acceptance gate consistent with the prompt contract.
- This is a latent defect in the default (small-window) usage — the model output limit usually keeps summaries under the budget — but it becomes load-bearing for any caller that passes a large source chunk (including the widened-backlog compaction described in #554).
- We run a local variant of hermes-lcm; happy to share details if useful.

Refs #554

title: fix(windows): restore externalization and recovery
body:
## Summary
- skip unsupported parent-directory `fsync` on Windows while retaining the payload-file flush and same-volume atomic replacement
- recover Hermes persisted outputs written with Windows CRLF expansion without changing standalone carriage returns
- add focused Windows CI and document the platform durability/ACL contract

## Why
Windows cannot open a directory through this POSIX `os.open()` path because it requires `FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS`, so externalized-payload writes fail with `PermissionError` after the payload file has already been flushed. Hermes can also report the original LF-based character count while Windows text mode stores CRLF, causing otherwise safe persisted-output recovery to fail.

This carries forward the correct direct guard from draft PR #522 against current `main`, credits that prior work, and adds the missing current-main recovery and CI coverage. It fixes the supported Windows write/replay contract without claiming that POSIX directory-entry durability exists on Windows.

title: fix: remove clock-uniqueness assumptions from storage
body:
## Expected behavior
Persisted identities and ordering should not assume the wall clock advances between adjacent operations:

- every message inserted by `append_batch()` should receive the distinct timestamp promised by its existing regression test;
- repeated externalization of the same content should not collide merely because `time.time_ns()` repeats.

## Actual behavior
On current `main`, the existing 50-row timestamp test fails on Windows with only 2 distinct timestamps. Freezing `time.time_ns()` also makes the second same-content externalization reuse the first filename; the exclusive create fails and externalization falls back inline.

## Minimal reproduction
At `22f6089b6e0f7ef43a787ae91713b6875ee21bb5`:

```text
python -m pytest -q -o 'addopts=' \
  tests/test_lcm_core.py::TestMessageStore::test_append_batch_timestamps_are_unique_per_row

Expected 50 unique timestamps, got 2
```

A deterministic companion regression freezes `time.time()` and `time.time_ns()`; both timestamp uniqueness and filename uniqueness fail on unpatched `main`.

## Proposed scope
- use a compact random suffix rather than `time_ns()` for externalized and temporary payload filenames;
- advance duplicate/non-increasing per-batch timestamps with `math.nextafter()`;
- make both regressions deterministic across platforms.

## Environment
Windows 11, Python 3.11. The frozen-clock reproductions are platform-independent.

## Validation attempted
- Unpatched current-main deterministic regressions: **2 failed**.
- Candidate implementation: **2 passed**; Ruff, compilation, and diff checks passed.

title: fix(storage): remove clock uniqueness assumptions
body:
## Summary

title: Manual state.db recovery replay appends duplicate rows to lcm.db (no replay marker)
body:
## Summary

A manual recovery replay (state.db restore path) re-appends already-persisted rows into `lcm.db` as duplicates — no replay marker or duplicate guard exists for this path. Duplicate counts observed: 124 and 2,530 replay entries for two affected sessions.

## Description

### Background

An earlier incident on the host side caused sessions to go missing from the Hermes instance's `state.db` while their full content remained intact in the LCM database. Recovery was done manually by copying the session rows from `lcm.db` into `state.db`. After that restore, the recovered sessions were replayed/ingested by the host again — and the LCM engine appended **duplicate rows** for those sessions into `lcm.db`.

### Bug

Duplicate rows were written with:
- identical `tool_call_id`s and content as the originals,
- timestamps **after the original session end time** (replay at 22:32 while the original session ended 20:31),
- no flag/marker distinguishing them as replays.

Observed per session: 124 and 2,530 duplicate replay rows.

### Impact

- Duplicate rows pollute `lcm_recall` / retrieval results (same content surfaces multiple times).
- Recovery and cleanup paths become error-prone: without a reliable replay marker, cleanup must rely on heuristics (e.g. "row timestamp after original session end = replay"), which is fragile.

### Expected behavior

A replay/restore of an already-persisted session must not append duplicate rows to `lcm.db` — either the ingest/reconcile layer should recognize already-persisted rows (similar to the partial-turn replay cases) or replayed rows should be marked distinctly (e.g. source/replay flag) so consumers can filter or dedupe them.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent on Linux (v0.21.0), multi-instance setup, WebUI (backend=local)
- hermes-lcm plugin, SQLite-backed (`lcm.db`), host-side SQLite instance state (`state.db`)

## Reproduction

1. Run interactive sessions in an instance (WebUI) so rows exist in `lcm.db`.
2. Lose/swap the instance `state.db` (e.g. restore from backup while Hermes is running).
3. Recover the missing sessions manually: copy rows from `lcm.db` into `state.db` (filtering replays: timestamp <= original session end), fix `sessions.message_count`, verify `messages == messages_fts`.
4. Let the host replay/ingest the recovered sessions again.
5. Inspect `lcm.db` `messages` for those sessions: duplicate rows with identical `tool_call_id`s and timestamps beyond the original session end are present.

## Related

- #513 — reconcile: post-compression replay can re-append an already persisted turn (same replay-guard gap, different trigger: compression mid-turn)
- #437 — fix: reconcile partial tool tail replay after restart (related replay-detection fix)
- NousResearch/hermes-agent#100960 — original incident report; maintainers pointed the `lcm.db` replay-duplicate part here

*Posted by Hermes Agent in collaboration with zunami — knowledge gathered through real-world production operation.*

title: fix: serialize concurrent FTS bootstrap repair
lcm_expand rejects raw user payloads after a same-conversation session rebind
body:
## Problem

`lcm_expand(externalized_ref=...)` (and `lcm_describe(externalized_ref=...)`) reject a raw user payload with

```
Externalized payload <ref>.json not found in current session
```

when the engine has been re-bound to a sibling session of the same conversation after the payload was externalized. The payload file is intact on disk under `lcm-large-outputs/`; only the session-gate in `_get_externalized_payload` rejects it.

### Evidence

Pasted a GitHub issue link in the desktop app; the host externalized my message:

```
[Externalized payload: kind=raw_payload; role=user; chars=21885; bytes=22310; ref=20260903_084418_raw_payload_user_<hash>_<seq>.json]
```

Subsequent tool call on the live engine:

```
WARNING [20260903_035032_21bec3] agent.tool_executor: Tool lcm_expand returned error:
{"error": "Externalized payload 20260903_085029_raw_payload_user_<hash>_<seq>.json not found in current session"}
```

Payload metadata (read directly from disk, still intact):

```json
{"kind": "raw_payload", "role": "user", "session_id": "<writer-session>",
 "content_chars": 21843, "content_bytes": 22268}
```

Session lineage in `lcm.db`:

```
<writer-session>  → conversation_id = <conversation-X>   (81 messages)
<reader-session>  → conversation_id = <conversation-X>   (4 messages)
```

Both sessions belong to the **same conversation**. The ref was captured under the writer session; by the time the model expanded it, the engine was bound to the reader session.

### Root cause

`_get_externalized_payload` (`tools.py`) only allows the payload when `payload.session_id == engine.current_session_id`. Any desktop foreground re-bind between write and expand — same conversation, sibling session — trips the guard.

### Fix direction

Widen the allow-list inside `_get_externalized_payload` to every `session_id` seen under the current `conversation_id` (scoped to `messages.conversation_id`, already indexed). Cross-conversation isolation is preserved — a payload from a different conversation is still rejected. Adds a regression test covering both `lcm_expand` and `lcm_describe`, reproducing the real rebind flow end-to-end.

---

**🛠️ Dev:** Halldrix
**🤖 Sidekick:** Hermes Agent v0.20.5
**🐞 Reproduction:** ✅ Confirmed

title: fix: preserve active context below the compaction threshold
body:
## Summary

Generic non-tool `raw_payload` externalization is durable-storage protection. It now leaves active provider replay text intact until normal compaction rather than hiding an oversized current user message or injected instructions before the configured threshold.

Below-threshold ingest cleanup can sanitize and reassemble context without producing a summary or DAG node. Ordinary replay-diff leaf work follows the configured threshold, measured from both the original and replay views. Manual force, overflow recovery, sensitive filtering, and explicitly enabled tool-result stubbing retain their separate semantics.

An independently eligible, opted-in deferred debt catch-up can run alongside cleanup within its existing `deferred_maintenance_max_passes` budget. This addresses the review finding that repeated cleanup could starve debt maintenance. Disabled maintenance, absent debt, and compression-boundary cooldown still leave that turn cleanup-only.

This intentionally revises the generic-text behavior from #226: durable SQLite/file externalization is unchanged, but generic non-tool text remains provider-visible until normal compaction. This can retain more prompt tokens; the existing threshold and overflow controls remain responsible for context pressure.

title: fix(codex): preserve host context for validated 900k variants
body:
## Summary
- apply a 900K ceiling only to Codex `-900k` variants that Hermes validates, instead of letting LCM's 372K family cap win
- delegate variant eligibility to Hermes' `is_codex_context_variant()` predicate while failing closed on older or broken hosts
- avoid loading the optional host predicate for ordinary model slugs
- add focused routing and engine-level regression coverage

## Why
Hermes now exposes explicit `-900k` Codex aliases for live-verified long-context routes. LCM's independent `"gpt-5.6": 372_000` substring cap also matched `gpt-5.6-sol-900k`, replacing the host-resolved 900,000-token window with 372,000 and triggering compression early.

The plugin should retain its conservative cap for ordinary Codex slugs and invalid aliases, but apply the variant's named 900K ceiling—not the lower family cap—when the host recognises it. This preserves a correctly resolved 900K window while still clamping stale host values above the provider limit. Importing the host predicate lazily preserves compatibility: hosts that do not expose it keep the existing conservative behavior.

This follows the single eligibility authority introduced in NousResearch/hermes-agent commits [`63a9c26`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/commit/63a9c26fbe6ca50138814111c21a4f4550ea85c1) and [`7b89e17`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/commit/7b89e177745fab390d2e7bdbf5e231bf164be24f).

title: feat(amr): Level-1 quote anchors + four-outcome citation verifier
body:
## Summary

Implements the AMR (auditable-memory-records 0.1) **Level-1 slice** for the V4 assertion family, per the public spec: https://github.com/phasespace-labs/auditable-memory-records (SPEC.md §4.2/§5/§6).

- `lcm_assertions` gains `source_quote_hash` (algorithm-prefixed AMR §5 sha256; column CHECK enforces the exact format **including lowercase hex** via `substr` prefix check + negated GLOB on the suffix — note: `GLOB 'sha256:[0-9a-f]*'` alone would NOT enforce case, since SQLite GLOB char classes match a single char followed by any chars) and `epistemic` (closed AMR §4.2 vocabulary: `fact`/`inference`/`open_question`/`unverified`; NULL is the unmarked state — *absent is not fact*, values are case-sensitive, unknown values are **rejected, never coerced**).
- `lcm_assertion_relations` gains `source_quote_hash`.
- **Hash binding is post-digest:** assertion/relation identity digests are unchanged, so existing ids remain stable across the migration and idempotent re-publication stays a zero-write no-op.
- Idempotent in-place migration rebuilds only the two rebuildable quote tables (insert guards temporarily down so already-invalidated generations survive the copy; the re-entrant call of `ensure_assertion_tables` inside the migration is documented in-code and terminates because `_needs_rebuild` is false on re-entry), backfills hashes via AMR §5 normalization (smart punctuation → ASCII, whitespace runs collapsed, trimmed), and preserves every `lcm_assertion_sources` row **including invalidation history**. The exact-shape schema verifier passes for fresh and migrated databases alike.
- New `assertion_amr.py`: read-only verifier reporting the four AMR §6 outcomes (`ok` / `anchor_tampered` / `source_drifted` / `source_missing`) with the §6.1 partial-check signal when no hash is stored. It never mutates state; the existing fail-closed query path is untouched.
- `lcm_query_state` exposes `epistemic` and per-anchor `quote_hash` in `source_ref`; absent values stay explicitly `null` so the unmarked state is visible to consumers.

## Test plan

- 14 new tests (`tests/test_assertion_amr.py`): vocabulary closure, normalization idempotence, anchor format (schema-level defense-in-depth incl. **case enforcement at correct length**), case sensitivity, all four verifier outcomes, migration preservation (invalidated generation + hash backfill), relation anchors, zero-write idempotency.

## Summary

Implements the **is_sufficient gate** half of the 2026-09-03 scout synthesis decision #2 (docs/research/2026-09-03-scout-synthesis.md, Decision Question on evidence sufficiency): a single-place policy that classifies every finished preanswer-evidence result into an explicit sufficiency vocabulary and maps it to one answer-contract policy action.

title: fix(recall): bound FTS arm subdeadline so it cannot starve vector arm…
body:
…s (issue #460)

Issue #460's two coupled failure surfaces:

  (1) comma-laden natural-language queries producing invalid FTS5 syntax
      and falling through to a LIKE full-scan: ALREADY fixed on main by
      PR #168 (b2f228c) and the wave-1 review-finding follow-ups (sanitize
      query + neutralize bare operators + NFC compose + combining-mark
      preservation + allow_operators marker + LIKE judges sanitized
      query + emoji stays on LIKE).

  (2) a slow or failing FTS arm consuming the entire recall deadline
      before summary/chunk arms get a chance, producing
      provenance.arms_run == []: STILL OPEN on main, this fix.

lcm_recall() built one absolute deadline from recall_query_timeout_s and ran the FTS arm first, synchronously, with that deadline. The progress-handler-interrupted LIKE scan still consumed the entire budget, so when the vector-arm gate checked time.monotonic() >= deadline it was true and the summary and chunk arms were skipped.

Fix: give the FTS arm a per-arm deadline of half the configured total budget (fts_arm_deadline = request_started + timeout_s * 0.5). Vector arms keep the original deadline, so total wallclock is still bounded by recall_query_timeout_s. No new config knob; no public surface change; operator-mode semantics preserved (allow_operators=True still flows through unchanged to the FTS arm).

Tests (18 new, 0 regressions):
- test_search_handles_issue_460_reproducer_on_fts_path: the verbatim issue query reaches the FTS path on a row seeded with all sanitized terms.
- test_search_sanitizes_issue_460_punctuation_matrix[8 marks]: the punctuation matrix from the issue (',;:()/..) locks onto FTS.
- test_recall_fts_arm_runs_with_a_bounded_subdeadline: asserts the FTS arm receives a deadline strictly less than the full deadline.
- test_recall_fts_arm_failure_does_not_starve_vector_arms: the FTS arm busy-waits its deadline and returns an error; the summary arm still runs and produces hits.
- test_recall_total_wallclock_stays_within_configured_timeout: with recall_query_timeout_s=0.5 the full call stays bounded.
- test_recall_operator_mode_semantics_preserved_after_scheduling_fix: allow_operators=True still preserves bare AND/OR/NOT/NEAR through the FTS arm.
- test_recall_fts_arm_subbudget_scales_linearly_with_total_timeout[5]: parametrized edge cases at the 0.001 floor and tiny/large budgets; FTS subbudget = half the total at every magnitude.

title: [Feature] Automatic periodic backup of lcm.db with rotation and integrity verification
body:
## Summary

hermes-lcm has manual backup mechanisms (`/lcm backup`, `rotate_backup_database`, `backup_database` in maintenance.py) but no automatic periodic backup. When `lcm.db` becomes corrupted between manual backups, the loss window is unbounded because the current dependency chain is: hermes-lcm saves context → Hermes snapshot (pre-update only, doesn't cover lcm.db) → no net.

## Problem

1. **No automatic trigger**: `backup_database` exists but is only invoked manually (slash command or CLI)
2. **No retention/pruning**: manual backups accumulate unbounded
3. **No integrity verification post-backup**: backup succeeds but may be corrupted without detection
4. **Hermes pre-update snapshot doesn't cover plugin DBs**: The safety net is structurally absent

## Proposed solution

Add automatic periodic backup to the hermes-lcm engine, mirroring existing manual paths:

```yaml
lcm:
  backup:
    enabled: true
    interval_hours: 6          # backup every 6h
    keep_last: 10              # retain N most recent
    dest_dir: /custom/path     # default: engine.backup_dir()
    verify_integrity: true    # PRAGMA integrity_check after backup
```

**Implementation hooks:**
- Hook into existing `maintain` periodic cycle (already runs compaction, rollups, FTS maintenance)
- Reuse existing `backup_database` logic — just add scheduling + pruning
- On corruption detection, attempt auto-restore from most recent valid backup

## Breaking changes
None — opt-in via config, default off.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Backups run automatically every N hours without operator intervention
- [ ] At most `keep_last` files retained in destination dir
- [ ] Failed backup produces a WARNING log; corrupt backup does NOT overwrite valid prior backup
- [ ] `integrity_check` on backup file is skipped/flagged on failure (fail-safe)
- [ ] Backup stores metadata (timestamp, db_size, integrity_status) alongside file

## Environment
- hermes-lcm current line (rc.1+)
- Hermes agent on Linux (WAL mode, ext4)

---
*Note: This issue was filed by GLaDOS, an AI agent assisted by human operator supervision. The goal is to improve robustness of the hermes-lcm plugin for all users by adding automatic backup capabilities.*

title: Repeated below-threshold maintenance hits Hermes would-grow guard without rejection backoff
body:
## Summary

With Hermes Agent v0.21.1 and Hermes-LCM v0.20.0, LCM repeatedly requests below-threshold preflight maintenance, but the host rejects the resulting assembled transcript because it is larger than the input. The installed LCM engine does not implement the rejection/backoff hooks the host uses to prevent repeated ineffective compression.

This produces recurring user-visible warnings:

> Compression refused: the generated summary would have GROWN the conversation instead of shrinking it. No messages were dropped — conversation continues unchanged.

## Environment and scope

- Hermes Agent: `b1f003e18633298d549668b8e186af84cca45b76` (v0.21.1)
- Hermes-LCM: `49e99a272d2d461e5c90732e7ef2bc20e96f0826` (v0.20.0)
- macOS, Telegram gateway, external context engine `lcm`
- Configured compression threshold: 204,000 tokens

These findings apply to the installed versions above. I have not reproduced this against current LCM main (`8d1b1e6d3d63f5fc7b209e8d7ec1dc9b814f2e54`).

## Observed behavior

Production logs show repeated same-session sequences of:

1. `Engine-driven preflight maintenance: lcm requested compress()` below the threshold.
2. Host refusal because the assembled candidate grew.
3. Conversation continues, followed by another maintenance/refusal attempt on a later turn.

Sanitized token-only examples from successive attempts:

| Original transcript | Rejected candidate |
| ---: | ---: |
| 38,186 | 38,621 |
| 38,355 | 38,835 |
| 38,557 | 39,081 |

The final example was triggered at an estimated total prompt size of ~57,332, below the 204,000 threshold. Trigger estimates and transcript estimates are different quantities; the host compares input/output with the same rough estimator.

Some repeats occur on closely spaced interactive turns. Successful shrinking compaction also occurs, so this is not a claim that all LCM compression fails.

## Source findings

At the pinned host revision, `agent/conversation_compression.py`:

- `_automatic_compression_gate_blocks()` (around lines 1306–1315) returns unblocked when the engine lacks `_automatic_compression_blocked`.
- `_salvage_or_refuse_grown_transcript()` (around 2825–2882) checks the fully assembled candidate, attempts mechanical salvage, then refuses growth.
- On refusal it calls `agent.context_compressor.record_rejected_compaction()` inside a swallowed-exception block, explicitly intended to prevent retries on every turn.
- Structural no-op backoff similarly depends on `_record_structural_no_op` being available.

The installed LCM engine and its inheritance chain lack all three hooks. The built-in compressor implements rejection strikes/backoff, but that protection does not apply to this external-engine path.

LCM's own session-boundary carry-over cooldown is a different mechanism and does not record host `would_grow` rejection.

## What is established versus unresolved

**Established:** LCM requests these attempts; the host rejects their larger candidates; the host's intended rejection breaker is not wired for the installed LCM engine.

**Not yet isolated:** the exact source of candidate growth. LCM can reassemble stored DAG summaries plus retained messages, and Hermes subsequently adds todo/user-intent anchoring before the final size check. The warning refers to the whole candidate, not necessarily an oversized newly generated summary.

LCM may persist DAG/frontier updates before the host accepts the transcript. Host rejection preserves the active transcript, but should not be interpreted as proof that plugin storage was unchanged. No data loss or corruption is established by this report.

## Expected behavior / suggested investigation

- Rejected external-engine compaction should trigger bounded, engine-compatible backoff rather than repeated maintenance warnings on unchanged state.
- Real new backlog/context pressure should allow useful work to resume; manual retry semantics should remain explicit.
- Do not remove the host anti-growth safety guard or solve this by discarding protected user context.
- Capture counts at three stages: input → direct LCM return → host-augmented candidate, without logging private content. This should identify which stage grows.
- Verify plugin frontier/storage consistency when the host refuses publication.

This may need a public ContextEngine rejection-feedback contract in Hermes rather than implementing private built-in-compressor methods directly in LCM.

## Regression coverage requested

1. An LCM maintenance candidate grows and is rejected; subsequent unchanged turns do not repeatedly retry immediately.
2. A no-leaf/cleanup-only LCM result becomes larger only after host augmentation and receives the same protection.
3. Useful new backlog or an explicit retry can recover, while the original active transcript remains available after rejection.

## Related

#562 / #561 address summary budget acceptance. This report is adjacent but distinct: small below-threshold candidate growth and missing host-rejection backoff. We have not established that oversized summary generation causes these particular attempts.

Read-only investigation only; no local workaround was applied.

title: fix: enforce preflight compaction threshold
body:
## Summary

- require configured threshold or critical pressure before ordinary eligible-leaf preflight summarization
- retain below-threshold raw backlog as maintenance debt
- publish deterministic replay cleanup below threshold without piggybacking summary work
- clear cleanup-only state before fallible ingest so a failed cleanup cannot poison later threshold compaction

Fixes #496.
Related: #503, #541, #582.

## Production reproduction

With a 1,000,000-token context window and an 850,000-token threshold, released v0.20.0 requested real leaf compaction at approximately 66,256 and 136,193 request tokens. Both created DAG summary nodes. Deferred maintenance was disabled; the trigger was the unconditional eligible-leaf branch in `should_compress_preflight()`.

## Behavioral contract

- ordinary eligible backlog below threshold is ingested and recorded as debt, without a summarizer call
- deterministic cleanup below threshold remains synchronous but cleanup-only
- threshold, configured critical pressure, overflow recovery, and explicit compression remain available
- a failed second ingest cannot leave cleanup-only state armed
- ignored backlog cleanup below threshold cannot piggyback summarization

title: Leaf eligibility and maintenance debt measure the assembled window, not the durable backlog — multi-million-token store backlog goes permanently silent
body:
## Expected behavior

With ~9.9M estimated tokens of unreflected raw messages in the durable store for a session, leaf-compaction eligibility and deferred-maintenance debt should reflect the durable backlog — the engine should keep requesting leaf passes until the store frontier advances.

## Actual behavior

After a healthy leaf pass, the engine went permanently silent for ~24h: no leaf passes, no `Engine-driven preflight maintenance` requests, no maintenance debt recorded — while the session ingested 15,376 more store rows (~5.4M tokens), the session store grew to 22,657 rows / ~9.9M est. tokens, and provider requests climbed to ~804K tokens against a 500K threshold.

The only compression activity was host `in_place_committed` commits preserving message count and shaving ~25K rough tokens each (`chunk_count: 0`). `lcm_status` mid-window reported `last_compression_status: "sanitized"`, `compression_count: 0`, `debt_kind: null`, `debt_size_estimate: 0`, with `debt_updated_at` frozen ~4 days stale and `current_frontier_store_id: 0` / `last_finalized_frontier_store_id: 621905`.

## Root cause

All three gates measure the **assembled context window's middle slice** — `messages[leading_anchor_count : fresh_tail_start]` — never the durable store:

- `_leaf_compaction_candidate_status`: `raw_tokens_outside_tail = count_messages_tokens(middle)` must reach `leaf_chunk_tokens` (200K).
- `_refresh_raw_backlog_debt`: `record_debt` requires the same `_raw_backlog_tokens(messages) >= leaf_chunk_tokens` — so debt can never be recorded from store reality.
- `_should_run_deferred_maintenance`: requires recorded debt → permanently false. `critical_budget_pressure_ratio: 0.0` disables the pressure escape.

Measured from `lcm.db` at quiet-window commits: the window's middle held **~116K** tokens (665-msg list) and **~142K** (821-msg list) vs the 200K bar — flood traffic rows had a median ~21 tokens, so the assembled middle cannot reach the bar while the real backlog lives in the store. The leaf loop exits before any summarizer call, the "sanitized" early return rewrites a few stubs, the host commits in place — silent and correct per current rules.

## Distinct from #441 / #414

There, the count-protected tail swallowed the window (`fresh_tail_start → 0`, `no eligible raw backlog outside fresh tail`). Here the window is healthy — the tail is ~85K of a ~500K request — but the middle stays under `leaf_chunk_tokens` while a multi-million-token durable backlog is invisible. Same window-measurement flaw, fourth variant, and it additionally breaks the debt path, which #441 did not cover.

Related: #553 (closed, unmerged) attacked the same hole from the frontier-advance side. #584 changes below-threshold eligible-leaf work to record debt but still measures the same window.

## Minimal reproduction

1. `LCM_LEAF_CHUNK_TOKENS=200000`, `LCM_FRESH_TAIL_COUNT=128`, `LCM_FRESH_TAIL_MAX_TOKENS=0`, `LCM_CONTEXT_THRESHOLD=0.50`, `LCM_DEFERRED_MAINTENANCE_ENABLED=true`, `critical_budget_pressure_ratio=0.0`, ~1M context window.
2. A long session gets a leaf pass (936 → 130 msgs in the observed case), collapsing the middle.
3. High-rate small-row traffic (tool-heavy loop, median ~21 tokens/store row) regrows the list to ~665 msgs ≈ ~200K message tokens while the host's rough request estimate (including ~300K of system + tool schemas) stays ≥500K.
4. Every `compress()` breaks at `raw_tokens_outside_tail < leaf_chunk_tokens`; `should_compress_preflight` reports nothing to do; the store backlog grows without bound; `debt_kind` stays null.

## Version and environment

hermes-lcm v0.21.0-rc2 (commit `2f590b9`, branch `fix/escalation-acceptance-budget`), Hermes Agent gateway, Telegram DM session, Python 3.12, model `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash` via custom provider, `context_length = 1,000,000`.

## Evidence

`lcm_status` tool output captured mid-window (2026-09-12 12:35, session `20260910_151009_42240006`):

```text
last_compression_status = sanitized
compression_count = 0
dag = {'total_nodes': 2, 'total_tokens': 6016, ... 'source_tokens': 428785}
store = {'messages': 23345, 'estimated_tokens': 9907777}
lifecycle.debt_kind = None
lifecycle.debt_size_estimate = 0
lifecycle.last_finalized_frontier_store_id = 621905
config.leaf_chunk_tokens = 200000
config.deferred_maintenance_enabled = True
config.critical_budget_pressure_ratio = 0.0
config.threshold_full_sweep_enabled = False
session_filters.ignored = False
session_filters.stateless = False
```

Store-side measurement of the window middle at two `in_place_committed` commits:

| commit time | list msgs | tail-128 tokens | middle tokens | leaf bar |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-09-12 07:28 | 665 | ~84.9K | ~116.3K | 200K — under |
| 2026-09-12 12:18 | 821 | ~84.9K | ~142.3K | 200K — under |

Timeline: last leaf pass 2026-09-11 12:45:24 (936 → 130 msgs, 289K → 71K tokens, 1 leaf pass). Next `Engine-driven preflight maintenance` log: none through 2026-09-12 14:00, despite ~15K rows ingested and requests of 665–804K tokens.

## Suggested direction

Measure leaf eligibility and maintenance debt against the **store frontier** — `SUM(token_estimate)` over session rows beyond the coverage/frontier cursor is one indexed query needing no message materialization — while keeping the window measurement for "what is compactable right now." `threshold_full_sweep` (newly enabled) is a partial mitigation for the ≥threshold path but does not record debt. A warn-level host log when the per-turn `compression_attempts` budget exhausts would also have surfaced this hours earlier.

No host or configuration workaround fixes the measurement; the store-vs-window gap is structural.

title: fix: rearm Hermes compaction budget after LCM progress
body:
## Summary

- Report a changed compaction result through the progress flag that Hermes reads before it commits the transcript.
- Consume the host's verification flag on the next foreground usage update. Clear both flags on session reset.
- Add a regression test that completes five LCM compactions in one host turn, plus tests for unchanged results, errors, missing/high usage, auxiliary usage, and session reset.

## Why

Hermes limits a turn to three compaction attempts until a completed compaction is followed by a provider prompt below the threshold. LCM successfully reduces the transcript but does not set `_last_compression_made_progress`, so the host never arms `_verify_compaction_cleared_threshold` and never resets its attempt counter. After three successful passes, automatic compaction stops for the rest of a long tool turn and context keeps growing.

The new long-turn test fails on unchanged `main` when the fourth compaction is blocked. With this change, all five passes complete. Cleanup, overflow recovery, and delegated compaction also qualify when they change the returned transcript; the host still requires provider usage below the threshold before it resets the counter.

## Validation

- [x] Focused regression: `tests/test_host_compaction_budget.py` -> 8 passed. The five-compaction regression was also observed failing on unchanged `main`.
- [ ] Default validation:
  - [ ] `pytest tests/test_lcm_core.py tests/test_lcm_engine.py tests/test_packaging_install.py -q` plus the new regression file -> 1,103 passed, 2 skipped, 13 failed on Windows. All 13 failures were reproduced on unchanged `main` at `8d1b1e6`.
  - [ ] `pytest -q` -> 2,955 passed, 24 skipped, 12 xfailed, 59 failed on Windows. All 59 failed cases were rerun on unchanged `main` and failed there too.
  - [ ] `scripts/validate_release.sh --full --keep-going --output <temporary-directory>` -> completed with the baseline pytest failures. The low-FD test pass has the same counts. Dependency, compile, shell syntax, benchmark smoke, stress smoke, and release stress gates pass.
  - [x] `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD`, `git diff --check`, and `git diff --cached --check` -> pass.
- [x] `python -m ruff check .` -> pass.
- [ ] Workflow validation: not applicable; no workflows changed.

## Notes

Tests use the repository's standalone ContextEngine helper, a temporary profile and database, and a deterministic summary stub. No provider calls or live profile changes are required. The host-contract test uses the real LCM engine with the Hermes commit/usage gates; it does not claim an end-to-end model run.

The broader suite failures are in existing Windows path, POSIX file-permission, import, and shell/install checks. All 59 failed full-suite cases also fail on unchanged `main`; no changed-head-only failure was found. The release script also reports a Git-status change because this unchanged patch was committed while validation ran. The final checkout is clean and all three diff checks pass.

The same source patch was applied to an isolated copy of the installed `0.21.0-rc2` revision (`10cbb783`): all eight regression cases pass there as well. Live installed files were not changed for these tests. This PR does not change MoA token accounting or the host attempt cap.

title: SQLite permission helpers drop active POSIX locks, reproducing deleted WAL/SHM handles and disk I/O errors
body:
## Summary

We observed recurring LCM initialization failures in a running Hermes deployment:

```text
Context engine 'lcm' could not be safely copied for this agent
(disk I/O error) — falling back to built-in compressor.
```

Inspection showed that long-lived service processes still held open file descriptors to deleted `lcm.db-wal` and `lcm.db-shm` files, while a different WAL file existed at the normal pathname.

We then reproduced the same deleted-sidecar state and subsequent `disk I/O error` using the **unmodified LCM permission helpers** against small disposable databases.

## Environment

- LCM commit: `8d1b1e6d3d63f5fc7b209e8d7ec1dc9b814f2e54`
- LCM working tree: clean
- Python: `3.11.15`
- SQLite: `3.53.1`
- Platform: Linux
- Database mode: WAL

The reproduction used the installed Hermes Python runtime and directly imported LCM's `sqlite_util.py`. It did not initialize the full plugin or access production databases. The implicated `open` / `fchmod` / `close` sequence is also present in upstream `main` at the time of filing.

## Observed production behavior

- Gateway, Dashboard and WebUI held descriptors to deleted LCM WAL/SHM files.
- A different, empty `lcm.db-wal` existed at the normal pathname.
- No matching LCM POSIX locks were visible for those processes in `/proc/locks` during inspection.
- The same service processes remained running across the observed recurrence; no service restart was involved.
- Creating a new LCM instance failed with `disk I/O error`.
- Manual compression still completed successfully through the built-in `ContextCompressor`, rather than LCM.

## Relevant code paths

In `sqlite_util.py`, `_chmod_sqlite_artifact_at()` performs:

```python
fd = os.open(...)
os.fchmod(fd, 0o600)
os.close(fd)
```

Both `_prepare_private_sqlite_file()` and `_restrict_existing_sqlite_artifacts()` use this helper for the database and existing sidecars, including WAL and SHM.

Relevant call sites at the tested commit:

- [`sqlite_util.py:66–120`](https://github.com/stephenschoettler/hermes-lcm/blob/8d1b1e6d3d63f5fc7b209e8d7ec1dc9b814f2e54/sqlite_util.py#L66-L120): artifact permission helper.
- [`store.py:121–130`](https://github.com/stephenschoettler/hermes-lcm/blob/8d1b1e6d3d63f5fc7b209e8d7ec1dc9b814f2e54/store.py#L121-L130): storage preparation invokes `_prepare_private_sqlite_file()`.
- [`store.py:357–362`](https://github.com/stephenschoettler/hermes-lcm/blob/8d1b1e6d3d63f5fc7b209e8d7ec1dc9b814f2e54/store.py#L357-L362): `MessageStore._init_db()` opens the SQLite connection, configures it, then invokes `_restrict_existing_sqlite_artifacts()`.
- [`engine.py:625–683`](https://github.com/stephenschoettler/hermes-lcm/blob/8d1b1e6d3d63f5fc7b209e8d7ec1dc9b814f2e54/engine.py#L625-L683): per-agent cloning constructs new storage helpers while the hosting process can retain existing connections.

SQLite documents that closing a separate file descriptor in the same process can cancel POSIX advisory locks held by SQLite on that file:

[SQLite documentation: POSIX advisory locks canceled by a separate thread doing close()](https://sqlite.org/howtocorrupt.html#_posix_advisory_locks_canceled_by_a_separate_thread_doing_close_)

## Reproduction procedure

Each test used a newly created temporary database:

1. Open a SQLite connection in process A.
2. Enable WAL, create a table, insert a row and commit. Keep the connection open.
3. Record the process's DB/SHM locks using `/proc/locks`.
4. Invoke one of the original LCM permission helpers in process A.
5. Record the locks again.
6. Start an independent Python process B, which opens the same database, executes a `SELECT`, and closes its connection normally.
7. Inspect process A's descriptors for deleted WAL/SHM files.
8. Insert and commit another row through A's existing connection.
9. Open a fresh connection and query the database.

The procedure did **not** manually unlink sidecars, restart services, delete backups or use production data.

## Results

Each variant was run three times:

| Variant | Runs | DB/SHM locks dropped from 2 to 0 | Deleted WAL/SHM handles | Fresh connection I/O error |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| No permission helper | 3 | 0/3 | 0/3 | 0/3 |
| `_prepare_private_sqlite_file()` | 3 | 3/3 | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| `_restrict_existing_sqlite_artifacts()` | 3 | 3/3 | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| Path-based chmod without additional open/close, diagnostic control only | 3 | 0/3 | 0/3 | 0/3 |

In the affected variants:

- Process B completed normally.
- Process A retained descriptors to deleted WAL/SHM files.
- The subsequent write through A's existing connection reported success.
- The fresh connection failed with:

```text
disk I/O error
SQLITE_IOERR_SHORT_READ
Extended error code: 522
```

In an initial variant without the subsequent write through A, deleted sidecars were already observable while fresh reads still succeeded.

The chmod-only variant was used solely as an experimental control, not as a proposed implementation change.

## Related reports

The [concurrent-startup report in #480](https://github.com/stephenschoettler/hermes-lcm/issues/480#issuecomment-5600030651) already identifies the artifact-permission pass as a relevant surface and reports a control with that pass disabled. It explicitly leaves the exact kernel/SQLite primitive unproven. This report adds a smaller helper-level reproduction measuring POSIX lock loss, subsequent deleted WAL/SHM descriptors, and a delayed fresh-connection I/O error.

#463 concerns clone-related file-descriptor multiplication/exhaustion. The experiment here does not require descriptor exhaustion or a large number of clones.

title: fix: resolve macOS APFS concurrency corruption, increase lock timeouts, and add FTS self-healing
body:
## Summary

This PR addresses database corruption (`database disk image is malformed`) and concurrency contention under multi-process environments on macOS (APFS), adds automatic self-healing for corrupted FTS5 shadow indexes, increases connection busy timeouts, and isolates test runs from user production databases.

## Problem Statement & Root Cause Analysis

In real-world setups running Hermes with concurrent processes (e.g., the supervised Hermes Gateway, the desktop Electron backend `hermes serve`, subagent runners, and CLI invocations), the SQLite database `lcm.db` periodically suffered corruption (`DatabaseError: database disk image is malformed`) during concurrent turn compactions.

Investigation identified four distinct failure modes:

1. **APFS Page Cache Incoherence via `PRAGMA mmap_size` on Darwin:**
   `db_bootstrap.py` configured `PRAGMA mmap_size = 268435456` (256 MiB) unconditionally. On macOS APFS, SQLite memory-mapped reads (`mmap`) combined with multi-process writes cause known page-cache incoherencies between processes sharing the same WAL file, leading SQLite to read out-of-sync B-tree frames and report `database disk image is malformed`.
2. **Hardcoded 5-Second Connection Timeouts:**
   Several stores (`store.py`, `dag.py`, etc.) hardcoded `sqlite3.connect(..., timeout=5.0)`. During deep compactions or heavy write bursts, concurrent readers/writers timed out after only 5 seconds, precipitating transaction rollback races.
3. **Missing FTS Self-Healing in Summary DAG & Shadow Index Desynchronization:**
   While `store.py` had partial handling, `dag.py` had no catch-and-retry logic for FTS index corruption during summary node insertion. Additionally, `repair_external_content_fts()` skipped deep structural rebuilds if external content table row counts matched.
4. **Test Suite Pollution of Production Databases:**
   Running `pytest` without explicit `HERMES_HOME` redirection defaulted to writing to and altering `~/.hermes/lcm.db`, risking production data integrity during local testing.

## Proposed Changes

### 1. Darwin APFS Hardening (`db_bootstrap.py`)
- Default `PRAGMA mmap_size = 0` on `sys.platform == "darwin"` to force POSIX `pread`/`pwrite` through the unified kernel buffer cache, eliminating APFS memory-map cache tearing.
- Allow environment override via `LCM_MMAP_SIZE`.
- Introduce `SQLITE_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS` / `SQLITE_BUSY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (defaulting to 30s/60s via `LCM_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS`).
- Add `force: bool = False` parameter to `repair_external_content_fts()` to enable deterministic unconditional FTS shadow-table rebuilds.

### 2. Lock Timeout Harmonization & FTS Self-Healing (`store.py`, `dag.py`, & stores)
- Upgrade `timeout=5.0` to `SQLITE_BUSY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` across `store.py`, `dag.py`, `lifecycle_state.py`, `query_view_store.py`, `rollup_store.py`, and `vector_store.py`.
- Wrap single and batch message insertions (`store.py`) and summary node insertions (`dag.py`) with automatic FTS error detection (`is_fts_corruption_error`). On failure, the store triggers a targeted `repair_external_content_fts(..., force=True)` and transparently retries the operation, preventing turn failures.

### 3. Graceful Compaction Fallback (`compaction.py`)
- Catch `sqlite3.DatabaseError` during compaction runs and gracefully delegate to `_compress_lcm_bypassed_session()`, ensuring agent turns never crash mid-conversation if a transient storage error occurs.

### 4. Test Suite Isolation & Regression Tests (`tests/conftest.py`, `tests/test_crash_safe_wal.py`)
- Added session-scoped autouse fixture `isolate_test_hermes_home` in `conftest.py` ensuring all tests execute in an isolated temporary directory.
- Added 19 comprehensive unit tests in `tests/test_crash_safe_wal.py` covering:
  - Darwin `mmap_size` defaults and environment variable overrides.
  - Busy timeout propagation across all store constructors.
  - Multi-process concurrent read/write stress without corruption.
  - FTS self-healing recovery during interrupted batch inserts.

## Verification & Validation

1. **Unit Test Suite:**
   `pytest tests/test_lcm_core.py tests/test_lcm_engine.py tests/test_crash_safe_wal.py tests/test_packaging_install.py`
   -> **1,128 passed, 1 skipped** (100% pass rate).
2. **Stress Check:**
   `scripts/lcm_stress_check.py --scenario concurrent_read_write_smoke` executed with 0 failures.
3. **Production Validation:**
   Tested live on macOS Darwin 24.x (APFS) with active Gateway and concurrent background tasks:
   - Processed >3,200 messages and >20 compactions over a 1.5-hour burn-in window.
   - `PRAGMA integrity_check` verified completely clean (`ok`).

---

### 🤖 Attribution & Verification Disclaimer

*This bug analysis, hardening patch, and regression test suite were developed with the assistance of **Google Antigravity (Gemini 3.8 Flash Thinking / High)**. All code modifications, test suites, and concurrency edge cases were reviewed, manually verified, and stress-tested in a live multi-process production environment on macOS (APFS) prior to submission.*

title: Epic: Eliminate subthreshold sanitation-driven context loss
body:
## Goal
Eliminate automatic lossy foreground-context reduction caused by Hermes-LCM replay sanitation below the effective automatic compaction floor, while preserving first-time sensitive sanitation, threshold/critical-pressure compaction, explicit manual compression, provider-overflow recovery, prompt caching, and session integrity.

## Verified production evidence
Affected Work conversation: `agent:main:slack:group:TD2ATF9DY:C0BN11SHC86`, session `20260911_183828_4f5c57`.

Automatic requests below the configured 850K threshold occurred on Sep 14 at approximately 354K, 192K, and 160K. Replay cleanup returned true before threshold policy because the canonical replay contained changed sensitive-redaction placeholders. Hermes then entered generic compression; two cleanup-only passes had no DAG work but invoked salvage and committed a smaller active transcript.

## Architecture decision
Ship the smallest compatible two-repository fix first:

1. Hermes-LCM: complete PR #584 policy, gate ignored backlog, make pure sanitation status unambiguous, and prove full-pipeline sanitation convergence.
2. Hermes core: add a sanitation-aware commit path with bounded placeholder growth and no generic salvage/todo/user/memory side effects.
3. Deploy as a compatible pair with Hermes first or atomically; qualify on Work before Home.

The public typed decision protocol and durable transcript CAS remain separate follow-up tracks. They do not block the incident fix.

## Execution order
- [ ] #591 — P0 preserve evidence and rescue deployed patch provenance
- [ ] #592 — P1 Hermes-LCM sanitation convergence and policy
- [ ] NousResearch/hermes-agent#111242 — P2 Hermes sanitation-aware commit
- [ ] #593 — P3 paired Work deployment and qualification
- [ ] NousResearch/hermes-agent#111243 — P4 typed context-engine protocol follow-up
- [ ] NousResearch/hermes-agent#111244 — P5 durable transcript CAS follow-up

## Cursor handoff
Each child is independently buildable by Cursor and includes exact source areas, tests, safety constraints, dependencies, and completion evidence. Cursor must inspect current upstream source and prove invariant tests RED before implementation. Do not blindly apply automated review suggestions or merge community PRs.

## Required runtime acceptance
- existing affected session remains stable;
- sanitation converges after one adoption;
- no summary/DAG/salvage/unrelated tool clearing for sanitation;
- goal continuation and concurrent/background traffic remain correct;
- one pinned 1M route reaches a provider-reported 600K+ prompt;
- declared effective automatic floor behaves as configured;
- provider overflow and manual compression remain functional;
- no context loss, unexpected rollover, restart, OOM, Xid, EngineDead, DB/FTS failure, or prompt-cache churn loop.

## Safety and non-goals
- No disabling sensitive protection, LCM, or compression globally.
- No context-window disguise or leaf-size-only workaround.
- No production mutation from issue creation.
- No raw credentials or sensitive payloads in fixtures, logs, issues, or telemetry.
- No bundling the CAS program into the initial incident fix.

title: P1: Make replay sanitation convergent and gate all noncritical subthreshold maintenance
body:
## Goal
Make Hermes-LCM replay sanitation terminal and convergent while preventing every noncritical summary-producing maintenance path from running below the effective automatic floor.

## Architecture decision
Rebase and update self-authored PR #584 rather than layering another predicate-specific hotfix. Keep its cleanup-only handoff and threshold policy, then add the missing ignored-backlog gate, unambiguous operation status, and full ingest→replay→adopt→re-ingest convergence.

## Verified source areas
- `compaction.py::should_compress_preflight`
- `compaction.py::_replay_diff_requests_ingest_cleanup`
- `compaction.py::_compress_impl`
- `engine.py::_redact_active_replay_messages`
- `ingest_protection.py::{redact_sensitive_text,redact_sensitive_value}`
- `sanitize.py::_contains_sensitive_redaction`
- relevant engine, replay, stubbing, and sensitive-ingest tests

## Required behavior
1. Below-floor replay cleanup enters the pure sanitation-only path.
2. `sanitized` is emitted only for pure deterministic sanitation. No-leaf scaffold/prefix reassembly must use a distinct status.
3. Ignored backlog below the floor records/defer work; it cannot invoke summary compaction until the floor or declared critical pressure is reached.
4. Manual force, provider-confirmed overflow, threshold, and critical-pressure paths remain intact.
5. One-shot sanitation state is cleared before fallible ingest and cannot hijack a later manual/threshold attempt.
6. The complete sanitation pipeline converges: after one host-shaped adoption, second replay is byte-identical and second preflight is false.
7. Positive preflight decisions emit low-cardinality operation/reason logs without content.

## Cursor implementation plan
1. Fetch current upstream main and rebase the PR #584 branch.
2. Inspect the current implementation; do not assume older line numbers remain valid.
3. Add invariant tests first and prove them RED on the rebased base.
4. Implement vertical slices:
   - pure sanitation status split;
   - ignored-backlog floor gate;
   - stale-flag abort safety;
   - pipeline convergence.
5. Build production-shaped sanitized fixtures covering:
   - quoted/unquoted spans;
   - short protected values with longer placeholders;
   - scalar/list/dict/key/JSON-string/tool-call/tool-result forms;
   - content vs tool-call JSON parsing;
   - active vs durable externalized representation;
   - restart;
   - adjacent sensitive text;
   - valid-looking and malformed quoted placeholders;
   - multiple placeholders.
6. If needed, add a provenance-checked metadata-insensitive placeholder-equivalence backstop. Both sides must be structurally valid engine placeholders for the same pattern; bare substring resemblance is insufficient.
7. Run focused/full suites, Ruff, compileall, diff checks, DB/FTS leakage checks, and inspect the full diff.

## Safety
- Do not disable sensitive patterns, LCM, compression, or overflow protection.
- Do not expose raw secrets in tests, logs, commits, or issue comments.
- Do not change production config or restart services.
- Do not add a new behavioral env var.
- Keep manual `/compress` and provider overflow semantics.
- No schema migration without backward-read support.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Every new invariant test is observed RED on upstream base.
- [ ] First sanitation adoption is exact and safe.
- [ ] Second and later replay are byte-identical; second preflight is false.
- [ ] Sanitation performs no summary-model call, leaf pass, condensation, or DAG write.
- [ ] `sanitized` cannot describe reassembly/summary work.
- [ ] Ignored backlog obeys the effective floor.
- [ ] Eligible backlog below floor remains deferred debt.
- [ ] Manual, threshold, critical-pressure, overflow, cooldown, and failed-ingest cases pass.
- [ ] Aborted preflight cannot poison the next operation.
- [ ] Raw sensitive values are absent from DB, FTS, logs, and telemetry.
- [ ] Full prescribed test/lint/compile/diff gates pass.
- [ ] Only task-scoped files changed.

## Completion evidence
Commit SHAs, RED/GREEN output, full-suite output, leakage checks, exact diff, and PR URL. Do not merge or deploy.

## Non-goals
- Hermes host commit behavior is tracked separately.
- Public typed context-engine protocol is a follow-up.
- Durable transcript CAS is a follow-up.

## Related
Parent epic: #590
Depends on: #591
Related upstream: #496, #582, PR #541, PR #584.

title: P3: Deploy and qualify the compatible Hermes/LCM sanitation fix on Work
body:
## Goal
Deploy the compatible Hermes/LCM sanitation fix to Work with rollback, then prove it under real foreground, goal, concurrent, long-context, threshold/critical-pressure, overflow, and manual-compression workloads before considering Home rollout.

## Prerequisites
- P0 provenance/evidence complete.
- Hermes-LCM implementation issue complete and reviewed.
- Hermes core sanitation-aware issue complete and reviewed.
- Cross-repo integration fixture green.
- Exact compatible commit pair approved by Devin.

## Deployment decision
Deploy Hermes first or both components atomically. Never leave new LCM paired with old Hermes. Roll back as a pair, or Hermes last.

## Preparation
1. Record live SHAs, service PID/start time, config, effective `LCM_*` environment, session routes, and DB integrity.
2. Back up source and patch manifests with hashes.
3. Confirm approved branches are pushed and clean.
4. Validate in a shadow profile or isolated gateway first.
5. Define a proven out-of-band restart executor and bounded automatic rollback.
6. Record the effective automatic floor: `min(threshold_tokens, critical_ratio × context_length)`.
7. Pin and record the intended 1M model route for long-context qualification.

## Runtime qualification

### Existing affected session
- Continue Slack conversation `C0BN11SHC86` on the same active session.
- Exercise representative tool-heavy work without reset or rollover.
- Provider prompt grows from the post-damage baseline.

### Sanitation convergence
- Use synthetic sensitive-shaped values only.
- First sanitation adoption is exact and safe.
- Second, third, and later replay remain byte-identical through the host commit path.
- No repeat sanitation commit without new sensitive-bearing content.
- No summary call, DAG delta, salvage, memory extraction, or unrelated tool clearing.
- Prompt cache may break once; subsequent turns recover and remain stable.

### Goal continuation
- Reach a bounded goal continuation.
- One logical generation; no replay-driven compaction.

### Concurrent/background activity
- Foreground turn plus background review and another channel.
- No stale commit, message loss, duplicate active generation, or repeated sanitation.
- A valid watermark is captured for every sanitation commit.

### Natural 600K+ growth
- Pin the 1M route throughout.
- Require a provider-reported prompt ≥600K in one stable foreground Slack session.
- Any fallback/route change invalidates the run.
- No automatic compaction below the declared effective floor.

### Effective floor
Current ratio 0.8 means an 800K floor on the 1M route. Choose explicitly:
- retain 0.8 and expect/test critical compaction near 800K; or
- separately approve ratio ≥0.85 and test the critical valve independently.

### Provider overflow
- Isolated route/profile.
- Provider-confirmed overflow below local estimate.
- Bounded recovery, stable session, no message loss.

### Manual compression
- Explicit `/compress` below floor.
- Manual reason; no sanitation misclassification.

### Archive/cache/health audit
- Every in-place commit maps to threshold, critical pressure, manual, provider overflow, or first-time sanitation.
- Preflight, salvage, finish, and provider token measurements identify their basis.
- No gateway restart, OOM, Xid, EngineDead, unexpected rollover, DB/FTS failure, cache/reaper corruption, or role/tool-pair breakage.

## Rollback triggers
- second sanitation commit for unchanged logical input;
- sensitive leakage;
- sanitation invokes salvage or unrelated tool clearing;
- summary work below floor outside declared critical-pressure/overflow/manual policy;
- stale or duplicate generation publication;
- missing watermark;
- model-route drift;
- gateway fails to reconnect;
- DB/FTS integrity failure.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Shadow qualification passed.
- [ ] Approved compatible pair deployed in safe order.
- [ ] Existing affected session passed.
- [ ] Sanitation convergence passed.
- [ ] Goal and concurrency tests passed.
- [ ] Provider-reported 600K+ stable foreground prompt reached.
- [ ] Effective floor behavior matched declared policy.
- [ ] Overflow and manual compression passed.
- [ ] Archive/cache/health audit clean.
- [ ] Rollback was rehearsed or dry-run verified.
- [ ] Devin approved Work promotion before any Home rollout.

## Safety
- Production deployment and restart require explicit Devin approval in this issue.
- Do not restore archived context into affected sessions.
- Do not alter Bifrost.
- Do not disable sensitive protection or compression.
- Preserve evidence and rollback artifacts.

## Completion evidence
Loaded SHAs, exact ET timestamps, service health, session IDs, provider usage, cache ratios, DAG deltas, logs, DB integrity, and rollback status.

Depends on LCM issue #592 and Hermes issue NousResearch/hermes-agent#111242.

title: Fix subthreshold replay sanitation and compaction policy
body:
## Problem
Hermes-LCM can request replay cleanup below the effective automatic compaction floor. Existing direct and host callers may then run summary-producing compaction or conflate pure sanitation with reassembly.

Internal tracking: Apple-Federal-Credit-Union/marvin#72.

## Changes
- Gate ordinary eligible-leaf, ignored-backlog, and deferred maintenance below the effective floor while preserving critical pressure, threshold, manual, and overflow paths.
- Make replay sanitation terminal and convergent.
- Distinguish pure `sanitized` output from `reassembled` output.
- Bind cleanup handoffs to session/message/replay identity.
- Add an opaque one-shot sanitation claim protocol for compatible hosts while preserving safe direct-caller behavior.
- Add content-free reason telemetry and production-shaped leakage/convergence tests.

## Verification
- New invariant tests observed RED before implementation.
- Target sanitation/active-tool tests: 65 passed.
- Core/engine/packaging: 1,114 passed.
- Additional focused: 203 passed.
- Leakage: 72 passed.
- Final parent focused rerun: 55 passed.
- Ruff, compileall, and diff checks passed.
- Cross-repository Hermes/LCM fixture passes on the paired Hermes branch.

## Safety
- Does not disable sensitive-pattern protection, LCM, compression, critical pressure, manual compression, or overflow recovery.
- Contains synthetic values only; no production secrets or PII.

title: fix: add _coerce_threshold_tokens_cap and threshold_tokens_cap to LCMEngine
body:
## Problem

The TUI gateway's live compression config sync (`tui_gateway/session_compression.py:_sync_live_compression`) calls these on the context engine object:

```python
cc.threshold_tokens_cap = cc._coerce_threshold_tokens_cap(compression.get("threshold_tokens"))
cc._threshold_tokens = cc._tail_token_budget = None
```

These attributes/methods exist on Hermes core's `ContextCompressor` but **not** on `LCMEngine` (which inherits from `ContextEngine` ABC instead). Every live compression config sync emits:

```
WARNING tui_gateway.server: Could not apply live compression config for <session>: 'LCMEngine' object has no attribute '_coerce_threshold_tokens_cap'
```

This warning fires on every Desktop/TUI session start when compression config is applied live.

## Fix

Adds the missing compatibility surface to `LCMEngine`:

1. **`_coerce_threshold_tokens_cap` static method** — mirrors `ContextCompressor._coerce_threshold_tokens_cap` (= `_coerce_max_tokens`): normalizes a value to a positive int or `None`.
2. **`threshold_tokens_cap` instance attribute** — initialized to `None` in `__init__`, reset to `None` in `_set_context_length`'s zero-path.
3. **`_threshold_tokens` and `_tail_token_budget` instance attributes** — cached trigger state invalidated after a config sync, same purpose as `ContextCompressor._threshold_tokens` / `_tail_token_budget`.

No behavioral change to LCM compaction itself — these are passive compatibility attributes that `session_compression.py` reads/writes during live config sync.

## Testing

Verified against Hermes Agent v2.3.0 with `tui_gateway/session_compression.py` line 148. The warning disappears after applying this patch.

```bash
# Before: every session start
WARNING tui_gateway.server: Could not apply live compression config for ac19d5a9: 'LCMEngine' object has no attribute '_coerce_threshold_tokens_cap'

# After: no warning
```

title: fix: honor Hermes SQLite journal mode
body:
## Summary

- Delegate LCM SQLite journal-mode selection to Hermes' canonical `apply_wal_with_fallback()` helper when available.
- Apply `wal_autocheckpoint` and `journal_size_limit` only when the effective mode is `wal`.
- Preserve the existing WAL bootstrap as a compatibility fallback for older hosts and standalone plugin tests.
- Add regression coverage for both `wal` and `delete`, and update the host dependency contract.

## Why

With Hermes configured with `database.journal_mode=delete`, `state.db` correctly remained in DELETE mode, while `lcm.db` was changed back to WAL by `db_bootstrap.configure_connection()`. During the reproduced incident, Dashboard alone could retain deleted `lcm.db-wal` and `lcm.db-shm` file handles.

After delegating journal-mode selection to Hermes, Dashboard + Gateway + WebUI were restarted together and `lcm.db` remained in DELETE mode, `PRAGMA quick_check` returned `ok`, and no deleted LCM handles were present.

When Hermes selects WAL, LCM retains its existing durability and hygiene pragmas: `synchronous=FULL`, `wal_autocheckpoint=500`, `journal_size_limit=67108864`, and `mmap_size=268435456`.

## Validation

- [x] `pytest tests/test_crash_safe_wal.py -q` — 17 passed
- [x] Targeted dependency and SQLite tests — 93 passed
- [x] `ruff check --no-cache db_bootstrap.py tests/test_crash_safe_wal.py tests/test_dependency_contract.py`
- [x] `python scripts/validate_dependency_contract.py`
- [x] `git diff --check`
- [ ] `pytest -q` — 3029 passed, 2 skipped, 12 xfailed, 2 failed. The same two failures reproduce on clean `origin/main` on macOS and are caused by `/var/...` versus `/private/var/...` path aliases in `test_path_containment_within_allowed_base` and `test_configured_externalization_path_inside_allowed_base_accepted`.

## Notes

- The compatibility fallback preserves current WAL behavior on older Hermes hosts that do not expose `hermes_state_wal`.
- The dependency contract was incremented from 1.0.4 to 1.0.5 because the repository requires every scanned runtime host import to be declared.
- No unrelated files are changed.

title: fix: keep SQLite POSIX locks while restricting artifact permissions
body:
## Summary
- `_chmod_sqlite_artifact_at()` now **returns early when an artifact is already mode `0600`**. It opens nothing, so the steady state never releases locks on any POSIX platform.
- When an existing artifact **does** need tightening and `O_PATH` plus `/proc/self/fd` are available (Linux), it changes permissions through an `O_PATH` descriptor's `/proc/self/fd/N` link instead of a regular read/write descriptor. Closing an `O_PATH` descriptor releases no POSIX locks.
- The no-follow, `(st_dev, st_ino)` identity, link-count and sidecar-disappearance checks are unchanged on both paths. Creating a new file (`O_CREAT | O_EXCL`) and platforms without `O_PATH` keep the existing regular-descriptor path.
- Adds regression tests. The existing symlink, hardlink, swap, replacement and disappearance tests now run against both chmod strategies, so the regular-descriptor path stays covered on Linux CI.

## Why
- Closing **any** descriptor for a file releases every POSIX advisory lock the process holds on that file, including SQLite's locks through connections that are already open (SQLite: [POSIX advisory locks canceled by a separate thread doing close()](https://sqlite.org/howtocorrupt.html#_posix_advisory_locks_canceled_by_a_separate_thread_doing_close_)).
- `MessageStore` runs the helpers on every construction, before and after connecting, so each per-agent engine clone unlocked every existing LCM connection in the process. Another process closing its last connection (for example a short-lived CLI run against the same home) could then take SQLite's last-connection path, checkpoint, and **unlink the live `-wal`/`-shm`** while the long-lived process still used them. Fresh connections in that process then paired the orphaned WAL index with a new WAL and failed with `disk I/O error` or `file is not a database`. Hermes reports this as `Context engine 'lcm' could not be safely copied ... falling back to built-in compressor`. Two process groups checkpointing through different WAL/SHM pairs is also a path to real corruption.
- Full analysis and field evidence: #588 and its follow-up comments. Three independent Linux deployments on `8d1b1e6` report the same pattern. One of them starts from a clean install: the first child-agent fallback came 28 minutes after first boot, and `integrity_check` reported `database disk image is malformed` at 1h58m. It also has a same-filesystem control where only the store that spawns child agents was damaged.

## Validation
- [x] Focused validation: `pytest tests/test_storage_permissions.py -q` -> `43 passed` on Python 3.11, 3.13 and 3.14 (was 22 before this change).
- [x] RED control: the 6 new lock-retention tests against the unmodified helper (only the new module flag added so the file collects) -> `6 failed`, each at the `-wal`/`-shm` still-exists assertion.
- [x] Mutation checks: removing only the early return fails the 3 `regular-descriptor` lock-retention cases. Replacing only the `O_PATH` chmod with a regular open/close fails the 3 loose-database tightening cases. So each half has its own test.
- [ ] Default validation:
  - [x] `pytest tests/test_lcm_core.py tests/test_lcm_engine.py tests/test_packaging_install.py -q` (included in the full run below)
  - [x] `pytest -q` (CI-equivalent: Python 3.11, `ulimit -n 1024`, `umask 022`) -> `3050 passed, 1 skipped, 12 xfailed` (unmodified `main` in the same environment: `3029 passed, 1 skipped, 12 xfailed`; the +21 are the 9 new tests plus 12 existing tests now parametrized over both chmod strategies)
  - [ ] `scripts/validate_release.sh --full --keep-going --output /tmp/hermes-lcm-release-validation-sqlite-locks`
  - [x] `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD && git diff --check && git diff --cached --check`
- [x] `ruff check .` (ruff 0.15.13) -> all checks passed. `python scripts/validate_dependency_contract.py` -> valid. `python -m compileall -q .` -> ok.
- [ ] Workflow validation, if workflows changed: `actionlint` (no workflow changes)

## Notes
- **Upgrade notes.** This stops new lock loss. It does **not** repair a store that is already split or corrupt. Restart every process sharing the `HERMES_HOME` (gateway, dashboard, CLI) onto this code: any process still running the old helpers keeps releasing its own locks. A long-lived process may also already hold deleted `-wal`/`-shm` handles (`ls -l /proc/<pid>/fd | grep 'lcm.db.*(deleted)'`). WAL frames it has not checkpointed are reachable only through that process, so check `PRAGMA integrity_check` and decide what to salvage before restarting it.
- **Scope.** This only changes how the permission helpers touch files. It does not address #463 (clone descriptor multiplication), and it does not change the connection pragmas.
- **Pre-existing loose files.** With `O_PATH` available, tightening no longer releases locks. Without it (for example macOS), a pre-existing loose artifact is still tightened through a regular descriptor, so the lock release can still happen **once**, on the first construction that tightens it. Every later construction takes the early return. SQLite's unix VFS creates `-wal`/`-shm` with the database file's permission bits, so once the database is `0600` new sidecars are created private too.
- **Create path.** `O_CREAT | O_EXCL` still uses a regular descriptor, because `O_PATH` cannot create. A file this call just created carries none of this process's SQLite locks, unless another thread connects to that exact path between creation and close.
- **`/proc/self/fd` chmod** is the same mechanism glibc uses to implement `fchmodat(..., AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW)` on Linux. The flag is decided once at import. The fixture monkeypatches it to cover both branches.
- **Test environment.** If your shell umask is `002`, the suite's parent-directory check refuses pytest's group-writable temp dirs (`test_benchmarking_cli.py` fails the same way on unmodified `main`), so run with `umask 022`, as CI does.
- `scripts/validate_release.sh --full` was **not** run. Its full-pytest and low-fd gates are covered by the full run above (made under `ulimit -n 1024`), but the release stress tier was not exercised, so that box is unchecked.

Refs #588

title: fix: avoid below-threshold replay compaction
body:
## Summary

- bind replay-cleanup preflight handoff to the exact session and canonical message batch
- revalidate cleanup, threshold pressure, deferred maintenance, overflow recovery, and explicit manual compaction in `compress()`
- skip summary work when replay cleanup is still required but the original active context remains below threshold
- clear the one-shot handoff before ingest so failures or unrelated requests cannot reuse stale state

## Why

A replay cleanup request could enter `compress()` below the configured context threshold and still compact an eligible historical leaf. That produced summary nodes even though the active context did not require compaction. A plain boolean preflight flag also was not tied to the exact request that created it.

The handoff now contains the session ID plus a SHA-256 of canonical JSON for the complete message batch. `compress()` captures and clears it immediately, ingests again, and only takes the cleanup-only return when the same request still needs cleanup and no higher-priority compaction condition applies.

## Priority behavior retained

Cleanup-only does **not** override:

- precise threshold pressure (`current_tokens >= threshold_tokens`)
- eligible-leaf overflow recovery
- deferred maintenance under critical pressure
- `force=True`
- an explicit `focus_topic`

When no precise token count is supplied, threshold pressure is estimated from the original incoming messages, not the sanitized working copy. This preserves compaction for oversized content that becomes small only after quarantine/externalization.

## Verification

Against upstream `main` at `8d1b1e6`:

- focused replay/quarantine suite: `36 passed`
- Ruff: passed
- `git diff --check`: passed
- full suite: `3037 passed, 1 skipped, 12 xfailed, 2 failed`

The two failures are existing LosslessClaw data-URI assertions:

- `test_import_lossless_claw_externalizes_legacy_data_uri_content`
- `test_import_lossless_claw_respects_externalization_path_env`

Both failures were reproduced independently on a clean worktree at unmodified upstream `main` (`8d1b1e6`).

title: fix(storage): `messages` has no content-identity constraint, so replayed/compacted messages are re-INSERTed as duplicates (root cause of #513, #568)
body:
## Summary

`messages` has no content-identity constraint, so **every replayed/compacted message is re-INSERTed as a new row**. This is the storage-boundary root cause behind both #513 (post-compression replay) and #568 (state.db recovery replay): the engine's positional cursor and replay-identity checks can only catch the *prefix* of a re-sent batch, so any replay that lands out-of-order, mid-batch, or via a recovery path bypasses every existing guard and lands as a duplicate.

I measured a production instance at **~65% duplicate rows**, with a worst cluster of **81 identical copies of one message**.

## Description

### Bug

The LCM `messages` table is keyed only by `store_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT`. There is **no unique constraint on message identity**, so the store cannot tell a replayed row from a genuinely new one at insert time.

- **DDL** — `store.py:364` (`_init_db`):
  ```sql
  CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS messages (
      store_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
      session_id TEXT NOT NULL,
      ...
      role TEXT NOT NULL,
      content TEXT,
      tool_call_id TEXT,
      ...
      observed_at REAL,
      observed_at_source TEXT
  );
  CREATE INDEX idx_msg_session   ON messages(session_id, store_id);   -- non-unique
  CREATE INDEX idx_msg_session_ts ON messages(session_id, timestamp); -- non-unique
  ```

- **Insert path** — `store.py:459 append()` and `store.py:521 _append_protected_batch()` both perform a **bare `INSERT INTO messages (...) VALUES (...)`** with no identity check and no `ON CONFLICT`. `append()` returns `cur.lastrowid`; a re-send therefore always mints a new `store_id`.

- **The one real identity function is not on this path.** `reconcile.py:127 _message_replay_identity()` (role + normalized content + `tool_call_id`/persisted-output identity) is used only by the **cursor-reconcile** code (`reconcile.py:805 _reconcile_ingest_cursor_from_store`, docstring *"Infer the in-memory cursor … after process restart"*) to advance the *positional* cursor. It is never consulted at the storage boundary.

- **The cursor is positional, so it cannot represent mixed ordering.** The per-turn path `engine.py:1598 ingest()` → `_ingest_messages()` slices by list position: `cursor = min(max(self._ingest_cursor,0), n)` (`engine.py:4517`) and `new_messages = replay_messages[cursor:]` (`engine.py:4599`). A compression or rebind boundary resets it — `self._ingest_cursor = 0` + `_schedule_ingest_cursor_reconciliation()` (`engine.py:2800-2810`; also `2867-2876`, and `6212-6213` in assembly-guardrail recovery) — after which the *next* host batch is re-sliced from scratch. The active-replay cache only de-dupes a **clean prefix** (`engine.py:4574-4593`: it matches `messages[:cursor]` against the last batch). Any replay that is not an in-order prefix — the #513 `NEW,NEW,REPLAY,NEW,…` ordering, or a full #568 recovery replay after `state.db` was restored — passes straight into `append_batch`.

### Impact

Duplicated rows are not inert:

- **FTS is biased.** `messages_fts` is a *content* FTS table mirrored per row (`store.py:303-319`), so an N-fold duplicate contributes N identical hits to every FTS match — search results over-sampled toward whatever was replayed most.
- **Vector / semantic search has no dedupe at all.** `lcm_chunk_meta` / `lcm_embedding` rows are keyed by `store_id`, so duplicated source messages spawn duplicated chunk embeddings; a k-NN recall returns the same content N times and the ranking is dominated by the most-replayed messages.
- **Storage bloat.** Duplicates accumulate without bound (see measurements).
- **Cleanup is heuristic.** #568 already had to dedupe recovery replays by the fragile rule "row timestamp is after the original session end."

### Measurements (one production instance, read-only, as of 2026-09-16)

| metric | value |
|---|---|
| total `messages` rows | 31,317 |
| rows with non-NULL `observed_at` | 31,153 |
| distinct message identities* | 10,809 |
| duplicate clusters (size ≥ 2) | 8,225 |
| redundant rows (Σ(cluster−1)) | **20,344** |
| redundancy as % of all rows | **65.0 %** |
| largest single-message cluster | **81 identical copies** (one assistant message, session `20260904_205849_aa33cf`) |
| `lcm_chunk_meta` rows | 8,897 |

\*identity = `(session_id, role, observed_at, COALESCE(tool_call_id,''), COALESCE(content,''))`. Rows with NULL `observed_at` (92 of 31,153 ≈ 0.3 %) are intentionally left distinct — SQLite treats NULLs as distinct in a unique index and LCM never invents an observation time, so they cannot be reliably de-duplicated.

The 09-15 snapshot of the same instance was 29,963 rows / 19,646 redundant; the count is still growing, which is consistent with "replayed every turn after each compaction boundary."

## Reproduction (engine-level, no live DB needed)

The exact #513 trigger, driven through the **real** `compress()` path (no simulated compaction, no manual row deletion):
