title: feat(compaction): make the automatic foreground compaction budget configurable
body:
## Summary
- Add `LCM_AUTOMATIC_FOREGROUND_MAX_PASSES` (default `12`) and `LCM_AUTOMATIC_FOREGROUND_MAX_SECONDS` (default `120`) so operators can cap how long automatic, non-forced compaction is allowed to hold a live turn.
- When either ceiling is lowered below the manual sweep ceiling, the existing sweep deadline is applied to the automatic path as well: leaf passes, pre-compaction extraction timeout, leaf summarization, and condensation.
- Surface both ceilings in `lcm_status`. The existing `threshold_full_sweep_max_passes` / `threshold_full_sweep_max_seconds` keys are unchanged.
- Forced/manual compaction always keeps the full `12` pass / `120` second ceiling regardless of the automatic setting.

## Why
Automatic compaction runs inside a live turn. With a large raw backlog and `LCM_THRESHOLD_FULL_SWEEP_ENABLED=true`, a threshold-triggered automatic run can legitimately consume the full 12-pass / 120-second sweep ceiling before the turn can continue, which is felt directly as agent latency.

There was no way to bound that from configuration: the pass and wall-clock ceilings were module constants, and the wall-clock deadline was only enforced when `threshold_full_sweep_active` was true. This change makes the automatic path bounded by policy while leaving the deliberate, operator-initiated path untouched.

## Behaviour at defaults
Defaults were chosen to equal the existing manual ceiling, and the new code paths are gated on an operator having actually lowered a ceiling (`automatic_budget_enforced`). At default configuration the automatic path is byte-identical to `main`, including the `deadline` kwarg not being passed to `_summarize_leaf_chunk_with_rescue`.

## Validation
- [x] Focused validation: `pytest tests/test_lcm_engine.py -k "automatic_foreground or forced_compaction_ignores or threshold_full_sweep or dynamic_leaf_chunk" -q` -> `13 passed, 748 deselected`
- [x] Default validation:
  - [x] `pytest tests/test_lcm_core.py tests/test_lcm_engine.py tests/test_packaging_install.py -q`
  - [x] `pytest -q` -> `6 failed, 3026 passed, 1 skipped, 12 xfailed`
  - [x] `bash -lc 'ulimit -n 1024 && pytest -q'`
  - [x] `python -m compileall -q .`
  - [x] `python -m py_compile scripts/import_lossless_claw.py`
  - [x] `bash -n scripts/install.sh scripts/update.sh`
  - [x] `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD && git diff --check && git diff --cached --check`
  - [x] `ruff check .` -> `All checks passed!`
- [ ] Workflow validation: not applicable, no workflows changed.

The 6 failures are pre-existing on `main` at `8d1b1e6` in this environment and are byte-identical before and after this branch (`tests/test_ingest_protection.py` x2, `tests/test_packaging_install.py` x4). Baseline on unmodified `main`: `6 failed, 3023 passed`. This branch: `6 failed, 3026 passed`. The delta is exactly the 3 tests added here.

## Notes
- Three new tests: defaults match the manual ceiling; a lowered pass ceiling bounds automatic compaction and reports `pass_budget_exhausted`; forced compaction ignores the lowered automatic ceiling.
- `lcm_status` gains two keys and removes none, so existing status consumers are unaffected.
- Docs updated in `README.md` and `docs/operator-guide.md` configuration tables.
- Tradeoff: an operator who lowers the ceiling will see `budget_exhausted` telemetry more often on the automatic path. That is the intended signal, not a failure, and the manual path remains available to finish the work.

Refs #

title: Offer: opt-in async background compaction (moves summary provider work off the turn-critical path)
body:
### Problem

Summary-provider work runs on the turn-critical path. When a session accumulates a large raw backlog, the compaction that clears it happens inside a live turn, so the provider round-trips are felt directly as agent latency. Raising the thresholds trades latency for prompt size; lowering them makes compaction more frequent. Neither removes the provider call from the turn.

### User or operator impact

On long-running sessions this is the dominant source of perceived stalls. It is worst exactly when the agent is most loaded, because backlog size and turn importance correlate.

### Proposed direction

We run a private production fork that addresses this with an opt-in async background compaction subsystem, and we are offering it rather than proposing it. It moves preparation off the turn, while foreground code remains the sole publisher of canonical summary nodes and advances the conversation frontier with a SQLite compare-and-swap.

The design contract and its five non-negotiable invariants are in `docs/async-background-compaction.md` on the reference branch. In short:

1. Raw rows in `messages` stay authoritative and are never deleted by the feature.
2. With the feature disabled, no background store, worker, or optional table is created.
3. Background preparation provider calls run outside SQLite transactions and outside the foreground turn. A bounded emergency path is the one explicit foreground exception.
4. Prepared nodes are inactive: DAG, search, expand, recall, GC, and active-context readers cannot see them.
5. Canonical nodes, lifecycle-frontier movement, and job publication commit as one durable transaction, and active-context assembly happens only after that transaction commits.

Nine environment-configurable settings, `LCM_BACKGROUND_COMPACTION_ENABLED` defaulting to `false`. 28 test files cover concurrency stress, queue races, partial repair races, reset fences, emergency and partial-emergency paths, publication fencing, source coverage, and security.

Reference branch, published purely so you can read it:
https://github.com/thebionaut/hermes-lcm/tree/reference/async-background-compaction

### Alternatives and tradeoffs

Being straight about the cost: this is a large subsystem, `background_compaction.py` is over 10k lines, and it brings its own `lcm_compaction_*` schema. It is a real maintenance commitment even though it is default-off.

The honest alternatives are (a) take nothing, (b) take the design and reimplement it in a shape you prefer, (c) take it in staged pieces, or (d) take it as-is. We have no stake in which. If the answer is (a), that is a completely fine answer and we will keep carrying it privately.

### Backward compatibility

Default-off by master flag. With `LCM_BACKGROUND_COMPACTION_ENABLED=false` the behaviour, schema, and process footprint are unchanged. The optional tables are only created when the feature is enabled.

### Validation or evidence

The subsystem has run in daily production use on our fork. 28 dedicated test files, plus a written design contract predating the implementation.

Important caveat, stated up front: **the reference branch will not merge and is not a pull request.** It is a single squashed snapshot based on the `v0.21.0-rc2` fork point, not current `main`, and everything else on it is stacked on this subsystem and its schema, including a read-only compaction invariant audit, durable historical projection recovery, detached model-switch summary preparation, and a lossless active replay preview. We tested each of our commits individually against current `main`: 44 of 51 do not apply, and of the 7 that do, 6 are semantically broken because they depend on modules `main` does not have. That is why this is an offer to read rather than a patch to apply.

The one piece that genuinely was upstream-shaped was rebuilt from scratch against current `main` and is #621.

### Implementation status

Implemented and in production use on a private fork.

### Additional notes

No obligation implied and no response needed if you are not interested. The branch is MIT like upstream, and you are welcome to take any part of it, in whole or in part, with or without us.

title: Explicit /new forgets that conversation's summary graph
body:
## Summary
- An explicit `/new` rotated the Hermes transcript but left this conversation's summary graph in place. `last_finalized_session_id` still pointed at the predecessor, so the next compression could carry those nodes into the new segment.
- `on_session_reset` for `new_session` / `session_reset` now deletes summary nodes for that conversation's current and last-finalized sessions, at every depth, and clears the carry pointer (`last_finalized_session_id`, frontiers, and debt).
- Raw messages stay, so explicit recall still works. Other conversations are not touched. Ordinary compression retain-depth is unchanged.

## Test
- `tests/test_explicit_new_forgets_carry.py`: predecessor nodes at depth 0 and 2 are deleted, a second conversation's node remains, and reassign of the old session moves nothing.

title: perf(engine): lazy storage binding — zero SQLite I/O in clone_for_agent/__deepcopy
body:
## Problem

Since deploying hermes-lcm as the Hermes context engine, every new AIAgent init deep-copies the registered plugin singleton (`agent/agent_init.py` uses `copy.deepcopy`). Our `LCMEngine.__deepcopy__` delegates to `clone_for_agent()`, which constructs a new engine whose constructor **eagerly calls `_bind_storage()`**, opening fresh `sqlite3` connections to the live WAL database.

Under concurrent write load (large message blobs, heavy ingest), some of those opens intermittently raise `sqlite3.OperationalError: disk I/O error`. Hermes then logs `Context engine 'lcm' could not be safely copied for this agent (disk I/O error) - falling back to built-in compressor` and the agent silently **loses the LCM context engine** for that session. We observed ~40 such fallbacks in 36h, including during a B-tree corruption event (the transient I/O errors clustered around it, but they are not caused by corruption - they reproduce on a healthy DB under load).

## Root cause

`__deepcopy__`/`clone_for_agent()` performed SQLite I/O at copy time. The copy path runs on every agent creation, so any transient I/O failure there degrades the engine silently.

## Change

- `clone_for_agent()` no longer touches the database: storage helpers (`MessageStore`, `SummaryDAG`, `LifecycleStateStore`, `AssertionStore`, `QueryViewStore`, `AdaptiveRetrievalRegistry`) are bound **lazily on first access** via a `_ensure_storage()` guard.
- Binding is idempotent and thread-safe (`threading.RLock`, bind exactly once under concurrent first-access).
- `_close_storage()` on an unbound clone is a safe no-op.
- `initialize_rollup_invalidation_outbox` still runs exactly once, at first bind.
- No public API changes, no new dependencies. Minimal diff.

## Verification

- 20x `copy.deepcopy(plugin_singleton)` against the live production database: **0** `sqlite3.connect` calls during the copy path.
- First real use of a clone triggers lazy binding exactly once (3 connections opened on first access, unchanged after repeated access).
- Plugin test suite: 3011 passed (the 22 failures in the run are pre-existing environment-dependent failures - verified byte-identical on the unpatched tree).
- New tests added in `tests/test_lcm_engine_lazy_storage.py` covering: zero-connect deepcopy, rollup-trigger exactly-once at first bind, shutdown-on-unbound-clone as a no-op, and a 20x deepcopy loop.

## Notes

After deploying this on our production Hermes instance, the fallback warnings went to zero.

title: fix: stop silently discarding database.journal_mode when the config is unreadable
body:
## Summary
- `_resolve_journal_mode_from_config()` now returns `""` — not `"wal"` — when the operator's config cannot be **read**, so an unreadable config is no longer indistinguishable from an operator who chose WAL.
- It logs a warning naming the exception and stating that the operator's journal-mode setting is not being applied (latched once per process, not per connection).
- `lcm_doctor`'s `sqlite_storage` check no longer reports `pass` on a WAL database; WAL now yields `warn` with the reason and the remedy.

## Why
`_configured_journal_mode()` read `database.journal_mode` inside a `try` whose handler was:

```python
except Exception:
    return "wal"
```

That discards the operator's setting for **any** failure and logs nothing. A failed read is therefore indistinguishable from an operator who asked for WAL, so a `delete` request can be silently ignored with no signal anywhere.

The failure is reachable, not theoretical. `hermes_cli` is importable only from the Hermes Agent install, so all of these land in that `except`:

- a cwd / `PYTHONPATH` change,
- a relocated or partially-installed host,
- a Python older than the host's syntax baseline — the host uses PEP-604 `int | None` annotations, so 3.9 raises `TypeError` at import.

Observed on a host where `config.yaml` said `journal_mode: delete` and the resolver returned `'wal'` with nothing logged.

This matters beyond tidiness because WAL is the documented hazard of a multi-process `lcm.db` — `configure_connection`'s own docstring says WAL "does NOT make sibling processes safe". Each holder (gateway, dashboard, TUI) keeps its **own** `-wal` inode, and unlinking a held sidecar produces the split-brain that tears the FTS shadow tables. That host saw four `lcm.db` corruptions in five days, with `integrity_check` returning `ok` throughout a live split-brain. An operator trying to escape to DELETE needs the setting to actually apply, and to know if it did not.

### Scope
No default change: a single-process install still gets WAL, and the never-live-downgrade rule is untouched — a live WAL database is still left in WAL. This change makes an already-supported escape hatch (`database.journal_mode` / `LCM_JOURNAL_MODE`) reliable and visible. It does not decide whether WAL should be the default for a multi-holder database; that is a larger call, and this PR deliberately leaves it to the maintainers.

## Validation
- [x] Focused validation: `python -m pytest tests/test_journal_mode_config.py -q` -> `18 passed`
- [x] Negative validation, proving the tests catch the defect: a variant keeping the new structure but the **old swallowing body** fails exactly the two bug-specific tests —
```
FAILED tests/test_journal_mode_config.py::test_unreadable_config_returns_empty_not_wal
FAILED tests/test_journal_mode_config.py::test_unreadable_config_logs_the_reason
2 failed, 2 passed, 14 deselected
```
and the same tests pass on this change (`4 passed`).
- [x] Default validation:
  - [x] `pytest tests/test_lcm_core.py -q` -> `311 passed`
  - [x] `bash -lc 'ulimit -n 1024 && pytest tests/test_journal_mode_config.py -q'` -> `18 passed`
  - [x] `python -m compileall -q .` -> OK
  - [x] `bash -n scripts/install.sh scripts/update.sh` -> OK
  - [x] `git diff --check` -> clean
- [x] `ruff check .` (0.15.13, matching CI) -> `All checks passed!`
- [ ] `pytest -q` full suite — not run here; see Notes.

## Notes
- I could not run the full `pytest -q` suite in this environment; `tests/test_lcm_core.py` (311 cases) plus the new file were run, and CI will cover the rest. Flagging rather than claiming it passed.
- The two behaviour changes are deliberately visible rather than silent: `lcm_doctor`'s `sqlite_storage` can now report `warn`. If a maintainer prefers `sqlite_storage` to keep reporting purely on integrity, the WAL signal could move to its own check instead — happy to restructure.
- The warning text is operator-facing and mentions `database.journal_mode` rather than a host-specific path.

Refs #361

title: Question: should desktop `hermes serve --isolated` sessions write to the shared default lcm.db? (second writer, deleted WAL fds, two corruption waves)
body:
## Context

Production Hermes deployment (Linux VPS, SQLite 3.53.1, Python 3.11.15, WAL mode). hermes-lcm plugin runs in the messaging gateway process (`hermes gateway run`), which owns the shared default DB `~/.hermes/lcm.db`. Named profiles (rab9, robot-man, …) each get their own DB under `~/.hermes/profiles/<name>/lcm.db`. Desktop client sessions spawn as `hermes serve --isolated …` (HERMES_DESKTOP=1, ppid=1) against the same workspace.

## What we saw (production evidence, Sep 22–24)

1. **Two corruption waves** of the shared default `lcm.db` (each ~12 h after a repair), while all profile DBs stayed healthy. `integrity_check` signature both times:

   ```
   Tree 2 page 2: btreeInitPage() returns error code 11
   Tree 2072 page N: ... + dozens of "2nd reference to page N"  (double page refs)
   ```

   Both waves repaired via controlled rebuild + swap; ingest froze mid-corruption (no writes for 25+ h in wave 2).

2. **`lsof` during the second wave:** the desktop `--isolated` process (spawned ~1 h before the wave) held rw fds on the *shared* `lcm.db` **and on deleted `lcm.db-wal`/`lcm.db-shm`** inodes, while the gateway process held the live ones. I.e. the WAL/SHM were unlinked and recreated while at least two processes still had the old inode open. This matches the mechanism reproduced in #588 (permission helpers) and the deleted-WAL-handles observation in #601.

3. We now run a small inotify watcher on `lcm.db*` lifecycle events (CREATE/DELETE/MOVE) with per-event fd-holder snapshots, to catch the unlinker in the act instead of inferring after the fact.

## Question

Is it intended for a desktop `hermes serve --isolated` session to open the **shared** default profile `lcm.db` at all?

Given #588 (permission helpers recreate sidecars → deleted handles under live connections) and #601 (unfenced schema/maintenance work on live DBs), every additional process initializing LCM against the same file looks like a corruption window, even when each writer alone is correct.

Should desktop isolated sessions get their own LCM storage (e.g. a per-session/per-profile `lcm.db` like named profiles have), or is there already a supported way to point a desktop session at different LCM storage (CLI flag / env / config)?

## Environment

- hermes-lcm: local production at `78ff02b` (branch `fix/lazy-storage-bind`, PR #626; the lazy-storage + quick_check guard is active locally)
- SQLite 3.53.1, Python 3.11.15, Linux (WAL mode)
- Corrupted DB: shared default `~/.hermes/lcm.db`; profile DBs (robot-man, job-hunter, rab9) never corrupted

Happy to share the watcher script or fd-snapshot logs if useful for #588's reproduction matrix.

title: perf(reconcile): make the ingest-cursor scan linear instead of O(n^2) per cursor
body:
## Summary
- `ReconcileMixin._find_reconciled_cursor_for_store_tail` now computes each per-message predicate and replay identity **once**, and answers every candidate cursor from prefix counts and slices. Before, it rebuilt every filtered list and recomputed every identity for `messages[:cursor]` at **each** cursor, which is O(n^2).
- `_matches_store_tail_suffix` compares from the newest row, so a miss costs O(1). The result is the same as the slice compare.
- `_ingest_messages` wraps the reconcile and the cached-prefix check in `_replay_identity_memo_scope()`. A row is identified once per ingest pass. The memo is keyed by object identity and closes before new rows are persisted.

Semantics are unchanged. Every derived value is the same expression the old loop evaluated, memoised by index.

## Why
After a compaction, the replayed active context is `[scaffold] + [summary] + [already-stored fresh tail]`. It never matches at the top cursor, so the scan walks all the way down to 0, paying O(cursor) identity work at every step. JSON canonicalisation and externalized-payload reads make each identity expensive. On a long session this was seconds to minutes of dead time before each turn reached the model (we profiled it in production, stuck in this listcomp, at 250-650k-token contexts).

Identity computations, measured on a synthetic 5k-row session:

| replay shape | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| scaffold + 200 rows | 63,126 | 1,821 |
| scaffold + 400 rows | 246,226 | 3,621 |
| scaffold + 800 rows | 972,426 (~47 s) | 7,221 (~1 s) |
| full replay, 5,000 rows | 55,005 | 15,002 |

The scan was introduced in #111 (`79629c2`) and later moved into `ReconcileMixin`.

## Validation
- [x] Focused validation: `pytest tests/test_reconcile_scan_cost.py -q` -> **7 passed** on this branch; **6 of 7 fail** on `upstream/main` (`8d1b1e6`). The one that passes on both pins the ingest outcome: no duplicates, and the new turn stored once. The test counts identity computations **and** per-message predicate evaluations, because a memo alone would hide a rescan.
- [x] Differential check (not committed): old vs new function on 4,000 randomized replay shapes (full, full+new, suffix, scaffold, scaffold+new, preserved-objective, stale head, delta, random; with and without ignore patterns; repeating vocabulary) gave **0 mismatches**. Two planted mutations were caught.
- [x] Default validation:
  - [x] `pytest tests/test_lcm_core.py tests/test_lcm_engine.py tests/test_packaging_install.py -q` under `ulimit -n 1024` -> 1115 passed, 1 failed. The failure is `test_on_session_end_returns_quickly_under_real_sqlite_writer_lock`, a wall-clock assertion that fails the same way on `upstream/main`.
  - [x] `pytest -q` (full suite) -> **3021 passed, 14 failed, 2 skipped, 12 xfailed**. `upstream/main` gives 3014 passed with the **identical 14 failures**, and the +7 passes are the new tests. On this macOS box those 14 are environmental: wall-clock deadline asserts in `test_embedding_provider.py`, `test_embedding_search_modes.py`, `test_compaction_telemetry.py` and `test_lcm_engine.py`, plus the `/var` -> `/private/var` symlink in `test_path_containment.py` and `test_path_security.py`.
  - [x] `python -m compileall -q .` -> ok
  - [x] `git diff --check` -> ok
  - [x] `ruff check .` (0.15.13) -> clean
- [ ] Workflow validation: not applicable, no workflow changes.

## Notes
- All fixtures are synthetic. No transcripts or real databases were used.
- `store.get_session_tail` showed up in the same profiles. It is served by the `(session_id, store_id)` index with a LIMIT, so it is bounded per call and left unchanged.
- I did not add a "skip preflight when far below threshold" shortcut. The reconcile has to run on the first ingest after a bind anyway, and once the scan is linear that shortcut isn't needed.
- Test environment note, possibly useful to others: a few tests clear `HERMES_HOME`-style overrides, and the store then falls back to `Path.home()/.hermes/lcm.db`. On a dev machine with a real store, that means the suite can open the **real** database. We run the suite with `HOME` pointed at a temp dir. Happy to send a separate small PR adding a conftest guard if you'd like one.

title: fix(storage): WAL contour guard — sentinel connection + sidecar identity tracking
body:
# fix(storage): WAL contour guard — sentinel connection + sidecar identity tracking

Closes the plugin-side part of #628. Python cannot disable SQLite's last-close unlink
(`SQLITE_FCNTL_PERSIST_WAL` is not exposed by python's `sqlite3`; `PRAGMA persistent_wal` does
not exist in SQLite 3.53.x — both verified empirically), so this PR makes the plugin **hold the
contour open** and **detect contour takeover loudly** instead of staying silent through a
split-brain.

## Problem (empirically reproduced, see #628)

In multi-process deployments sharing the default `lcm.db`, SQLite's last-close unlinks the shared
`-wal`/`-shm`. A long-lived process parked on deleted sidecar inodes while another process
recreates fresh sidecars at the same paths ends in a split-brain and page-level corruption
(`2nd reference to page N`) — reproduced end-to-end with auditd + an fd-watcher (~50 ms cadence).

## What this does

1. **Sentinel connection** (`store.py`): `MessageStore` holds one extra connection for its
   lifetime; ordinary `close()` no longer creates last-close windows inside a running process.
   Explicit `shutdown()` closes it (reset paths use it before unlinking). Memory DBs skip it.
2. **Contour identity tracking** (`store.py`): at first materialization the store snapshots
   `(st_dev, st_ino)` of `-wal`/`-shm`; checks compare against the snapshot:
   - identity mismatch (alien recreate at the same path) → confirmed split-brain, refuse + raise;
   - a single "missing" observation is only a warning (multi-process fresh init legitimately
     produces transient vanishes — strace-verified); confirmed via 1 s re-probe;
   - write paths re-stat at most once per second (rate-limited inline check).
3. **Engine fuse** (`engine.py`): confirmed failures fire contour-failure listeners; the engine
   sets its unavailable-reason, unbinds, and tears down ALL helpers (DAG/lifecycle/assertions/
   query-views + sentinel) on the next access — nothing keeps writing into an orphaned contour.
   A 30 s daemon guard timer (weakref-based) covers quiet processes.
4. **Docs** (`README.md`): "Multi-process deployments" section — risks, `?immutable=1` for live
   diagnostics, restart-all-holders rule after any repair/swap.

## Trade-offs (stated openly)

- A standalone `MessageStore` (no engine timer) that goes fully quiet may not notice a
  persistently missing sidecar until its next identity event or shutdown — wall-clock rate
  limiting and the warning-only missing path are deliberate to keep multi-process fresh init
  working (strace shows SQLite itself unlinks sidecars under live peer fds during init races).
- On confirmed failure the process goes offline (restart required); there is no auto-repair.

## Validation

- New invariant tests in `tests/test_crash_safe_wal.py`: sentinel holds contour inodes across
  `close()`; alien recreate raises; transient missing tolerated on write path; reset closes the
  sentinel; engine-wide fuse tears down DAG too; rate-limited re-stat catches alien WAL.
- Existing multi-process spawn test (`test_db_bootstrap_fts.py`) passes — an earlier strict
  variant of the detector flaked it ~1/8 runs (strace-verified transient vanishes), which is why
  the missing-then-reprobe design exists.
- Full suite: no regressions vs parent commit (delta empty; 3024 passed).

Validation context: this branch was built on a live deployment that then suffered exactly the
#628 corruption again from an unrelated process (main db overwritten at the filesystem level);
the rebuilt database now serves production traffic through this branch's guards.

title: reconcile: post-compaction re-bind re-appends the replayed fresh tail when the store holds a row the replay lacks
body:
## Summary

When a session is re-bound after a compaction (host restart, session switch), the replayed post-compaction context `[scaffold + summaries] + [fresh tail]` re-appends the fresh tail. This happens whenever the store holds even one row that the replay does not carry. In the repro below one re-bind re-appends the 7-row fresh tail (122 -> 129 rows). A store that already holds one duplicate copy plus a store-only row grows again on the next re-bind (129 -> 136), so the duplication compounds.

## Where

`reconcile.py` @ `8d1b1e6` (v1.0.0-rc.1): `_reconcile_ingest_cursor_from_store` (L804) proves a replay only through `_find_reconciled_cursor_for_store_tail` (L421, called at L857). That requires the stored tail to be an exact contiguous suffix of the incoming replay. A store-only row breaks the proof. Examples are an orphan-recovery tool row written at shutdown, a background-review row, or an earlier missed replay. The scaffold-headed fresh tail then falls through to the ambiguous-delta path and is persisted again. Each miss also makes the next proof harder, so it compounds.

## Reproduction (clean `main` @ 8d1b1e6)

This uses the real `compress()` path with the offline summarizer. It appends one store-only tool row and then binds a fresh `LCMEngine` to the same session (so `_ingest_cursor_needs_reconcile` is true). All content is synthetic.

```
4 failed, 1 passed
test_replaying_real_compacted_context_twice_appends_nothing   assert 129 == 122
test_replay_over_already_duplicated_store_appends_nothing     assert 136 == 129
test_new_turn_repeating_stored_tail_is_still_appended         assert 131 == 122 + 2
test_new_turn_after_clean_replay_is_appended                  assert 130 == 122 + 1
test_delta_without_scaffold_is_never_deduplicated             passes (dup-over-loss control)
```

The two open PRs in this area do **not** change the result: the same file is 4 failed / 1 passed on #550 (`60901d2`) and on #613 (`e02df2a`). #550's contiguous-run rule needs a 4+ row user+assistant run. The replayed fresh tail after the scaffold is not proven by that rule here. This is a distinct shape from #513 (mid-turn compress) and #568 (state.db recovery replay). The symptom family is the one #599 describes at the storage layer.

<details><summary>tests/test_rebind_replay_window_dedup.py</summary>

```python
"""Re-binding an existing session must not re-append the post-compaction replay.

A host re-bind (restart, session switch) replays the post-compaction active
context ``[scaffold + summaries] + [fresh tail]``. When the store also holds a
row the replay does not carry (e.g. an orphan-recovery tool row), the stored
tail is no longer an exact suffix of the replay, reconcile cannot prove the
replay, and the fresh tail is re-appended on every re-bind.

These tests drive the real ``compress`` (offline summarizer) to build the
post-compaction context, then bind a fresh engine to the same session and
replay it. All content is synthetic.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import sqlite3

from hermes_lcm.config import LCMConfig
from hermes_lcm.engine import LCMEngine

SESSION = "rebind-sess"
ORPHAN = (
    "[Orphan recovery: interrupted side-effecting tool may have executed; "
    "its result was not observed.]"
)


def _cfg(tmp_path):
    return LCMConfig(
        database_path=str(tmp_path / "lcm.db"),
        leaf_chunk_tokens=120,
        condensation_fanin=2,
        fresh_tail_count=6,
        context_threshold=0.05,
        incremental_max_depth=3,
    )


def _engine(tmp_path):
    eng = LCMEngine(config=_cfg(tmp_path), hermes_home=str(tmp_path))
    eng.on_session_start(SESSION)
    return eng


def _transcript(n_pairs=30):
    msgs = [{"role": "system", "content": "You are a helpful assistant."}]
    for i in range(n_pairs):
        msgs.append({"role": "user", "content": f"do task {i} " + ("w" * 30)})
        msgs.append({
            "role": "assistant",
            "content": "",
            "tool_calls": [{"id": f"c{i}", "type": "function",
                            "function": {"name": "run", "arguments": f'{{"i": {i}}}'}}],
        })
        msgs.append({"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": f"c{i}", "content": f"result {i} " + ("z" * 60)})
        msgs.append({"role": "assistant", "content": f"done {i}"})
    return msgs


def _rows(tmp_path):
    return sqlite3.connect(str(tmp_path / "lcm.db")).execute(
        "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM messages WHERE session_id=?", (SESSION,)
    ).fetchone()[0]


def _count(tmp_path, content):
    return sqlite3.connect(str(tmp_path / "lcm.db")).execute(
        "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM messages WHERE session_id=? AND content=?", (SESSION, content)
    ).fetchone()[0]


def _compacted(tmp_path):
    """Run a real compaction and return (engine, post-compaction context)."""
    eng = _engine(tmp_path)
    compressed = eng.compress(list(_transcript()), current_tokens=10**9)
    assert eng._last_compression_status == "compacted", eng._last_compression_status
    assert any(eng._is_replayed_context_scaffold_message(m) for m in compressed)
    return eng, compressed


def _store_only_row(eng):
    # A row the store holds but the host transcript never carries, e.g. the
    # orphan-recovery tool row written at shutdown.
    eng._store.append_batch(SESSION, [{"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": "c29", "content": ORPHAN}])


def _rebind_ingest(tmp_path, messages):
    fresh = _engine(tmp_path)  # restarted process: cursor unknown -> reconcile
    assert fresh._ingest_cursor_needs_reconcile
    fresh._ingest_messages([dict(m) for m in messages])
    return fresh


class TestRebindReplayWindowDedup:
    def test_replaying_real_compacted_context_twice_appends_nothing(self, tmp_path):
        eng, compressed = _compacted(tmp_path)
        _store_only_row(eng)
        n0 = _rows(tmp_path)
        _rebind_ingest(tmp_path, compressed)
        assert _rows(tmp_path) == n0
        _rebind_ingest(tmp_path, compressed)
        assert _rows(tmp_path) == n0

    def test_replay_over_already_duplicated_store_appends_nothing(self, tmp_path):
        # Backlog shape: the fresh tail was already re-appended once by an
        # earlier missed replay, then a store-only row landed after it.
        eng, compressed = _compacted(tmp_path)
        tail = [m for m in compressed if not eng._is_replayed_context_scaffold_message(m)
                and m.get("role") != "system"]
        eng._store.append_batch(SESSION, [dict(m) for m in tail])
        _store_only_row(eng)
        n0 = _rows(tmp_path)
        _rebind_ingest(tmp_path, compressed)
        assert _rows(tmp_path) == n0

    def test_new_turn_repeating_stored_tail_is_still_appended(self, tmp_path):
        # No-loss control: a genuinely new turn whose content repeats the
        # last stored turn exactly must be appended, not skipped as replay.
        eng, compressed = _compacted(tmp_path)
        _store_only_row(eng)
        n0 = _rows(tmp_path)
        last_user = next(m for m in reversed(compressed) if m.get("role") == "user")
        last_asst = compressed[-1]
        assert last_asst.get("role") == "assistant"
        before_user = _count(tmp_path, last_user["content"])
        _rebind_ingest(tmp_path, compressed + [dict(last_user), dict(last_asst)])
        assert _rows(tmp_path) == n0 + 2
        assert _count(tmp_path, last_user["content"]) == before_user + 1

    def test_new_turn_after_clean_replay_is_appended(self, tmp_path):
        eng, compressed = _compacted(tmp_path)
        _store_only_row(eng)
        n0 = _rows(tmp_path)
        new = {"role": "user", "content": "GENUINELY_NEW_TURN"}
        _rebind_ingest(tmp_path, compressed + [new])
        assert _rows(tmp_path) == n0 + 1
        assert _count(tmp_path, "GENUINELY_NEW_TURN") == 1

    def test_delta_without_scaffold_is_never_deduplicated(self, tmp_path):
        # Dup-over-loss: an anchorless delta that repeats stored rows is kept.
        eng, compressed = _compacted(tmp_path)
        _store_only_row(eng)
        n0 = _rows(tmp_path)
        tail = [m for m in compressed if m.get("role") in ("user", "assistant", "tool")
                and not eng._is_replayed_context_scaffold_message(m)]
        _rebind_ingest(tmp_path, tail[-2:])
        assert _rows(tmp_path) > n0
```

</details>

## The policy question (why this is an issue, not a PR)

A fix exists and makes all 5 tests above pass. It is a fallback in `_reconcile_ingest_cursor_from_store`, used only when the replay is headed by a replayed-context scaffold. It anchors on the last stored occurrence of the first fresh-tail row and consumes the replayed window against the stored window as a multiset, so store-only rows are stepped over. Anything left after the window is appended as the real delta.

But it goes against six existing tests that deliberately assert the dup-over-loss contract for scaffolded replays:

- `test_lcm_engine.py::test_existing_compacted_session_restart_skips_synthetic_context_but_persists_new_tool` (L3818). The store is `[system, user, assistant]` and the replay is note + summary + those two rows + a new tool call. It asserts the two fresh-tail rows are re-appended (7 rows).
- `test_lcm_engine.py` L4303 `..._persists_scaffolded_delta_message_matching_store_tail`, and its `_with_followup` variant
- `test_lcm_engine.py` L4394 `..._cleanup_sensitive_scaffolded_repeated_tail`, and its `_with_followup` variant
- `test_lcm_core.py::test_preserved_objective_scaffold_does_not_skip_new_repeated_user_tail` (L4717)

These encode "a scaffolded row that matches the stored tail might be new, so persist it". That is a defensible policy. The cost is that every post-compaction re-bind duplicates the fresh tail, and the loss it guards against is a genuinely new turn that repeats the last stored turn byte-for-byte. The repro's `test_new_turn_repeating_stored_tail_is_still_appended` shows the dedup can still keep that case, because rows beyond the replayed window are appended.

Which contract do you want for scaffold-headed re-bind replays: keep dup-over-loss (and this is a won't-fix), or dedup the replayed window? If it is the latter, I'm happy to open the PR with those six tests updated and each change justified.

title: fix: declare minimal [project] metadata so Hermes uv workspace lock succeeds
body:
## Problem

Hermes' package manager treats every enabled plugin that ships a `pyproject.toml` as a **uv workspace member** (`pm/plugin_declarations.py::PythonDeclaration.is_member` → `pyproject is not None`). For a member without `[build-system]`, `pm/workspace.py::_workspace_member` marks it virtual and injects `[project].name = "hermes-plugin-<key>"`.

hermes-lcm's `pyproject.toml` is ruff-config only, with no `[project]` table. After Hermes injects the name, the member has `[project]` without `version`, and uv rejects it, which fails the **entire** `uv lock`:

```
`pyproject.toml` is using the `[project]` table, but the required `project.version` field is neither set nor present in the `project.dynamic` list
```

The result is that the plugin environment can't be resolved and hermes-lcm gets dropped or disabled.

## Fix

Add a minimal, metadata-only `[project]` table (`name`, placeholder `version = "0.0.0"`, `requires-python = ">=3.11"`, empty `dependencies`). There is still no `[build-system]`, so the member stays virtual: Hermes keeps renaming it per profile and never builds it. The version therefore doesn't need to track `plugin.yaml`. The header comment is updated to say why the table exists.

```
Resolved 2 packages in 22ms
```

The same change has been running on a production Windows 11 install. `lcm_doctor` reports `healthy`, and there are no lock or TOML errors in the logs.

## Note

This is independent of #595 (`_coerce_threshold_tokens_cap`), which touches `engine.py` only.

title: fix: re-bind replay must not re-append the stored fresh tail (#631)
body:
## Summary
- Re-bind replay (restart, session switch) no longer re-appends the already-stored fresh tail.
- Adds `_rebind_replay_stored_window_cursor` in `reconcile.py`. It is a fallback inside `_reconcile_ingest_cursor_from_store` and runs only when two things are true: the existing exact-suffix proof covered no durable row, and the replay is scaffold-headed. It anchors on the last stored occurrence of the first durable replay row, then consumes leading replay rows against the multiset of stored rows from that anchor on. Anything left over is appended as usual.
- **Policy change, stated explicitly:** a scaffold-headed re-bind replay of the stored fresh tail is now treated as a replay (skipped), not as new user turns (appended). Before this change the suite asserted **duplication over loss** for that shape on purpose. Six tests are flipped (listed below).

## Why
Closes #631.

A re-bind replays the post-compaction active context: scaffold, then summaries, then fresh tail. Reconcile only skipped the fresh tail when it was an exact contiguous suffix of the stored tail. Any store-only row breaks that proof, for example an orphan-recovery tool row or a duplicate left by an earlier replay. When the proof broke, the whole fresh tail was re-appended on every re-bind, and each duplicate made the next proof fail too, so the damage compounded. On one 12 GB production store, **84% of newly written rows were exact duplicates**. The downstream fork has run this fix as ANG-Ventures/hermes-agent#1048.

Trade-off: when a scaffold-headed replay's leading rows match stored rows since the anchor, they are read as the replay rather than as a genuinely repeated message. Rows past the matched window are still persisted. A delta with no scaffold is never deduplicated, which is covered by `test_delta_without_scaffold_is_never_deduplicated`.

### The six flipped tests (each asserted dup-over-loss on purpose)
1. `tests/test_lcm_core.py::TestAssemblyBudgetSelection::test_preserved_objective_scaffold_does_not_skip_new_repeated_user_tail` → `..._skips_replayed_user_tail_but_keeps_new_followup`. `"repeat me"` is the replayed stored tail, not a new turn. Only `"new followup"` is new, and it is still persisted.
2. `tests/test_lcm_engine.py::TestEngineABC::test_existing_compacted_session_restart_skips_synthetic_context_but_persists_new_tool` → `..._skips_synthetic_context_and_replayed_tail_but_persists_new_tool`. The compacted fresh tail (user/assistant) is already stored. Re-appending it was the #631 bug. The new tool turn is still appended.
3. `test_existing_session_restart_persists_scaffolded_delta_message_matching_store_tail` → `test_existing_session_restart_skips_scaffolded_replay_matching_store_tail`. A scaffold-headed replay whose delta equals the stored tail is the re-bind shape, so the store must be unchanged.
4. `test_existing_session_restart_persists_scaffolded_delta_message_matching_store_tail_with_followup` → `..._skips_scaffolded_replay_matching_store_tail_but_persists_followup`. Same as 3. The replayed `"retry"` is skipped and `"next answer"` is persisted.
5. `test_existing_session_restart_persists_cleanup_sensitive_scaffolded_repeated_tail` → `test_existing_session_restart_skips_cleanup_sensitive_scaffolded_replayed_tail`. The literal-JSON assistant row still matches its stored copy after cleanup, so the replay is recognised (`reason == "replayed stored window since anchor"`) and nothing is re-appended.
6. `test_existing_session_restart_persists_cleanup_sensitive_scaffolded_repeated_tail_with_followup` → `..._skips_cleanup_sensitive_scaffolded_replayed_tail_but_persists_followup`. Same as 5, and the genuine `"new follow-up"` is still persisted.

New regression tests (`tests/test_rebind_replay_window_dedup.py`):
- replaying a real compacted context twice appends nothing
- a replay over an already-duplicated store appends nothing
- a new turn that repeats the stored tail is still appended
- a new turn after a clean replay is appended
- a delta without a scaffold is never deduplicated

## Validation
- [x] Focused validation: `pytest -q tests/test_rebind_replay_window_dedup.py tests/test_lcm_core.py tests/test_lcm_engine.py -k "rebind or scaffold or restart or replay or preserved_objective"` → `119 passed, 955 deselected`
- [x] Default validation:
  - [x] `pytest -q` (local, macOS, Python 3.14, `ulimit -n 1024`, hermetic HOME/HERMES_HOME) → `13 failed, 3020 passed, 2 skipped, 12 xfailed`. All 13 are environmental and none touch reconcile or ingest. 11 are wall-clock deadline assertions (`test_embedding_provider.py`, `test_embedding_search_modes.py`, `test_compaction_telemetry_lock_contention_is_nonblocking`, `test_on_session_end_returns_quickly_under_real_sqlite_writer_lock`), and which ones fail varies from run to run. The other 2 are the macOS `/var` → `/private/var` path-prefix tests. I re-ran the same 13 on pristine `upstream/main` @ `8d1b1e6`: 9 failed that time, and the rest flaked the same way on both trees when isolated. They behave identically with and without this patch.
  - [x] `ruff check .` (0.15.13) → `All checks passed!`
  - [x] `git diff --check` → clean
  - [ ] `python -m compileall` / install script checks: not run. No scripts or packaging are touched.
- [ ] Workflow validation: N/A, no workflow changes.

## Notes
- I did not get a full green locally on macOS; the reds above are this repo's known environmental baseline on macOS. Linux CI on this PR is the authoritative run.
- All test data is synthetic.

Refs #631

title: fix(pyproject): declare runtime dependencies so the PM workspace venv resolves them
body:
## Summary

Extends #632 with the missing runtime dependencies.

#632 adds the minimal `[project]` table so `uv lock` accepts this plugin as a virtual workspace member — that part works and unblocks the eviction bug. But `dependencies = []` leaves the plugin resolving its import-time requirements from whatever happens to be installed in the host environment, which defeats the point of the managed venv: on a clean generation rebuild the plugin (and the session that loads it) fails on the first missing import.

An AST audit of the plugin's runtime modules shows these are the packages actually imported at load time:

```toml
dependencies = [
    "numpy>=1.26",
    "tiktoken>=0.7",
    "pyyaml>=6.0",
    "fastembed>=0.3",
    "huggingface-hub>=0.24",
    "regex>=2024.4",
]
```

With these declared, the Hermes package manager unions them into the managed venv on every generation rebuild, so plugin startup no longer depends on host state.

## Validation

- `uv lock` of the PM workspace succeeds with this member
- generation rebuild installs all six packages; every import resolves in the fresh venv
- plugin loads cleanly and full `hermes update` cycles pass with the plugin enabled (no eviction, no lock failure)
- lower bounds are the versions actually exercised, kept deliberately loose

---

title: feat: mark LCM-generated recovery rows with display_kind so hosts can identify them
body:
### Problem

`_assemble_context()` in `engine.py` adds recovery summaries to the assembled context as ordinary `role`/`content` messages. Nothing on those rows says LCM generated them. A host that also uses the returned messages to show or store a transcript has no reliable way to separate them from real user or assistant turns.

### User or operator impact

Any host that shows or stores the returned messages has to guess which rows came from LCM. We hit this in Hermes WebUI, where recovery summaries showed up in the chat transcript after compaction as if they were part of the conversation.

Guessing fails both ways:

1. Matching the summary heading also hides a genuine user or assistant message that starts with the same text.
2. Inferring from the current-turn boundary lets a summary through whenever that boundary can't be resolved.

Turn-boundary data tells a host which turn a row belongs to, not who wrote it. Only LCM knows which rows it generated.

### Proposed direction

Set `display_kind="hidden"` on the rows `_assemble_context()` generates, and leave copied fresh-tail messages untouched.

Hermes already uses this field for its own model-facing scaffolding, and the plumbing is in place on the host side: the Agent sets `display_kind` on synthetic rows, `messages` has a column for it, the session-preview query excludes `hidden` rows, and the WebUI sessions endpoint already reads it. LCM currently sets the field nowhere, so its generated rows are the ones that slip past.

Acceptance criteria:

- Rows generated by `_assemble_context()` carry `display_kind="hidden"`.
- Copied fresh-tail messages, including real prompts and answers, stay unmarked.
- The marked rows still reach the model. The field is already handled on the display and persistence paths, and Hermes strips internal display fields where provider payloads are built.
- A test covers a generated summary next to a genuine headed turn and checks that only the generated row is marked.

### Alternatives and tradeoffs

- **Host-side heading matching.** No LCM change, but it hides real messages that share a heading and breaks whenever LCM changes its wording.
- **Host-side turn-boundary inference.** Works in the common case, but fails open when the boundary is missing, and it answers ownership rather than origin.
- **A dedicated LCM origin field.** Clearer meaning and no overlap with display semantics, but every host has to learn a new key when `display_kind` already covers this case.
- **Not returning summaries in the message list.** Removes the ambiguity but drops the recovered context the model needs, so I don't think it's viable.

### Backward compatibility

The change is additive. Hosts that ignore the field behave exactly as they do now, and no host change is required to adopt it.

Rows already persisted before the change stay unmarked and render as they do today.

### Validation or evidence

- Checked against `main` at `8d1b1e6`: the rows emitted by `_assemble_context()` carry no origin or visibility metadata, and `display_kind` appears nowhere in the LCM codebase.
- Host side already handles the field: the Agent stamps `display_kind` on its own synthetic rows, `messages.display_kind` is a persisted column, the preview query filters on it, and the WebUI sessions endpoint projects it.
- Hermes docs on `display_kind` and not inferring origin from text: https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/developer-guide/programmatic-integration#rebuilding-the-in-flight-turn-on-reconnect

### Implementation status

Design sketched

### Additional notes

Related but separate: #512 covers synthetic summaries persisted as user rows and confused with real user input. This issue is about marking generated rows so hosts don't have to guess.

Happy to open a small PR with the change and tests.

title: fix: lcm_expand_query degrades on a malformed auxiliary response instead of raising TypeError
body:
## Summary
- `_synthesize_expansion_answer` read `response.choices[0].message.content` without a guard. This change guards that access and raises a typed `_ExpansionSynthesisError` when the response is malformed.
- The `lcm_expand_query` handler catches that error and returns the same degraded payload a synthesis timeout already returns: `degraded: true`, with the retrieved `node_ids` and matches kept.
- Regression test: `TestEngineTools::test_handle_expand_query_malformed_synthesis_response_is_degraded`.

## Why
Under load, the auxiliary call can return an error-shaped or partial object whose `.choices` is `None`, empty, or not subscriptable. The unguarded read then raised `TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable`. That failed the whole expand call, so the caller lost the node matches it had already retrieved, not only the synthesized prose. The handler already degrades on `TimeoutError` and on a blank answer. This PR handles the third failure shape the same way.

title: fix: run the ingested_at legacy backfill once (migration marker)
body:
Fix: gate the legacy `ingested_at` backfill behind a one-time migration marker, so it runs once instead of on every start (found during a fork audit of #902 against a live database).

## Change (d3c7af1)
`MessageStore._ensure_time_contract_columns` ran `UPDATE messages SET ingested_at = timestamp WHERE ingested_at IS NULL` every time the store opened. That is a full-table scan on every init, because no index can serve `IS NULL` on a column that is never NULL after the legacy rows are filled. The UPDATE is now gated behind a one-time `lcm_migration_state` marker (`messages_ingested_at_backfill_v1`), and `db_bootstrap.is_migration_step_complete()` is added next to `mark_migration_step_complete()`.

## Local verification (hermetic HOME/HERMES_HOME, py3.13)
